title.zh: 卷六十七 列傳第二十七 謝靈運
title.raw: 卷六十七 列傳第二十七 謝靈運 Volume 67 Biographies 27: Xie Lingyun

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十七 謝靈運

translations.literal: Biography 27: Xie Lingyun
translations.idiomatic: Biography 27: Xie Lingyun

sentences.zh: 謝靈運，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖玄，晉車騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan was General of Chariots and Cavalry of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan had been Jin's General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父瑍，生而不慧，為秘書郎，蚤亡。

translations.literal: His father Min was dull from birth, served as Secretary Gentleman, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Min had been slow-witted from childhood, held the post of Secretary Gentleman, and died young.

sentences.zh: 靈運幼便穎悟，玄甚異之，謂親知曰：「我乃生瑍，瑍那得生靈運！」

translations.literal: Lingyun as a child was already sharp and perceptive; Xuan greatly marveled at this and said to intimates, "I bore Min—how could Min have borne Lingyun!"
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun showed exceptional brilliance even as a boy. Xuan was astonished and told those close to him, "I fathered Min—how could Min have fathered Lingyun!"

sentences.zh: 靈運少好學，博覽群書，文章之美，江左莫逮。

translations.literal: Lingyun in youth loved learning, read widely among the classics, and in the beauty of his writing none south of the Yangzi could match him.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Lingyun was devoted to study and read widely; in literary excellence none in the lands south of the Yangzi could rival him.

sentences.zh: 從叔混特知愛之，襲封康樂公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Hun especially knew and loved him; he inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Kangle with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Hun on his father's side took a special liking to him. He inherited the title Duke of Kangle, with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以國公例，除員外散騎侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: By the precedent for dukes of a state, he was appointed Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Under the usual rule for hereditary dukes, he was appointed supernumerary attendant cavalier, but he declined the office.

sentences.zh: 為琅邪王大司馬行參軍。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Adjutant in the headquarters of the Prince of Langye, Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting adjutant on the staff of the Prince of Langye, who held the post of grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 性奢豪，車服鮮麗，衣裳器物，多改舊制，世共宗之，咸稱謝康樂也。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant and proud; his carriages and robes were fresh and splendid, and his garments and utensils mostly altered the old styles—the age together took him as model, and all called him "Xie of Kangle."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was lavish and proud. His carriages and dress were strikingly fine, and he often redesigned garments and furnishings in new styles. People took him as a fashion setter, and everyone called him "Xie of Kangle."

sentences.zh: 撫軍將軍劉毅鎮姑孰，以為記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the General Who Pacifies the Army Liu Yi garrisoned Gushu, Lingyun was made Recorder in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi, General Who Pacifies the Army, was stationed at Gushu, he appointed Lingyun recorder on his staff.

sentences.zh: 毅鎮江陵，又以為衛軍從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Yi garrisoned Jiangling, he again made him Attendant Gentleman of the Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi moved his garrison to Jiangling, he again appointed Lingyun attendant gentleman on the guard army staff.

sentences.zh: 毅伏誅，高祖版為太尉參軍，入為秘書丞，坐事免。

translations.literal: When Yi was executed, the High Ancestor by provisional appointment made him Adjutant to the Grand Commandant; he entered service as Secretary Director and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi was put to death, the High Ancestor provisionally appointed him adjutant to the grand commandant. He later entered the capital as director of the secretariat but was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 高祖伐長安，驃騎將軍道憐居守，版為諮議參軍，轉中書侍郎，又為世子中軍諮議，黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor campaigned against Chang'an, the General of Agile Cavalry Daolian remained to guard the capital; by provisional appointment Lingyun became Advisory Adjutant, then transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, and again served as advisory officer to the heir apparent's central army and as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: While the High Ancestor marched on Chang'an, Daolian the General of Agile Cavalry stayed behind to guard the capital. Lingyun was provisionally made advisory adjutant on his staff, then promoted to attendant gentleman of the palace secretariat, and later served as advisory officer to the heir apparent's central army and as attendant gentleman at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 奉使慰勞高祖於彭城，作《撰征賦》。

translations.literal: Sent on a mission to comfort and salute the High Ancestor at Pengcheng, he composed the "Rhapsody on Recording the Campaign."
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to offer congratulations to the High Ancestor at Pengcheng, he wrote the "Rhapsody on Recording the Campaign."

sentences.zh: 其序曰：

translations.literal: Its preface says:
translations.idiomatic: The preface reads:

sentences.zh: 蓋聞昏明殊位，貞晦異道，雖景度回革，亂多治寡，是故升平難於恆運，剝喪易以橫流。

translations.literal: I have heard that darkness and brightness occupy different positions, constancy and obscurity follow different paths; though the seasons turn and change, disorder is plentiful and order scarce—therefore lasting peace is hard under a constant cycle, and ruin and loss easily spread in a torrent.
translations.idiomatic: It is said that light and dark hold different stations, and steadfastness and decline follow different courses. Though the seasons revolve, ages of disorder outnumber ages of order; lasting peace is therefore rare in the long run, while ruin spreads easily like a flood.

sentences.zh: 皇晉□□河汾，來遷吳楚，數歷九世，年逾十紀，西秦無一援之望，東周有三辱之憤，可謂積禍纏釁，固以久矣。

translations.literal: The Jin royal house [text lost] the Fen and Yellow Rivers, then came and moved to Wu and Chu; it passed through nine generations and more than ten decades—Qin in the west had not a hope of aid, Zhou in the east bore the fury of three humiliations; one may say accumulated calamity and entwined strife have indeed been long.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin royal house [lacuna] the Fen and Yellow Rivers and moved its seat to Wu and Chu, it passed through nine reigns and more than a century. The west had no hope of relief from Qin, and the east nursed the shame of three defeats. Calamity piled upon calamity for a very long time.

sentences.zh: 況乃陵塋幽翳，情敬莫遂，日月推薄，帝心彌遠。

translations.literal: Moreover the imperial tombs lay in gloom and shade, feeling and reverence could not be fulfilled; as days and months pressed on, the imperial heart grew ever more distant.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the imperial tombs lay shrouded in shadow, so that loyal devotion could not be properly paid. As the years wore on, the court's heart turned ever farther from the north.

sentences.zh: 慶靈將升，時來不爽，相國宋公，得一居貞，回乾運軸，內匡寰表，外清遐陬。

translations.literal: Blessed numen was about to rise, the season came without error; the Duke of Song as Chancellor, obtaining the One and dwelling in constancy, turned the axle of Heaven's motion, within rectified the realm's surface, without cleared distant marches.
translations.idiomatic: A blessed age was rising and the moment had come. The Duke of Song, as chief minister, held fast to the right course, turned the wheel of state, restored order within the empire, and cleared the distant frontiers.

sentences.zh: 每以區宇未統，側席盈慮。

translations.literal: He constantly, because the realm was not yet united, sat sideways on his mat with cares overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm was not yet reunified, he constantly sat uneasy on his throne, his mind full of concern.

sentences.zh: 值天祚攸興，昧弱授機，龜筮元謀，符瑞景徵。

translations.literal: It happened that Heaven's mandate was rising; in obscurity the weak received the pivot; tortoise and milfoil gave the primal plan, talismans and auspicious signs were brilliant omens.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate was stirring again: the obscure and weak received their moment, tortoise and milfoil confirmed the grand design, and omens and auspicious signs appeared in abundance.

sentences.zh: 於是仰祗俯協，順天從兆，興止戈之師，躬暫勞之討。

translations.literal: Thereupon looking up in reverence and bowing in accord, following Heaven and obeying the omen, he raised an army to halt the weapons and personally undertook for a time the toilsome punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Then, reverent toward Heaven and in harmony with the signs, he followed destiny's promptings, raised an army to end the fighting, and personally led a campaign of hard exertion.

sentences.zh: 以義熙十有二年五月丁酉，敬戒九伐，申命六軍，治兵于京畿，次師于汳上。

translations.literal: On the dingyou day of the fifth month of the twelfth year of Yixi, with solemn warning he undertook the nine punishments, proclaimed orders to the six armies, drilled troops in the capital region, and stationed the host on the Bian.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the fifth month of the twelfth year of Yixi, he solemnly proclaimed the punitive expedition, issued orders to the six armies, mustered troops in the capital region, and encamped the host on the Bian River.

sentences.zh: 靈檣千艘，靁輜萬乘，羽騎盈途，飛旍蔽日。

translations.literal: Spirit-prowed ships numbered a thousand, thundering supply wagons ten thousand teams, feather-capped horsemen filled the road, flying banners hid the sun.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand warships with spirit prows, ten thousand thundering supply trains, armored horsemen crowding every road, and flying banners that blotted out the sun.

sentences.zh: 別命群帥，誨謨惠策，法奇於《三略》，義秘於《六韜》。

translations.literal: He separately charged the host of commanders with instructive plans and gracious stratagems—methods wondrous beyond the Three Stratagems, principles arcane within the Six Secret Teachings.
translations.idiomatic: He separately charged his generals with wise counsel and generous strategy—tactics more subtle than the Three Stratagems and principles as profound as those in the Six Secret Teachings.

sentences.zh: 所以鉤棘未曜，殞前禽於金墉，威弧始彀，走鈒隼於滑臺。

translations.literal: Thus before the barbed halberd had yet gleamed, the forward quarry fell at Jinyong; when the mighty bow was first drawn, the hooked falcon fled at Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Before his weapons had even flashed in full, the enemy fell at Jinyong; as soon as his bow was drawn, the foe fled in rout from Huatai.

sentences.zh: 曾不踰月，二方獻捷。

translations.literal: In less than a month, both regions presented victory.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month, victory was reported from both fronts.

sentences.zh: 宏功懋德，獨絕古今。

translations.literal: Grand achievement and abundant virtue stood alone beyond past and present.
translations.idiomatic: His great achievement and abundant virtue were unmatched in all history.

sentences.zh: 天子感《東山》之劬勞，慶格天之光大，明發興於鑒寐，使臣遵于原隰。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, moved by the toil in "Dongshan," rejoiced in the vast glory reaching to Heaven; at dawn he rose from mirrored sleep and sent his minister to follow the lowlands and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved by the hardships recalled in "Dongshan," rejoiced in his glory reaching to Heaven; at daybreak he rose from troubled sleep and sent his envoy across the plains and marshes.

sentences.zh: 余攝官承乏，謬充殊役，《皇華》愧於先《雅》，靡盬顇於征人。

translations.literal: I, holding office in default, wrongly filled a special duty; "Splendid the Blossom" shamed me before the earlier "Ya," and I had no comfort for the wearied men on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: I was holding a post in default and was wrongly assigned this special mission; compared with the earlier odes, "Splendid the Blossom" left me ashamed, and I could offer no relief to the weary soldiers on the march.

sentences.zh: 以仲冬就行，分春反命。

translations.literal: I set out in mid-winter and returned with my report at the spring equinox.
translations.idiomatic: I departed in mid-winter and returned with my report at the spring equinox.

sentences.zh: 塗經九守，路踰千里。

translations.literal: The route passed nine garrisons and the road exceeded a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: My route passed nine garrison districts and stretched more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 沿江亂淮，溯薄泗、汳，詳觀城邑，周覽丘墳，眷言古跡，其懷已多。

translations.literal: Along the river I crossed the Huai, upstream I drew near the Si and Bian, closely observed the cities, broadly viewed the mounds and tombs, and turning to speak of ancient traces, my feelings were already many.
translations.idiomatic: I traveled along the Yangzi and crossed the Huai, went upstream toward the Si and Bian, studied the cities in detail, and surveyed mounds and tombs on every side. As I lingered over ancient sites, my heart was full.

sentences.zh: 昔皇祖作藩，受命淮、徐，道固苞桑，勳由仁積。

translations.literal: Formerly my imperial ancestor served as feudatory, received mandate at Huai and Xu; the Way was firm as mulberry roots, merit accumulated through benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago my imperial ancestor held a feudal domain and received his charge on the Huai and Xu. His way was rooted like the mulberry, and his merit was built through humane rule.

sentences.zh: 年月多歷，市朝已改，永為洪業，纏懷清曆。

translations.literal: Years and months had passed in multitude, markets and courts were already changed; forever it became great enterprise, and I was entwined in longing for the clear calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Many years had passed, markets and courts had changed, yet his great enterprise endured, and I was bound in longing for that brighter age.

sentences.zh: 於是釆訪故老，尋履往跡，而遠感深慨，痛心殞涕。

translations.literal: Thereupon I gathered and questioned the old elders, traced and followed former footprints, and from distant feeling came deep sighs; my heart was wounded and tears fell in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: I then sought out the old inhabitants and walked in the footsteps of the past. Deep emotion and heavy sighs overcame me; my heart ached and tears fell.

sentences.zh: 遂寫集聞見，作賦《撰征》，俾事運遷謝，託此不朽。

translations.literal: Then I wrote down and collected what I had heard and seen, composed the rhapsody "Recording the Campaign," so that as affairs and fortune shifted and faded, I might entrust to this imperishability.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore set down what I had heard and seen and wrote the rhapsody "Recording the Campaign," so that though times change and fade, something of them might endure.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: 系烈山之洪緒，承火正之明光。

translations.literal: We are tied to the great lineage of Lieshan and inherit the bright glory of the Director of Fire.
translations.idiomatic: We trace our line to the great house of Lieshan and inherit the bright glory of the fire officer.

sentences.zh: 立熙載於唐后，申譖事於周王。

translations.literal: He established glorious burden after Tang, and presented slanderous affairs to the Zhou king.
translations.idiomatic: He raised up glorious service after the age of Tang and laid his grievances before the Zhou king.

sentences.zh: 疇庸命而順位，錫寶珪以徹疆。

translations.literal: He matched merit to mandate and took his proper place; he was granted the precious jade tablet to mark his border.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was matched to his mandate and he took his rightful place; he received the sacred jade tablet that defined his domain.

sentences.zh: 歷尚代而平顯，降中葉以繁昌。

translations.literal: Through honored ages he was level and manifest; descending to the middle leaf, he flourished in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Through glorious ages his house stood plain and bright; in the middle period it grew rich and flourishing.

sentences.zh: 業服道而德徽，風行世而化揚。

translations.literal: His enterprise submitted to the Way and his virtue was illustrious; his wind moved through the age and transformation was raised.
translations.idiomatic: His house followed the Way and his virtue shone; his influence spread through the world and his transforming power was exalted.

sentences.zh: 投前蹤以永冀，省輶質以遠傷。

translations.literal: I cast myself on former tracks for lasting hope and examined the light carriage of substance to keep distant harm.
translations.idiomatic: I set my hopes on the footprints of the past and examined my own slight worth to keep sorrow far away.

sentences.zh: 睽謀始於蓍蔡，違用舍於行藏。

translations.literal: Estranged counsel began with milfoil and tortoise; going against employment and release in action and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Divination with milfoil and tortoise first revealed estrangement; advance and withdrawal depended on when to act and when to hide.

sentences.zh: 庇常善之罔棄，憑曲成之不遺。

translations.literal: Sheltered by constant goodness that is not cast away, relying on crooked completion that does not abandon.
translations.idiomatic: Sheltered by constant kindness that is never cast aside, I rely on partial success that is never forgotten.

sentences.zh: 昭在幽而偕煦，賞彌久而愈私。

translations.literal: Brightness in the dark shares warmth; favor through long time grows ever more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: His light shines even in darkness and shares its warmth; his favor, the longer it lasts, grows ever more personal.

sentences.zh: 顧晚草之薄弱，仰青春之葳蕤。

translations.literal: I look back on late grass, weak and thin, and gaze up at spring green, lush and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: I see myself as late grass, frail and slight, and look up to the lush verdure of spring.

sentences.zh: 引蔓穎於松上，擢纖枝於蘭逵。

translations.literal: I draw trailing tips onto the pine and pluck slender branches on orchid paths.
translations.idiomatic: I trail my shoots onto the pine and raise slender branches along orchid-lined paths.

sentences.zh: 施隆貸而有渥，報涓塵而無期。

translations.literal: He bestows lofty favor with richness; to repay a speck of dust has no term.
translations.idiomatic: He grants generous favor in abundance; to repay even a speck of dust seems beyond any deadline.

sentences.zh: 歡太階之休明，穆皇道之緝熙。

translations.literal: I rejoice in the great terrace's restful brightness and in the solemn imperial Way, well ordered and shining.
translations.idiomatic: I rejoice in the peace and brilliance of the age and in the solemn, well-governed imperial Way.

sentences.zh: 惟王建國，辨方定隅，內外既正，華夷有殊。

translations.literal: When the king established the state, he distinguished regions and fixed the corners; within and without were already rectified, and Hua and Yi had their differences.
translations.idiomatic: When the king founded the realm, he marked the regions and fixed the borders; inner and outer were set right, and the center and the barbarians were kept distinct.

sentences.zh: 惟昔《小雅》，逮于班書，戎蠻孔熾，是殛是誅。

translations.literal: From old in the "Lesser Ya" down to the Ban histories, Rong and Man were greatly rampant—thus they were punished and executed.
translations.idiomatic: From the "Lesser Ya" odes down to the histories of Ban Gu, the Rong and Man grew fiercely strong and had to be punished and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 所以宣王用棘於獫狁，高帝方事於匈奴。

translations.literal: Therefore King Xuan used thorns against the Xianyun, and the High Emperor was just then engaged with the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Thus King Xuan took up arms against the Xianyun, and the founding emperor of Han was then campaigning against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 然侵鎬至涇，自塞及平。

translations.literal: Yet they invaded from Hao to the Jing, from the passes to Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they raided from the capital region to the Jing River, from the frontier passes to the plains.

sentences.zh: 闚郊伺鄙，□□□□。

translations.literal: They spied on the suburbs and watched the borders, [text lost].
translations.idiomatic: They peered at the suburbs and watched the frontier towns, [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 慕攜王之矯處，階喪亂之未寧。

translations.literal: They admired King Xie's forced sojourn and climbed the steps of disorder not yet pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They took King Xie's forced exile as a model and rose on the unrest that had not yet been settled.

sentences.zh: 竊彊秦之三輔，陷隆周之兩京。

translations.literal: They stole the three adjuncts of mighty Qin and overthrew the two capitals of illustrious Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the three metropolitan districts of Qin and captured the two capitals of glorious Zhou.

sentences.zh: 雄崤、澠以制險，據繞霤而作扃。

translations.literal: They made Xiao and Mian formidable to control the passes and held the winding defiles as a barred gate.
translations.idiomatic: They fortified the Xiao and Mian passes to command the terrain and held the winding defiles as a barred gateway.

sentences.zh: 家永懷於故壤，國願言於先塋。

translations.literal: Families forever yearn for the old soil; the state longs to speak of the ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Families forever yearn for their native soil, and the state longs to return to the tombs of its forefathers.

sentences.zh: 俟太平之曠期，屬應運之聖明。

translations.literal: They await the distant term of great peace and belong to the sage brilliance that meets the age's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: They await the long-deferred age of peace and now belong to the sage ruler who answers the call of the times.

sentences.zh: 坤寄通於四瀆，乾假照於三辰。

translations.literal: Earth lodges and communicates through the four streams; Heaven lends its illumination to the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Earth extends its reach through the four great rivers; Heaven lends its light to sun, moon, and stars.

sentences.zh: 水潤土以顯比，火炎天而同人。

translations.literal: Water moistens earth to show union; fire blazes toward Heaven and joins with men.
translations.idiomatic: Water moistens the earth in manifest union; fire rises to Heaven in fellowship with mankind.

sentences.zh: 惟上相之叡哲，當草昧而經綸。

translations.literal: Only the chief minister's sage wisdom, in the twilight of origins, laid out the great design.
translations.idiomatic: Only the chief minister's sage wisdom, in the chaos of a new age, wove the great design of state.

sentences.zh: 總九流以貞觀，協五才而平分。

translations.literal: He gathered the nine streams for correct viewing and harmonized the five talents in equal division.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered all schools of thought into a true vision and balanced the five talents in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 時來之機，悟先於介石，納隍之誡，一援於生民。

translations.literal: The pivot of the season's coming—he understood it first in the jade tablet; the warning of the pit's brink—he once rescued the living people.
translations.idiomatic: He grasped the moment's turning point as if reading it in jade, and at the brink of the pit he once lifted the people to safety.

sentences.zh: 龜筮允臧，人鬼同情。

translations.literal: Tortoise and milfoil were truly good; men and ghosts shared the same feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Tortoise and milfoil confirmed the omen; the living and the dead were of one mind.

sentences.zh: 順天行誅，司典詳刑。

translations.literal: Following Heaven he carried out punishment; the minister of rites reviewed the penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Following Heaven's mandate he carried out punishment, and the minister of rites reviewed the penalties in detail.

sentences.zh: 樹牙選徒，秉鉞抗旍。

translations.literal: He planted the battle standards and chose the troops, grasped the battle-axe and raised the pennants.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the battle standards and chose his troops, took up the battle-axe and raised the war banners.

sentences.zh: 弧矢罄楚孝之心智，戈棘單吳子之精靈。

translations.literal: Bows and arrows exhausted the loyal heart of Chu; spears and halberds alone held the spirit of the Son of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Bows and arrows bore all the loyal resolve of Chu; spears and halberds alone embodied the martial spirit of Wu.

sentences.zh: 迅三翼以魚麗，襄兩服以雁逝。

translations.literal: Swiftly the three wings formed the fish-scale array; the two wings were wrapped as geese in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Swiftly the three wings formed the fish-scale formation; the two wings swept forward like geese in flight.

sentences.zh: 陣未列於都甸，威已振於秦、薊。

translations.literal: Before the battle line was drawn in the capital fields, his might already shook Qin and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army even formed its ranks in the capital region, his might had already shaken Qin and Ji.

sentences.zh: 灑嚴霜於渭城，被和風於洛汭。

translations.literal: He sprinkled stern frost on Weicheng and spread gentle wind on the Luo bend.
translations.idiomatic: He brought stern justice to Weicheng and gentle peace to the bend of the Luo.

sentences.zh: 就終古以比猷，考墳冊而莫契。

translations.literal: Measured against the farthest antiquity for comparison of plans, examined in tomb records yet none matched.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with all antiquity, his design had no parallel; searched through the records of the past, none matched it.

sentences.zh: 昔西怨於東徂，今北伐而南悲。

translations.literal: Formerly the west grieved at marching east; now on the northern campaign the south laments.
translations.idiomatic: Once the west grieved at marching east; now on the northern campaign the south is filled with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 豈朝野之恆情，動萬乘之幽思。

translations.literal: Was this merely the constant feeling of court and countryside? It moved the ten-thousand-chariot lord's hidden thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Was this only the usual feeling of court and country? It stirred the emperor's deepest thoughts.

sentences.zh: 歌零雨於《豳風》，興《采薇》於周詩。

translations.literal: He sang of drizzling rain in the "Bin Airs" and raised "Gathering Thorn-fern" from the Zhou odes.
translations.idiomatic: He sang of drizzling rain as in the "Bin Airs" and took up "Gathering Thorn-fern" from the Zhou odes.

sentences.zh: 慶金墉之凱定，眷戎車之遷時。

translations.literal: He rejoiced in the triumph settled at Jinyong and was attached to the war chariot's shifting season.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoiced that victory was secured at Jinyong and lingered over the season when the war chariots had moved.

sentences.zh: 佇千里而感遠，涉弦望而懷期。

translations.literal: He stood a thousand li and felt the distance; he crossed the bow's span and gazed, cherishing the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: He waited a thousand li away, moved by distance; he gazed across the horizon, holding to the promised day.

sentences.zh: 詔微臣以勞問，奉王命於河湄。

translations.literal: He decreed the humble minister to offer comfort and inquiry and to bear the king's command on the river's bank.
translations.idiomatic: He charged this humble minister to offer congratulations and bear the royal command to the river's bank.

sentences.zh: 夕飲餞以俶裝，旦出宿而言辭。

translations.literal: At evening they drank the farewell and fitted the traveling gear; at dawn I went out to lodge and spoke my parting words.
translations.idiomatic: At evening they gave a farewell feast and I made ready to depart; at dawn I set out, lodged overnight, and spoke my farewells.

sentences.zh: 歲既晏而繁慮，日將邁而戀乖。

translations.literal: The year was already late and cares multiplied; the day was about to pass and longing clung to separation.
translations.idiomatic: The year was already late and my cares multiplied; the day was passing and I clung to those I must leave.

sentences.zh: 闕敬恭於桑梓，謝履長於庭階。

translations.literal: I lacked reverent respect at the mulberry homeland and took leave of treading long on the courtyard steps.
translations.idiomatic: I could not pay full respect at my native place and bade farewell to the long-familiar steps of the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 冒沈雲之晻藹，迎素雪之紛霏。

translations.literal: I braved the deep clouds' dim mist and met the plain snow's drifting fall.
translations.idiomatic: I passed through deep clouds, dim and close, and met plain snow drifting down.

sentences.zh: 淩結湍而凝清，風矜籟以揚哀。

translations.literal: I crossed frozen rapids into congealed clarity; the wind, stern in the pipes, raised sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: I crossed frozen rapids into icy clarity; the wind, sharp in the reeds, lifted a note of grief.

sentences.zh: 情在本而易阜，物雖末而難懷。

translations.literal: Feeling lies in the root and easily mounts; things though slight are hard to hold in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling springs from the root and easily swells; even slight things are hard to bear in the heart.

sentences.zh: 眷余勤以就路，苦憂來其城頹。

translations.literal: Attached to my diligence in taking the road, bitter grief came like a crumbling wall.
translations.idiomatic: Though I pressed on diligently along the road, bitter grief came like a wall collapsing inward.

sentences.zh: 爾乃經雉門，啟浮梁，眺鍾巖，越查塘。

translations.literal: Then I passed the Pheasant Gate, opened the floating bridge, gazed from Bell Cliff, and crossed Zha Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Then I passed the Pheasant Gate, crossed the floating bridge, gazed from Bell Cliff, and went over Zha Pond.

sentences.zh: 覽永嘉之紊維，尋建武之緝綱。

translations.literal: I viewed the tangled cords of Yongjia and sought the drawn net of Jianwu.
translations.idiomatic: I surveyed the tangled disorder of the Yongjia era and traced the restored order of the Jianwu reign.

sentences.zh: 于時內慢神器，外侮戎狄。

translations.literal: At that time within they slighted the sacred vessel; without, Rong and Di insulted them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court neglected the imperial regalia within, while the Rong and Di harassed them from without.

sentences.zh: 君子橫流，庶萌分析。

translations.literal: The noble men drifted in torrent; the common sprouts split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Men of worth were swept adrift, and the common people were torn apart.

sentences.zh: 主晉有祀，福祿來格。

translations.literal: The lord of Jin had sacrifice; blessing and emolument came to lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Jin still had its sacrifices, and blessing and rank returned.

sentences.zh: 明兩降覽，三七辭厄。

translations.literal: The two bright ones descended to view; at three-seven they left distress.
translations.idiomatic: The two bright rulers looked down from on high; at the twenty-first year they escaped calamity.

sentences.zh: 元誕德以膺緯，肇回光於陽宅。

translations.literal: The Primal was born with virtue to receive the celestial woof and first turned back light in the yang dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The Primal Emperor was born with virtue to receive Heaven's mandate and first brought back light to the yang realm.

sentences.zh: 明思服於下武，興繼代以消逆。

translations.literal: Ming thought to submit to the later martial one and rose to continue the age to extinguish rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sought to follow the later martial ruler and raised a successor age to put down rebellion.

sentences.zh: 簡文因心以秉道，故沖用而刑廢。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen followed the heart to hold the Way, therefore in empty use punishments were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen held to the Way through inner sincerity, and therefore in gentle rule punishments fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 孝武捨己以杖賢，亦寧外而治內。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu set himself aside to lean on the worthy and also pacified without while governing within.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu set himself aside to rely on the worthy and pacified the outer realm while governing within.

sentences.zh: 觀日化而就損，庶雍熙之可對。

translations.literal: Observing the daily transformation he achieved decrease, hoping that harmonious splendor might be answered.
translations.idiomatic: Watching the daily change he practiced restraint, hoping that a harmonious age might yet be attained.

sentences.zh: 閔隆安之致寇，傷龜玉之毀碎。

translations.literal: He grieved that Long'an brought invaders and mourned the tortoise jade's shattering.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved that the Long'an era brought invaders and mourned the shattering of the sacred jade and tortoise.

sentences.zh: 漏妖凶於滄洲，纏釁難而盈紀。

translations.literal: Leaked calamities grew fierce at Cangzhou; border conflicts entangled and filled a full cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters and evil omens ravaged the coastal lands, and border warfare entangled the realm for a full twelve-year cycle.

sentences.zh: 時焉依於晉、鄭，國有蹙於百里。

translations.literal: At times one relied on Jin and Zheng; the state's territory was constricted to a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: At times the court could lean only on fragmented allies like Jin and Zheng, and the state's domain shrank to a mere hundred li.

sentences.zh: 賴英謨之經營，弘兼濟以忘己。

translations.literal: Relying on heroic strategy's management, he broadly aided all and forgot himself.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to his heroic planning and stewardship, he broadly aided others and forgot himself in the cause.

sentences.zh: 主寰內而緩虞，澄海外以漬滓。

translations.literal: He governed the inner realm and eased anxieties; he clarified the overseas and washed away dregs.
translations.idiomatic: He held the inner realm and eased its fears, and cleared the outer marches, washing away the filth of disorder.

sentences.zh: 至如昏祲蔽景，鼎祚傾基。

translations.literal: As when dark miasma veils the sun, the imperial foundation's base topples.
translations.idiomatic: Dark omens blocked the sun, and the throne's foundations gave way.

sentences.zh: 《黍離》有歎，《鴻雁》無期。

translations.literal: "Shu's Lament" has sighs; "Wild Geese" has no fixed date.
translations.idiomatic: There were sighs like those in "Shu's Lament," and longings like "Wild Geese" with no hope of return.

sentences.zh: 瞻天命之貞符，秉順動而履機。

translations.literal: He gazed upon Heaven's mandate's true sign; he held to compliant action and trod the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: He looked to Heaven's true mandate, acted in accord with the times, and seized the turning point.

sentences.zh: 率駿民之思效，普邦國而同歸。

translations.literal: He led the excellent people's desire to serve; universally among states they returned together.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the people's desire to serve, and all the realm turned to him as one.

sentences.zh: 蕩積霾之穢氛，啟披陰之光暉。

translations.literal: He cleared the accumulated haze's foul vapors; he opened and parted the shade's bright radiance.
translations.idiomatic: He swept away the foul vapors of accumulated gloom and parted the clouds to let bright light shine through.

sentences.zh: 反平陵之杳藹，復七廟之依俙。

translations.literal: He restored Pingling's dim mist; he restored the seven temples' nearness.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the shadowed imperial tombs at Pingling and brought the seven ancestral temples back to their former dignity.

sentences.zh: 務役簡而農勸，每勞賞而忠甄。

translations.literal: Corvée labor was simplified and farming encouraged; every reward for labor and loyalty was discerned.
translations.idiomatic: He simplified forced labor and encouraged farming, rewarding every loyal effort and distinguishing true devotion.

sentences.zh: 燮時雍於祖宗，□□□□□□。

translations.literal: He harmonized the age at the ancestors, [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: He brought harmony to the ancestral rites and the age, [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 掃逋醜於漢渚，滌僭逆於岷山。

translations.literal: He swept fugitive villains at Han Ford; he washed usurpers at Min Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He swept fugitive rebels from the Han Ford on the Yangtze and cleansed usurpers from the Min Mountains in Shu.

sentences.zh: 羈巢處於西木，引鼻飲於源淵。

translations.literal: Tethered nests dwelt in western woods; they led trunks to drink at source abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians who nested in the western forests led their elephants trunk by trunk to drink at deep springs.

sentences.zh: 惠要襋而思韙，援冠弁而來處。

translations.literal: He rewarded with caps and robes and they thought of virtue; they drew official caps and came to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed caps and robes with grace, and they pondered righteousness; they put on official regalia and came to submit.

sentences.zh: 視冶城而北屬，懷文獻之收揚。

translations.literal: He viewed Yecheng and turned north; he cherished culture and merit's gathering and raising.
translations.idiomatic: He looked upon Yecheng and turned north, cherishing how culture and merit had been gathered and raised up.

sentences.zh: 匪元首之康哉，孰股肱之惟良。

translations.literal: If not the chief's well-being, who would be the excellent arm and thigh?
translations.idiomatic: Without a sovereign's well-being, how could there be excellent ministers to serve as his arms and legs?

sentences.zh: 譬觀曲而識節，似綴組以成章。

translations.literal: It is like observing a melody to recognize the beat; like threading tokens to form a pattern.
translations.idiomatic: It is like knowing the rhythm by listening to the melody, or reading the design by seeing how the threads are strung.

sentences.zh: 業彌纏而彌微，事愈有而莫傷。

translations.literal: The enterprise grew ever more entangled yet ever finer; affairs grew ever more numerous yet were never harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Their enterprise grew ever more intricate yet refined, and though affairs multiplied, nothing was harmed.

sentences.zh: 次石頭之雙岸，究孫氏之初基。

translations.literal: He stopped at Shitou's twin banks; he investigated the Sun clan's original foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He paused at the twin banks of Shitou and traced the Sun clan's earliest foundations.

sentences.zh: 幸漢庶之漏網，憑江介以抗維。

translations.literal: Fortunately Han refugees slipped through the net; relying on river barriers they resisted and endured.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chinese refugees fortunately escaped the net of chaos and, relying on the river barrier, held out and endured.

sentences.zh: 初鵲起於富春，果鯨躍於川湄。

translations.literal: At first a magpie rose at Fuchun; indeed a whale leaped at the river's edge.
translations.idiomatic: At first like a magpie rising at Fuchun, then truly like a whale leaping from the river's edge.

sentences.zh: 匝三世而國盛，歷五偽而宗夷。

translations.literal: Spanning three generations the state flourished; passing five usurpers the lineage was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: For three generations the state prospered, but after five false rulers the royal line was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 察成敗之相仍，猶脣亡而齒寒。

translations.literal: Observing success and failure in succession, it was still like lips gone and teeth cold.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how success and failure followed one another, it was still the proverb: when the lips are gone, the teeth grow cold.

sentences.zh: 載十二而謂紀，豈蜀滅而吳安。

translations.literal: Recording twelve and calling it an era — how could Wu be secure when Shu perished?
translations.idiomatic: They marked twelve years as one cycle — yet how could Wu remain secure once Shu had fallen?

sentences.zh: 眾咸昧於謀兆，羊獨悟於理端。

translations.literal: All were blind to the omen within the plan; Yang alone grasped the principle's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone else missed the signs hidden in the strategy, but Yang Hu alone saw where the logic led.

sentences.zh: 請廣武以誨情，樹襄陽以作藩。

translations.literal: He requested Guangwu to instruct intentions; he planted Xiangyang as a frontier screen.
translations.idiomatic: He urged building defenses at Guangwu to make the point clear, and established Xiangyang as a strategic bulwark.

sentences.zh: 拾建業其如遺，沿萬里而誰難。

translations.literal: Gathering Jiankang as if abandoned; along ten thousand li, who could oppose?
translations.idiomatic: They held Jiankang as if it were already lost, and along ten thousand li of frontier, who could stand against them?

sentences.zh: 疾魯荒之詖辭，惡京陵之譖言。

translations.literal: He loathed Lu Huang's false words; he hated Jingling's slander.
translations.idiomatic: He despised the twisted words of Lu Bao and the slanders spread from Jingling.

sentences.zh: 責當朝之憚貶，對曩籍而興歎。

translations.literal: He blamed the court for fearing demotion; facing old records he raised sighs.
translations.idiomatic: He reproached the court for fearing censure, and turned to the old annals with a deep sigh.

sentences.zh: 敦怙寵而判違，敵既勍而國圮。

translations.literal: Dun relied on favor and broke faith; the enemy was already strong and the state collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, pampered by royal favor, turned against the throne; the foe grew powerful and the state broke apart.

sentences.zh: 彼問鼎而何階，必先賊於君子。

translations.literal: They asked about the tripod — what steps could there be? One must first destroy the noble men.
translations.idiomatic: Those who ask about seizing the tripod — what path is there? They must first destroy the men of worth.

sentences.zh: 原性分之異託，雖殊塗而歸美。

translations.literal: Tracing nature's different entrustments, though paths differed they returned to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how nature assigns different roles: though their paths diverged, each in the end earned its praise.

sentences.zh: 或卷舒以愚智，或治亂其如矢。

translations.literal: Some expanded and contracted by folly and wisdom; some order and chaos were straight as arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Some advanced or retreated through folly or wisdom; for others, rise and fall flew straight as an arrow.

sentences.zh: 謝昧跡而託規，卒安身以全里。

translations.literal: Xie hid his tracks and entrusted rules; in the end he secured his person and preserved his village.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An concealed his ambitions and entrusted his counsel, and in the end preserved himself and his household.

sentences.zh: 周顯節而犯逆，抱正情而喪己。

translations.literal: Zhou displayed integrity yet committed treason; he held righteous feeling yet lost himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi showed forthright integrity yet fell into rebellion; he clung to righteousness yet destroyed himself.

sentences.zh: 薄四望而尤眄，歎王路之中鯁。

translations.literal: He looked thinly in four directions with anxious gaze; he sighed that the royal way was blocked mid-throat.
translations.idiomatic: He scanned the four quarters with anxious eyes and lamented that the royal road was choked.

sentences.zh: 蠢干越之妖燼，敢淩蹈於五嶺。

translations.literal: The foolish Gan-Yue remnant embers dared to tread upon the Five Ridges.
translations.idiomatic: The mad remnants of the Gan-Yue cult dared to invade across the Five Ridges.

sentences.zh: 崩雙嶽於中流，擬凶威於荊郢。

translations.literal: Twin peaks collapsed midstream; fierce might matched Jing and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Twin peaks seemed to crumble in midstream, and their fierce power rivaled that of old Jing and Ying.

sentences.zh: 隱雷霆於帝坐，飛芒鏃於宮省。

translations.literal: Thunder hid at the imperial seat; flying arrowheads at the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder seemed to gather at the emperor's throne, and arrowheads flew through the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 于時朝有遷都之議，人無守死之志。

translations.literal: At that time the court had debate over moving the capital; people lacked the will to die defending it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court debated abandoning the capital, and the people had no heart to die in its defense.

sentences.zh: 師旅痛於久勤，城墉闕於素備。

translations.literal: Armies were pained by long exertion; walls lacked their usual preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The armies were worn down by long campaigns, and the city walls had never been properly fortified.

sentences.zh: 安危勢在不侔，眾寡形於見事。

translations.literal: Safety and danger — the power was unmatched; few and many — it showed in visible events.
translations.idiomatic: Safety and danger were grossly unequal in strength, and the mismatch between the few and the many was plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 於赫淵謀，研其神策。

translations.literal: Splendid was the deep counsel; he studied its divine strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid was the profound counsel; he refined its master strategy.

sentences.zh: 緩轡待機，追奔躡跡。

translations.literal: He slackened reins and awaited opportunity; he pursued the fleeing and trod their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: He held his forces in check and waited for the right moment, then pursued the fleeing enemy and ran them down.

sentences.zh: 遇雷池而振曜，次彭蠡而殲滌。

translations.literal: He met Lei Pool and shook radiance; next at Poyang Lake he annihilated and cleansed.
translations.idiomatic: At Lei Pool his banners blazed forth; then at Lake Poyang he destroyed and swept clean the enemy.

sentences.zh: 穆京甸以清晏，撤多壘而寧役。

translations.literal: He placated the capital region into clear calm; he withdrew many fortresses and pacified corvée.
translations.idiomatic: He brought peace and order to the capital region, dismantled redundant fortresses, and eased the people's labor.

sentences.zh: 造白石之祠壇，懟二豎之無君。

translations.literal: He built the white stone altar; he confronted the two petty men without a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan built an altar at White Stone and set himself up as ruler; two worthless rebels defied all authority.

sentences.zh: 踐掖庭以幽辱，凌祧社而火焚。

translations.literal: He tread the inner court with dark humiliation; he overstepped the ancestral temple and set fire.
translations.idiomatic: They trampled the inner palace in shameful disgrace and attacked the ancestral temple with fire.

sentences.zh: 愍文康之罪己，嘉忠武之立勳。

translations.literal: He pitied Wen Kang's self-blame; he praised Loyal Martial's establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned Wang Dao's self-reproach and praised Liu Yu for establishing his loyal merit.

sentences.zh: 道有屈於災蝕，功無謝於如仁。

translations.literal: The Way had bends from disaster and erosion; achievements owed no decline compared with such benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The Way was bent by calamity and decay, yet merit never fell short of true benevolence.

sentences.zh: 訊落星之饗旅，索舊棲於吳餘。

translations.literal: I inquired after the fallen star's lodging for travelers, seeking old dwellings among Wu's remnants.
translations.idiomatic: I asked about the hostel of the falling star and searched for ancestral homes among the ruins of Wu.

sentences.zh: 跡階戺而不見，橫榛卉以荒除。

translations.literal: Traces of steps and thresholds were nowhere seen; brambles and wild plants sprawled over abandoned paths.
translations.idiomatic: No sign remained of steps or doorways; thorny weeds choked the overgrown clearings.

sentences.zh: 彼生成之樂辰，亦猶今之在余。

translations.literal: Those days of birth and growth in happy seasons are still, as today, within me.
translations.idiomatic: The joyful days of that generation live on in memory, as vivid to me as the present.

sentences.zh: 慨齊吟於爽鳩，悲唐歌於《山樞》。

translations.literal: I sighed over Qi's lament at Shuangjiu, grieved at Tang's song in "Discarding the Juniper."
translations.idiomatic: I sighed at Qi's songs at Shuangjiu and mourned to Tang's lyrics in the "Discarding the Juniper" ode.

sentences.zh: 弔偽孫於徐首，率君臣以奉疆。

translations.literal: I mourned the false Sun at Xu Shou, where ruler and ministers led the land in submission.
translations.idiomatic: At Xu Shou I mourned the puppet Sun ruler, where king and court once held the realm in fealty.

sentences.zh: 時運師以伐罪，偏投書於武王。

translations.literal: The season favored the army in punishing crime; they sent over letters of surrender to King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's timing favored the punitive campaign, and they sent letters of submission to King Wu.

sentences.zh: 迄西北之落紐，乏東南以振綱。

translations.literal: When the northwest's ties were severed at last, the southeast lacked strength to restore the guiding cord.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the northwest's lifeline was cut, the southeast could no longer rally the reign's order.

sentences.zh: 誠鉅平之先覺，實中興之後祥。

translations.literal: Truly Juping's early foresight, indeed the later auspice of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: It was truly Juping's prescience—and truly an omen of the later restoration.

sentences.zh: 據左史之攸徵，胡影跡之可量。

translations.literal: Relying on the Left Historian's verified signs, how could traces or shadows be measured?
translations.idiomatic: By the Left Historian's recorded evidence, how can such shadows and traces even be reckoned?

sentences.zh: 過江乘而責始，知遇雄之無謀。

translations.literal: Crossing at Jiangcheng to hold the beginning to account, I knew that meeting the Hero lacked all strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the river at Jiangcheng, I traced blame to its source and saw that confronting the mighty was folly without a plan.

sentences.zh: 厭紫微之宏凱，甘陵波而遠遊。

translations.literal: Weary of Ziwei's grand triumph, he gladly rode the waves on distant travels.
translations.idiomatic: Tired of the grand victories at the Purple Residence, he was content to ride the waves and wander far.

sentences.zh: 越雲夢而南泝，臨浙河而東浮。

translations.literal: Crossing Yunmeng and ascending southward, approaching the Zhe River and drifting east.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Yunmeng Marsh and traced south, then reached the Zhe River and floated east.

sentences.zh: 彀連弩於川上，候蛟龍於中流。

translations.literal: He strung repeating crossbows along the riverbanks, waiting for flood dragons in midstream.
translations.idiomatic: Along the river he set repeating crossbows and waited for dragons in the midstream currents.

sentences.zh: 爰薄方與，迺屆歐陽。

translations.literal: Then passing close by Fangyu, he arrived at Ouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Fangyu, he came at last to Ouyang.

sentences.zh: 入夫江都之域，次乎廣陵之鄉。

translations.literal: He entered the territory of Jiangdu and halted in the district of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the lands of Jiangdu and made camp in the countryside of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 易千里之曼曼，泝江流之湯湯。

translations.literal: The endless thousand li gave way; he traced back against the surging river current.
translations.idiomatic: The vast thousand li fell away behind him as he pushed upstream against the rushing river.

sentences.zh: 洊赤圻以經復，越二門而起漲。

translations.literal: Again and again he passed Chichi; crossing Two Gates, the waters rose.
translations.idiomatic: He passed Red Embankment time and again, and surging flood rose as he crossed the Twin Gates.

sentences.zh: 眷北路以興思，看東山而怡目。

translations.literal: Gazing toward the northern road stirred his thoughts; looking at Eastern Hill pleased his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Looking north along the road stirred deep thoughts; turning to Eastern Hill delighted his eyes.

sentences.zh: 林叢薄，路逶迤，石參差，山盤曲。

translations.literal: Dense groves and thin woods; winding roads; uneven stones; coiling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Thick forest and sparse undergrowth, winding paths, jagged stones, and mountains that loop and fold.

sentences.zh: 水激瀨而駿奔，日映石而知旭。

translations.literal: Water struck rapids and surged swiftly; sunlight on the stones showed the dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Rapids drove the water into a fierce rush; sunlight glinting on stone announced the rising sun.

sentences.zh: 審兼照之無偏，怨歸流之難濯。

translations.literal: Observing impartial double illumination, he resented that returning currents are hard to cleanse.
translations.idiomatic: He saw that light shines on all without favor—and resented how a returning stream cannot wash away the stain.

sentences.zh: 羨輕魵之涵泳，觀翔鷗之落啄。

translations.literal: He envied small fish swimming beneath the surface; he watched soaring gulls descend to peck.
translations.idiomatic: He envied the small fish darting underwater and watched gulls wheel down to dip and feed.

sentences.zh: 在飛沈其順從，顧微躬而緬邈。

translations.literal: Whether flying or sinking, all followed their nature; turning to his humble self, he felt far away.
translations.idiomatic: In rise and fall alike they yielded to their nature; glancing at his own slight frame, he felt immeasurably distant.

sentences.zh: 於是抑懷蕩慮，揚搉易難。

translations.literal: Thereupon he checked his heart and cleared his cares, weighing what is easy against what is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Then he checked his feelings, cleared his mind, and weighed ease against hardship.

sentences.zh: 利涉以吉，天險以艱。

translations.literal: Crossing benefited from auspiciousness; Heaven's peril brought hardship.
translations.idiomatic: To cross brought good fortune; Heaven's natural barrier brought hardship.

sentences.zh: 于敵伊阻，在國斯便。

translations.literal: For the enemy it was a barrier; for the state it was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: For the foe it was an obstacle; for the realm it was an advantage.

sentences.zh: 勾踐行霸於琅邪，夫差爭長於黃川。

translations.literal: Goujian pursued hegemony at Langye; Fuchai vied for ascendancy at Huangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Goujian set out to build his hegemony at Langye, and Fuchai contested for mastery at Huangchuan.

sentences.zh: 葛相發歎而思正，曹后愧心於千魂。

translations.literal: Prime Minister Ge sighed and longed for rectitude; Lady Cao felt shame before the Thousand Souls.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Ge sighed and yearned for righteousness; Lady Cao was stricken with shame at Qian Hun.

sentences.zh: 登高堞以詳覽，知吳濞之衰盛。

translations.literal: Climbing the high parapet to look closely, I learned of Liu Bi's rise and decline.
translations.idiomatic: From the high battlements I took a long look and saw the rise and fall of Liu Bi of Wu.

sentences.zh: 戒東南之逆氣，成劉后之駴聖。

translations.literal: Warning against rebellious vapors in the southeast, fulfilling Empress Liu's startled awe of the sage.
translations.idiomatic: A warning against the rebellious spirit of the southeast—and the moment that left Empress Liu awestruck before a sage.

sentences.zh: 藉鹽鐵之殷阜，臨淮楚之剽輕。

translations.literal: Relying on the wealth of salt and iron, facing the swift fierceness of Huai and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: They drew on the riches of salt and iron and faced the reckless swiftness of Huai and Chu.

sentences.zh: 盛几杖而弭心，怒抵局而遂爭。

translations.literal: Presenting mat and staff to calm the heart, yet in anger striking the game board they came to strife.
translations.idiomatic: They offered seat and cane to soothe tempers, yet in rage one struck the chessboard—and conflict erupted.

sentences.zh: 忿爰盎之扶禍，惜徒傷於家令。

translations.literal: Angry at Yuan Ang's sustaining calamity, regretting that only the household commandant was harmed in vain.
translations.idiomatic: They raged at Yuan Ang for nursing disaster and lamented that only the Household Commandant was pointlessly ruined.

sentences.zh: 匪條侯之忠毅，將七國之陵正。

translations.literal: Had it not been for the Marquis of Tiao's loyal steadfastness, the seven states would have overturned righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Without the Marquis of Tiao's loyal resolve, the seven states would have trampled the righteous order.

sentences.zh: 褒漢藩之治民，竝訪賢以招明。

translations.literal: They praised the Han prince's governance of the people, and together sought the worthy to summon wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: They praised how the Han princes governed their people and searched out worthy men to draw in enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 侯文辨其誰在，曰鄒陽與枚生。

translations.literal: The marquis in his refined discourse asked who remained; the answer was Zou Yang and Master Mei.
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked who among the eloquent still remained—and was told Zou Yang and Mei Sheng.

sentences.zh: 據忠辭於吳朝，執義說於梁庭。

translations.literal: Upholding loyal words in the court of Wu, holding to righteous persuasion in the hall of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yang held to loyal speech in Wu's court; Mei Sheng argued righteousness in Liang's hall.

sentences.zh: 敷高才於兔園，雖正言而免刑。

translations.literal: He displayed lofty talent in the Rabbit Garden; though his words were upright, he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He showed his brilliant gifts in the Rabbit Garden and, though he spoke plain truth, was spared the lash.

sentences.zh: 闕里既已千載，深儒流於末學。

translations.literal: Confucius's hometown had already seen a thousand years; deep Confucian learning had flowed into shallow late learning.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand years had passed since Confucius's home; profound Confucianism had been thinned to shallow study of the later age.

sentences.zh: 欽仲舒之睟容，遵縫掖於前躅。

translations.literal: He admired Zhongshu's serene bearing and followed in the scholar's robe along earlier footsteps.
translations.idiomatic: He revered Dong Zhongshu's calm dignity and followed, in scholar's garb, the path of those who came before.

sentences.zh: 對園囿而不闚，下帷幕而論屬。

translations.literal: Facing gardens and parks without peering in, he lowered curtains and debated classification.
translations.idiomatic: He faced the park without stealing a glance and, behind lowered curtains, held forth on the order of things.

sentences.zh: 相端、非之兩驕，遭弘、偃之雙慝。

translations.literal: Duan and Fei, the two proud men, met Hong and Yan, the paired villains.
translations.idiomatic: The proud pair Duan and Fei crossed paths with the treacherous pair Hong and Yan.

sentences.zh: 恨有道之無時，步險塗以側足。

translations.literal: He grieved that the Way had no season; he walked a perilous path on sidelong feet.
translations.idiomatic: He lamented that the Way had no proper age and picked his way along a dangerous road on cautious feet.

sentences.zh: 聞宣武之大閱，反師旅於此廛。

translations.literal: Hearing of Xuanwu's great review, he turned the army back to this market town.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of Emperor Xuanwu's grand inspection, he marched the host back to this town.

sentences.zh: 自皇運之都東，始昌業以濟難。

translations.literal: Since the imperial fortune moved its capital east, the enterprise first flourished in aiding through hardship.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic fortune shifted eastward, the realm first prospered by meeting crisis with resolve.

sentences.zh: 抗素旄於秦嶺，揚朱旗於巴川。

translations.literal: They raised white banners on Qinling and flew red flags over Bachuan.
translations.idiomatic: White standards rose on the Qin Mountains; red banners unfurled over the Ba River lands.

sentences.zh: 懼帝系之墜緒，故黜昏而崇賢。

translations.literal: Fearing the imperial line would drop its thread, they deposed the benighted and exalted the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the imperial line would snap, they removed the corrupt and honored the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 嘉收功以垂世，嗟在嗣而覆旃。

translations.literal: They praised achievements handed down through generations, yet sighed that the successor overturned the banner.
translations.idiomatic: They celebrated victories meant to last for ages—and mourned how the heir overturned the imperial standard.

sentences.zh: 德非陟而繼宰，釁踰禹其必顛。

translations.literal: Virtue did not ascend to the throne, yet a minister succeeded; calamity exceeded Yu's, and collapse was bound to come.
translations.idiomatic: When virtue did not mount the throne but a regent seized succession, the blow surpassed Yu's flood—and ruin was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 造步丘而長想，欽太傅之遺武。

translations.literal: Arriving at Bu Hill, I fell into long reverie, admiring the Grand Tutor's remaining martial accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: At Buqiu I lingered in deep reflection, honoring the Grand Tutor's living legacy of arms.

sentences.zh: 思嘉遁之餘風，紹素履之落緒。

translations.literal: I pondered the lingering wind of noble reclusion and continued the fallen thread of plain conduct.
translations.idiomatic: I recalled the afterglow of noble withdrawal and took up the frayed thread of simple integrity.

sentences.zh: 民志應而願稅，國屯難而思撫。

translations.literal: The people's will responded, wishing for tax relief; the state in hardship longed for consolation.
translations.idiomatic: The people's hearts answered with longing for relief, while the state in crisis hungered for consoling rule.

sentences.zh: 譬乘舟之待楫，象提釣之假縷。

translations.literal: It is like a boat awaiting its oars, like fishing that relies on thread.
translations.idiomatic: As a boat waits for its oars, as the angler needs his line.

sentences.zh: 揔出入於和就，兼仁用於默語。

translations.literal: In all coming and going he achieved harmony, employing benevolence alike in silence and in speech.
translations.idiomatic: In every public move he sought harmony, wielding benevolence in word and in silence alike.

sentences.zh: 弘九流以拮四維，復先陵而清舊宇。

translations.literal: He spread the nine schools to shore up the four pillars and restored ancestral tombs to clear the old domain.
translations.idiomatic: He enlarged the nine currents of learning to brace the realm's four pillars, and renewed the ancestral graves to purify the old domains.

sentences.zh: 卻西州之成功，指東山之歸予。

translations.literal: He turned from the success at Xizhou and pointed toward Dongshan's return to me.
translations.idiomatic: He renounced the triumph at Xizhou Gate and turned homeward toward Dongshan—as toward myself.

sentences.zh: 惜圖南之啟運，恨鵬翼之未舉。

translations.literal: I grieved that the southward flight had opened the fated course, yet resented the Peng bird's wings still unraised.
translations.idiomatic: I mourned that soaring south had opened the age's fortune, yet grieved that the Peng's wings had never fully spread.

sentences.zh: 發津潭而迥邁，逗白馬以憩舲。

translations.literal: I set out from Jintan on a far, sweeping journey and tarried at White Horse to rest my boat.
translations.idiomatic: From Jintan I pushed far outward, pausing at White Horse to rest my craft.

sentences.zh: 貫射陽而望邗溝，濟通淮而薄甬城。

translations.literal: I pierced through Sheyang and gazed toward Hangou Canal, forded the Tong-Huai River and drew near Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: I passed through Sheyang toward the Hangou Canal, crossed the Tong-Huai, and approached Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 城坡陁兮淮驚波，平原遠兮路交過。

translations.literal: City slopes tumble—Huai's waves in alarm; the plain stretches far—roads crossing and passing.
translations.idiomatic: Tumbling ramparts, and the Huai in wild alarm; endless plain, and paths weaving everywhere.

sentences.zh: 面艽野兮悲橋梓，遡急流兮苦磧沙。

translations.literal: Facing thorn-choked wilds, I grieved for homeland trees; ascending swift currents, I suffered gravel sands.
translations.idiomatic: Before thorny wastes I mourned my native hills; against rushing eddies I wrestled bitter shoals.

sentences.zh: 夐千里而無山，緬百谷而有居。

translations.literal: A thousand li stretched without a mountain; a hundred valleys distant, yet with homes.
translations.idiomatic: For a thousand li no mountain rose; across a hundred valleys, distant dwellings still clustered.

sentences.zh: 被宿莽以迷徑，睹生煙而知墟。

translations.literal: Night-thick weeds cloaked the path in confusion; rising smoke showed where ruins lay.
translations.idiomatic: Old weeds choked the trail; from living smoke I knew an abandoned village near.

sentences.zh: □□□□□□，謂信美其可娛。

translations.literal: [lacuna], claiming that truly its beauty could delight.
translations.idiomatic: The passage is lost, yet I held that its beauty, in truth, could still delight.

sentences.zh: 身少長於樂土，實長歎於荒餘。

translations.literal: From youth I grew on this joyful soil, yet in truth I long sigh over its wasted remains.
translations.idiomatic: I had grown up on this blessed land—yet now could only lament its ruined desolation.

sentences.zh: □□□□具瘁，值歲寒之窮節。

translations.literal: [lacuna], utterly worn, in the season of winter's deepest cold.
translations.idiomatic: The opening line is lost; utterly spent, I faced the year's harshest cold.

sentences.zh: 視層雲之崔巍，聆悲飆之掩屑。

translations.literal: I watched layered clouds rise in towering height and heard the mournful gale scatter its broken cries.
translations.idiomatic: Towering strat clouds rose above; the wailing storm scattered its broken sighs.

sentences.zh: 彌晝夜以滯淫，怨凝陰之方結。

translations.literal: Day and night long, the lingering rain continued; I resented the dark clouds just gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Through day and night the rains hung on; I grieved as the gathered gloom began to knit.

sentences.zh: 望新晴於落日，起明光於躋月。

translations.literal: At the setting sun I hoped for fresh clearing; bright light rose with the ascending moon.
translations.idiomatic: At sunset I looked for clearing skies; bright light answered as the moon climbed.

sentences.zh: 眷轉蓬之辭根，悼朔雁之赴越。

translations.literal: I cherished the tumbleweed torn from its root and mourned the wild geese flying south to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: I grieved like tumbleweed ripped from its root, mourning wild geese bound for the southern wilds.

sentences.zh: 披微物而疚情，此思心其可說。

translations.literal: Moved by humble things, my heart ached; how could such longing be told?
translations.idiomatic: Humble sights pierced me with grief—what words could ease a heart such as this?

sentences.zh: 問傜役其幾時，駭閱景於興沒。

translations.literal: I asked how long the corvee would last and shuddered to watch the days rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: I asked how long forced service would run—and trembled watching days flare up and die.

sentences.zh: 感曰歸於《采薇》，子來思於雨雪。

translations.literal: I felt the 'we must return' of 'Gathering Ferns' and the 'sons will come' longing through rain and snow.
translations.idiomatic: I felt the Wei Poems' cry—'We must return'—and that old hope where sons would come through rain and snow.

sentences.zh: 豈初征之懼對，冀鸛鳴之在垤。

translations.literal: Was it not the first march's dread of the enemy facing me? I hoped for the stork's cry upon the anthill.
translations.idiomatic: Was this not the dread of a first campaign—and the hope of storks calling from the anthills, signalling return?

sentences.zh: □□□□踰宿，騖吾楫於邳鄉。

translations.literal: [lacuna], past one night's lodging, I drove my oars toward Pi village.
translations.idiomatic: After a night's stay—where the prior line is lost—I urged my boat toward Pi township.

sentences.zh: 奚車正以事夏，虺左相以輔湯。

translations.literal: Xi Chezheng served Xia in his ministry; Hui as left minister aided Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chezheng served Xia in office; Yi Yin as chief minister steered Tang to power.

sentences.zh: 綿三代而享邑，廁踐土之一匡。

translations.literal: For three generations they held their fief, taking part in the Jiantu enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations held their fief, sharing in the lords' enfeoffment at Jiantu.

sentences.zh: 嗟仲幾之寵侮，遂捨存以徵亡。

translations.literal: I sighed over Zhong Ji's pampered arrogance and how he traded survival for ruin.
translations.idiomatic: I lamented Zhong Ji's spoiled contempt—and how he chose ruin over survival.

sentences.zh: 喜薛宰之善對，美士彌之能綱。

translations.literal: I rejoiced in the district magistrate of Xue's apt reply and praised Shi Mi's power to hold the realm together.
translations.idiomatic: I admired the magistrate of Xue's wise answer—and Shi Mi's gift for holding all in order.

sentences.zh: 升曲垣之逶迤，訪淮陰之所都。

translations.literal: I climbed the winding curved ramparts and visited the seat of Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: I climbed winding walls and sought the old seat of Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 原入跨之達恥，俟遭時以遠圖。

translations.literal: Reflecting on Kuaixia's well-known shame, he waited for his time to pursue a far-reaching design.
translations.idiomatic: He understood the humiliation of passing under a stranger's legs—and waited his season for grand ambition.

sentences.zh: 捨西楚以擇木，迨南漢以定謨。

translations.literal: He abandoned Western Chu to choose the better perch and reached Southern Han to fix his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He forsook Western Chu for a better foothold and joined Southern Han to shape the realm's design.

sentences.zh: 亂孟津而魏滅，攀井陘而趙徂。

translations.literal: At Mengjin ford he threw Wei into chaos and brought its ruin; at Jingxing Pass he scaled the heights and Zhao perished.
translations.idiomatic: At Mengjin he routed Wei; at Jingxing he scaled the heights and Zhao fell.

sentences.zh: 播靈威於齊橫，振餘猛於龍且。

translations.literal: He spread his numinous might over Qi and Heng and shook his remaining fury through Long Ju.
translations.idiomatic: His mystic awe ran through Qi and Tian Heng; his last thunder shook Long Ju from the field.

sentences.zh: 觀讓通而告豨，曷始智而終愚。

translations.literal: Seeing Rang Tong and warning Chen Xi—why was he wise at first yet foolish at the end?
translations.idiomatic: He saw Rang Tong and warned of Chen Xi's revolt—yet why wise at the start and foolish at the end?

sentences.zh: 迄沂上而停枻，登高圯而不進。

translations.literal: I reached the Yi River's banks and stopped my oars; I climbed the Gaotai Bridge and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yi River I dropped my oars; at Gaotai Bridge I halted and would not go on.

sentences.zh: 石幽期而知賢，張揣景而示信。

translations.literal: The Old Man of the Yellow Stone set a secret tryst, knowing the worthy man; Zhang measured the moment and showed his faith.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Stone laid a hidden tryst, discerning true worth; Zhang Liang read the scene and proved his trust.

sentences.zh: 本文成之素心，要王子於雲仞。

translations.literal: With the plain heart of one who accomplishes his craft, he sought the princely lord at cloud's edge.
translations.idiomatic: True to his original heart as a man of letters, he sought the prince amid the clouded heights.

sentences.zh: 豈無累於清霄，直有槩於貞吝。

translations.literal: Was he not burdened in the clear heavens? He bore only indignation at stubborn parsimony.
translations.idiomatic: Could one be free of worldly tethers in the high heavens? He held only righteous scorn for mean constraint.

sentences.zh: 始熙績於武關，卒敷功於皇胤。

translations.literal: At first he gloried in merit at Wuguan Pass; at last he spread his achievements among the imperial heirs.
translations.idiomatic: He first won glory at Wuguan Pass and at last extended his service to the imperial line.

sentences.zh: 處夷險以解挫，弘憂虞以時順。

translations.literal: In ease and peril alike he resolved defeat; in care and worry he enlarged timely compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Through hardship and ease he turned defeat aside; in anxiety he bent with the season's demands.

sentences.zh: 矜、華之翳晷，哀飛驂之落駿。

translations.literal: The shadowed brilliance of Jing and Hua; I mourned the fallen chargers of the flying team.
translations.idiomatic: Splendor dimmed for Jing and Hua; I mourned the swift horses fallen from the flying chariot.

sentences.zh: 傷粒食而興念，眷逸翮而思振。

translations.literal: Grieving for grain moved him to think; cherishing soaring pinions, he longed to shake free and rise.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the people's hunger for grain, he yearned to serve; cherishing wings at rest, he longed to beat heavenward.

sentences.zh: 戾臣山而東顧，美相公之前代。

translations.literal: Turning at Chen Mountain I looked east and praised the Prime Minister's earlier age.
translations.idiomatic: From Chen Mountain I turned east, honoring the Prime Minister's forebears.

sentences.zh: 嗟殘虜之將糜，熾餘猋於海濟。

translations.literal: I sighed that remnant enemies were about to crumble, yet fierce winds still blazed along the sea coast.
translations.idiomatic: I mourned how broken foes were nearly spent—yet their last rage still burned along the northern coast.

sentences.zh: 驅鮐稚於淮曲，暴鰥孤於泗澨。

translations.literal: They drove young sturgeon from the Huai's bend and left widowers and orphans exposed on the Si's shore.
translations.idiomatic: They harried the helpless along the Huai's curve and abandoned widows and orphans on the Si's banks.

sentences.zh: 託未命□□雲，冀靈武之北閱。

translations.literal: Entrusting the final charge [lacuna] cloud, he hoped for northern review at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted the late mandate [lacuna] upon the clouds, hoping for imperial review in the north at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 惟授首之在晨，當盛暑而選徒。

translations.literal: Only at dawn would heads be surrendered; in midsummer heat he mustered the host.
translations.idiomatic: Surrender would come only at dawn—and in scorching summer he still chose his marching men.

sentences.zh: 肅嚴威以振響，漸溫澤而沾腴。

translations.literal: With solemn awe he raised a thunderous cry; with warming grace he slowly soaked the fertile soil.
translations.idiomatic: Stern awe thundered forth; then gentle warmth slowly steeped the rich earth.

sentences.zh: 既雲撤於朐城，遂席捲於齊都。

translations.literal: Already like clouds clearing from Jucheng, then sweeping through the Qi capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jucheng fell as swiftly as clouds parting; then the army rolled through the Qi capital.

sentences.zh: 曩四關其奚阻，道一變而是孚。

translations.literal: Formerly what did the four passes obstruct? The Way changed once and there was good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Once the four frontier passes had barred all advance—what could still stand in the way? One turn of fortune, and loyal trust was secured.

sentences.zh: 傷炎季之崩弛，長逆布以滔天。

translations.literal: Grieving the flaming dynasty's collapse and laxity, rebels spread far and overflowed heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I grieved the Han dynasty's final collapse and decay, as rebellion spread on and on until it seemed to flood the heavens.

sentences.zh: 假父子以詐愛，借兄弟以偽恩。

translations.literal: Feigning father-and-son love through deceit, borrowing brotherhood for false kindness.
translations.idiomatic: They feigned father-and-son devotion through fraud and borrowed the language of brotherhood to mask false grace.

sentences.zh: 相魏武以譎狂，宄謨奮於東藩。

translations.literal: Matching Cao Cao in crafty madness, treacherous schemes stirred in the eastern marches.
translations.idiomatic: Rivaling Cao Cao in cunning and arrogance, conspirators roused treason in the eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 桴未譟於東郭，身已馘於樓門。

translations.literal: Before the drum had yet clamored at the eastern suburb, the body was already decapitated at the tower gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before war drums could even sound at the eastern wall, the foe's head was already taken at the tower gate.

sentences.zh: 審貢牧於前說，證所作於舊徐。

translations.literal: Examining tribute and pasturing in earlier accounts, verifying what was done in old Xu.
translations.idiomatic: I reviewed earlier records of tribute and frontier governance and tested them against what I had seen in old Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 聆泗川之浮磬，翫夷水之蠙珠。

translations.literal: Listening to the floating stone chimes of the Si River, admiring the pearl oysters of the Yi River.
translations.idiomatic: I listened for the floating stone chimes along the Si and admired the pearl-bearing waters of the Yi.

sentences.zh: 草漸苞於熾壤，桐孤幹於嶧隅。

translations.literal: Grass gradually encased the scorched soil; a paulownia stood alone with its trunk at the corner of Mount Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Grass slowly reclaimed the burned earth, while a lone paulownia rose from the slopes of Mount Yi.

sentences.zh: 慨禹跡於尚世，惠遺文於《夏書》。

translations.literal: Moved by Yu's traces in high antiquity, grateful for the legacy text in the Documents of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: I was moved by the traces of Yu the Great in ages past and grateful for the surviving text preserved in the Documents of Xia.

sentences.zh: 紛征邁之淹留，彌懷古於舊章。

translations.literal: Amid varied expeditions and lingering journeys, ever more cherishing antiquity in old records.
translations.idiomatic: Through long campaigns and lingering delays, my longing for the past in ancient records only grew.

sentences.zh: 商伯文於故服，咸徵名於彭、殤。

translations.literal: Reflecting on Bo Wen in the old domain, all seeking renown through Peng and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: I pondered Bo Wen in his former fief, where all alike sought fame at Peng and Shang.

sentences.zh: 眺靈壁之曾峰，投呂縣之迅梁。

translations.literal: Gazing at the layered peaks of Lingbi, casting myself upon the swift bridge of Lü County.
translations.idiomatic: I looked out on the towering peaks of Lingbi and crossed the rushing bridge at Lü County.

sentences.zh: 想蹈水之行歌，雖齊汩其何傷。

translations.literal: Recalling the song of treading water, though swept along in the torrent what harm?
translations.idiomatic: I recalled the song sung while fording the waters—though swept along in the flood, what injury could that bring?

sentences.zh: 啟仲尼之嘉問，告性命以依方。

translations.literal: Opening Confucius's fine inquiry, telling of fate and life according to the proper Way.
translations.idiomatic: I opened Confucius's noble questioning and spoke of destiny and life in accord with the Way.

sentences.zh: 豈苟然於迂論，聆寓言於達莊。

translations.literal: How could one casually accept pedantic discourse? Listening to parables in the penetrating Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: How could one rest content with hollow pedantry? I listened instead to the allegories of Zhuangzi, master of insight.

sentences.zh: 於是濫石橋，登戲臺。

translations.literal: Then fording Lanshi Bridge, ascending Play Platform.
translations.idiomatic: Then I crossed Lanshi Bridge and climbed Play Platform.

sentences.zh: 策馬釣渚，息轡城隅。

translations.literal: Urging horses to the fishing islet, resting the reins at the city corner.
translations.idiomatic: I spurred my horse to the fishing shoal and drew rein at the corner of the city wall.

sentences.zh: 永感四山，零淚雙渠。

translations.literal: Ever moved by the four mountains, shedding tears at the twin canals.
translations.idiomatic: Forever stirred by the four surrounding mountains, I shed tears beside the twin canals.

sentences.zh: 怨物華之推驛，慨舟壑之遞遷。

translations.literal: Lamenting that nature's splendor passes like a relay post, sighing that valleys become rivers in turn.
translations.idiomatic: I lamented how the glory of things races past like a relay station and sighed that valleys in time become rivers.

sentences.zh: 謂徂歲之悠闊，結幽思之方根。

translations.literal: Saying the departing years are vast and long, forming deep thoughts rooted firm.
translations.idiomatic: The years that have gone seem boundless; deep thoughts took root and would not loosen.

sentences.zh: 感皇祖之徽德，爰識沖而量淵。

translations.literal: Moved by the imperial ancestor's fine virtue, thus measuring profundity with humility.
translations.idiomatic: Touched by the imperial ancestor's luminous virtue, I sought to measure the depths with a humble heart.

sentences.zh: 降俊明以鏡鑒，回風猷以昭宣。

translations.literal: Bestowing talent and brilliance as a mirror for reflection, turning wind-like policies to shine and proclaim.
translations.idiomatic: He sent down the wise and bright as mirrors for the age and turned his policies to the wind, making them shine abroad.

sentences.zh: 道既底於國難，惠有覃於黎元。

translations.literal: The Way having reached the bottom of national crisis, grace has spread broadly among the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Way had touched the depths of national peril, his grace spread far among the common people.

sentences.zh: 士頌歌於政教，民謠詠於渥恩。

translations.literal: Scholars sing praises of governance and education; the people chant ballads of rich favor.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars sang the praises of his rule and teaching, and the people voiced songs of his generous grace.

sentences.zh: 兼《采芑》之致美，協《漢廣》之發言。

translations.literal: Combining the beauty of "Gathering Millet," harmonizing with the expressions of "Han Broad."
translations.idiomatic: His reign matched the beauty praised in "Gathering Millet" and echoed the voice of "Broad Han."

sentences.zh: 彊虎氐之搏翼，灟雲網於所禁。

translations.literal: The Qiang, Hu, and Di tribes spreading wings, casting cloud-like nets where forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang, Hu, and Di spread their wings in rebellion, casting cloud-dark nets over the forbidden lands.

sentences.zh: 驅黔萌以蘊崇，取園陵而湮沈。

translations.literal: Driving the common people into accumulated misery, seizing imperial gardens and tombs to submerge and destroy.
translations.idiomatic: They drove the common people into mounting misery, seized imperial parks and tombs, and buried them in ruin.

sentences.zh: 錫殘落於河西，序淪胥於漢陰。

translations.literal: Granting scattered remnants in Hexi, arraying ruin in the south of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors were cast off to wither in Hexi, and ruin was ordered across the lands south of the Han.

sentences.zh: 攻方城而折扃，擾譙潁其誰任。

translations.literal: Attacking Fangcheng and breaking the bolt, disturbing Qiao and Ying—who could bear the burden?
translations.idiomatic: They struck Fangcheng and broke its gate-bolts; chaos engulfed Qiao and Ying—who could answer for it?

sentences.zh: 世闕才而貽亂，時得賢而興治。
