translations.literal: Ages lacking talent bequeath chaos; times gaining worthy men give rise to good governance.
translations.idiomatic: When an age lacks talent it inherits disorder; when the times gain worthy men, good order rises.

sentences.zh: 救祖考之邦壤，在幽人而枉志。

translations.literal: Saving the ancestral homeland lay with recluses who bent their wills.
translations.idiomatic: Salvation for the ancestral domain rested with recluses who bent their ambitions to the task.

sentences.zh: 體飛書之遠情，悟犒師之通識。

translations.literal: Embodying the distant sentiment of flying letters, comprehending the universal insight of rewarding troops.
translations.idiomatic: I entered the far-reaching feeling of letters sent on the wing and grasped the broad wisdom of rewarding the army.

sentences.zh: 迨明達之高覽，契古今而同事。

translations.literal: Awaiting the far-sighted view of the enlightened, matching ancient and modern in common cause.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting the lofty vision of the enlightened ruler, past and present were joined in a single purpose.

sentences.zh: 拔淵謨於潛機，騁神鋒於雲斾。

translations.literal: Drawing deep schemes from hidden opportunity, unleashing divine sharpness on cloud banners.
translations.idiomatic: He drew profound stratagems from hidden opportunity and unleashed his spirit's edge beneath cloud-dark banners.

sentences.zh: 驅斥澤而風靡，蹙坑谷而鳥竄。

translations.literal: Driving through marshes like wind sweeping, pressing into ravines where birds flee cowering.
translations.idiomatic: He swept the marshes as the wind sweeps all before it and pressed into ravines until birds scattered in terror.

sentences.zh: 中華免夫左衽，江表此焉緩帶。

translations.literal: The Chinese heartland was spared the left lapel; south of the Yangtze here one could loosen the belt.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland was spared barbarian dress; here south of the Yangtze men could at last loosen their belts in peace.

sentences.zh: 既克黜於肥六，又作鎮於彭沛。

translations.literal: Having subdued Fei and Lu, then establishing a garrison at Peng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Having subdued Fei and Lu, he then established his stronghold at Pengcheng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 晏皇塗於國內，震天威於河外。

translations.literal: Pacifying the imperial roads within the realm, shaking heaven's majesty beyond the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He brought peace to the imperial highways within the realm and shook heaven's majesty beyond the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 掃東齊而已寧，指西崤而將泰。

translations.literal: Sweeping Eastern Qi already to peace, pointing west to Xiao Pass soon to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: He swept Eastern Qi into calm and turned west toward Xiao Pass, where peace was soon to come.

sentences.zh: 值秉均而代謝，實大業之興廢。

translations.literal: Encountering the change of those holding balance, truly the rise and fall of great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: When power passed from one balanced hand to another, the rise and fall of a great enterprise was truly revealed.

sentences.zh: 心無忝於樂生，事有像於燕惠。

translations.literal: The heart without shame before Yue Yi, affairs resembling King Hui of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His heart was unashamed before Yue Yi, yet his affairs recalled King Hui of Yan.

sentences.zh: 抱明哲之不伐，奉宏勳而是稅。

translations.literal: Embracing wisdom without boasting, accepting great merit and thus withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: He held to wisdom without self-praise, offered up his great achievements, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 捐七州以爰來，歸五湖以投袂。

translations.literal: Relinquishing seven provinces and coming hither, returning to the Five Lakes to fling one's sleeves in resolve.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered seven provinces and came here, then returned to the Five Lakes and cast aside his sleeves in departure.

sentences.zh: 屈盛績於平生，申遠期於暮歲。

translations.literal: Submitting great achievements across a lifetime, extending far-reaching plans into old age.
translations.idiomatic: Great deeds were constrained within a single lifetime, yet far-reaching hopes were pressed into his later years.

sentences.zh: 訪曩載於宋鄙，採《陽秋》於魯經。

translations.literal: Visiting past records in Song's outer territories, gathering the Spring and Autumn from Lu's classic.
translations.idiomatic: I sought past records in the borderlands of Song and drew the Spring and Autumn from the classic of Lu.

sentences.zh: 晉申好於東吳，鄭憑威於南荊。

translations.literal: Jin at Shen established friendship with Eastern Wu; Zheng relied on might in southern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin made alliance with Eastern Wu at Shen; Zheng leaned on power in southern Jing.

sentences.zh: 故反師於曹門，將以塞於夷庚。

translations.literal: Therefore turning the army back at Cao Gate, intending to block at Yigeng.
translations.idiomatic: So the army was turned back at Cao Gate, intending to seal the pass at Yigeng.

sentences.zh: 納五叛以長寇，伐三邑以侵彭。

translations.literal: Harbor five turncoats thus lengthening the raiding, attacking three cities to invade Peng.
translations.idiomatic: They harbored five defectors and so prolonged the raids, then attacked three towns to threaten Peng.

sentences.zh: 美西鋤之忠辭，快韓厥之奇兵。

translations.literal: Admiring Xi Chu's loyal remonstrance, delighting in Han Jue's brilliant troops.
translations.idiomatic: I admired the loyal remonstrance of Xi Chu and rejoiced in the surprise force of Han Jue.

sentences.zh: 追項王之故臺，跡霸楚之遺端。

translations.literal: Pursuing the old terrace of King Xiang, tracing the remnant traces of hegemonic Chu.
translations.idiomatic: I followed the old terrace of Xiang Yu and traced the lingering traces of Chu's hegemony.

sentences.zh: 挺宏志於總角，奮英勢於弱冠。

translations.literal: Raising a grand aspiration in the hair-tied years of youth, stirring heroic momentum at the weak-crown age.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he nursed a grand ambition; at twenty he unleashed heroic vigor.

sentences.zh: 氣蓋天而倒日，力拔山而傾湍。

translations.literal: His spirit covered heaven and overturned the sun; his strength uprooted mountains and overturned rapids.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit towered over heaven and seemed to turn back the sun; his strength could uproot mountains and topple rushing waters.

sentences.zh: 始飆起於勾越，中電激於衡關。

translations.literal: First a whirlwind rose from Gou and Yue; midway lightning struck at Heng Pass.
translations.idiomatic: First he rose like a storm wind from Gou and Yue; midway he flashed like lightning at Heng Pass.

sentences.zh: 興偏慮於攸吝，忘即易於所難。

translations.literal: Partial anxieties arose over narrow scruples; he forgot that ease lay within what was hard.
translations.idiomatic: Partial anxieties arose over trifling scruples, while he forgot that the difficult could become easy.

sentences.zh: 忌陳錦而莫照，思反鄉而有歎。

translations.literal: Jealousy kept displayed brocade from shining; thoughts of returning home brought sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Envy kept fine brocades from shining; thoughts of returning home drew only sighs.

sentences.zh: 且夫殺義害嬰，而[忄戛]豐疑，緤賢不策，失位誰持。

translations.literal: Moreover, he killed Emperor Yi and harmed the innocent, yet [lacuna] bred suspicion toward Feng; he bound worthy men without employing strategy—when the throne was lost, who would uphold it?
translations.idiomatic: He killed Emperor Yi and harmed the innocent, yet [lacuna] bred suspicion toward Feng; he restrained talented men without strategy—once his position was lost, who could hold it for him?

sentences.zh: 迨理屈而愈閉，方怨天而懷悲。

translations.literal: When his cause was exhausted he closed himself in all the more; then he blamed Heaven and harbored grief.
translations.idiomatic: When his cause was exhausted he shut himself in ever more tightly; then he blamed Heaven and nursed his grief.

sentences.zh: 對駿騅以發憤，傷虞姝於末詞。

translations.literal: Facing his splendid black steed he vented his fury; in his final words he grieved for Yu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Before his fine black steed he poured out his fury; in his last words he grieved for Yu Ji.

sentences.zh: 陟亞父之故營，諒謀始之非託。

translations.literal: Ascending the old camp of the Chief Minister, I realized that the opening plan had never rested on true trust.
translations.idiomatic: Climbing to the old camp of Fan Zeng, I realized the opening strategy had never rested on true trust.

sentences.zh: 遭衰嬴之崩綱，值威炎之結絡。

translations.literal: He rose when declining Ying's bonds were collapsing, and met powerful Han when its ties were coalescing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose when Qin was debilitated and its bonds collapsing, and met the Han when its power was coalescing.

sentences.zh: 迄皓首於阜陵，猶謬覺於然諾。

translations.literal: Even unto white-haired age at Fuling, he still mistakenly believed in the weight of sworn promises.
translations.idiomatic: Even to white-haired age at Fuling, he still wrongly believed in the weight of a sworn promise.

sentences.zh: 視一人於三傑，豈在己之庸弱。

translations.literal: To set one man against the Three Heroes—was the fault truly in his own feebleness?
translations.idiomatic: To place one man against the Three Heroes—surely the fault lay not in his own weakness.

sentences.zh: 置豐沛而不舉，故自同於俎鑊。

translations.literal: He left Feng and Pei unseized, and so made himself no better than meat on the block and in the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: He left Feng and Pei unseized, and so made himself no better than meat on the block and in the cauldron.

sentences.zh: 發卞口而遊歷，迄西山而弭轡。

translations.literal: Setting out from Biankou to travel, reaching Western Hills and reining in the horses.
translations.idiomatic: I departed from Biankou to journey forth and, at Western Hills, drew up my reins.

sentences.zh: 觀終古之幽憤，懷元王之沖粹。

translations.literal: Observing the hidden grief of ages past, cherishing the pure simplicity of Prince Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: I contemplated the hidden grief of ages past and recalled the serene purity of Prince Yuan.

sentences.zh: 丁戰國之權爭，方恬心於道肆。

translations.literal: Amid the power struggles of the Warring States, he found peace of mind in the halls of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the power struggles of the Warring States he found his heart at ease in the halls of the Way.

sentences.zh: 學浮丘以就德，友三儒以成類。

translations.literal: Studying with Fuqiu to attain virtue, befriending three scholars to form a fellowship.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with Fuqiu to cultivate virtue and joined three scholars to form a circle of like minds.

sentences.zh: 潔流始於初源，累仁基於前美。

translations.literal: Pure streams begin at the earliest source; accumulated benevolence rests on earlier excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Clear water springs from its first source; accumulated benevolence rests on earlier virtue.

sentences.zh: 撥楚族之休烈，傳芳素於來祀。

translations.literal: Drawing forth the glorious achievements of the Chu lineage, transmitting pure fragrance to future sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He drew out the splendid legacy of the Chu house and passed its untainted fame to generations yet to come.

sentences.zh: 彊見譽於清虛，德致稱於千里。

translations.literal: He was praised for clarity and emptiness; his virtue won acclaim a thousand li around.
translations.idiomatic: He won praise for his purity and detachment, and his virtue was celebrated far and wide.

sentences.zh: 或避寵以辭姻，或遺榮而不仕。

translations.literal: Some shunned favor to decline marriage alliance; some left glory and would not serve.
translations.idiomatic: Some rejected favor to avoid marriage ties; others abandoned glory and refused office.

sentences.zh: 政直言以安身，駿絕才以喪己。

translations.literal: Zheng kept himself safe through blunt honesty; Jun's surpassing talent cost him his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng kept himself safe through blunt honesty; Jun's surpassing talent cost him his life.

sentences.zh: 驅通道之成終，表昧世之虧始。

translations.literal: It drives home how the thoroughfare reaches its end, revealing where a benighted age first went wrong.
translations.idiomatic: It drives home how the thoroughfare reaches its end, revealing where a benighted age first went wrong.

sentences.zh: 悟介焉之已差，則不俟於終日。

translations.literal: Once one sees that the slightest lapse is already amiss, one need not wait until the day's end.
translations.idiomatic: Once one sees that the slightest lapse is already amiss, one need not wait out the whole day.

sentences.zh: 既防萌於未著，雖念德其何益。

translations.literal: Even if evil is checked before it appears, remembering past virtue is of little avail.
translations.idiomatic: Even if evil is checked before it shows, remembering past virtue is of little avail.

sentences.zh: 爾乃孟陬發節，雷隱蟄驚。

translations.literal: Then in early spring the season unfolded; hidden thunder startled the hibernating creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Then came early spring, when the season opened and hidden thunder shook the creatures from their sleep.

sentences.zh: 散葉荑柯，芳蘤飾萌。

translations.literal: Leaves unfolded on tender shoots; fragrant blossoms trimmed the newborn buds.
translations.idiomatic: Leaves unfolded on tender branches; fragrant blossoms trimmed the newborn buds.

sentences.zh: 麥萋萋於旄丘，柳依依於高城。

translations.literal: Wheat grew lush on Mao Hill; willows trailed gently along the high city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Wheat grew lush on Mao Hill; willows trailed gently along the high city walls.

sentences.zh: 相雎鳩之集河，觀鳴鹿之食苹。

translations.literal: Observing ospreys gathering by the river, watching calling deer eating duckweed.
translations.idiomatic: I watched ospreys gather by the river and saw calling deer feeding on the marsh plants.

sentences.zh: 沂泗遠兮清川急，秋冬近兮緒風襲。

translations.literal: Yi and Si lay far behind as clear streams rushed on; autumn and winter drew near as remnant winds struck.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Si lay far behind as clear streams rushed on; autumn and winter drew near as remnant winds struck.

sentences.zh: 風流蕙兮水增瀾，訴愁衿兮鑒戚顏。

translations.literal: Wind rippled through orchids and the water rose in waves; grief spoke from my collar, mirrored in a sorrowful face.
translations.idiomatic: Wind rippled through orchids and the water rose in waves; grief spoke from my collar, mirrored in a sorrowful face.

sentences.zh: 愁盈根而蕰際，戚發條而成端。

translations.literal: Sorrow filled the roots and gathered at the border; grief rose from branch tips to its full term.
translations.idiomatic: Sorrow filled the roots and gathered at the border; grief rose from branch tips to its full term.

sentences.zh: 嗟我行之彌日，待征邁而言旋。

translations.literal: Alas, my journey lengthens with each passing day; I wait for the campaign to advance so I may speak of going home.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, my journey lengthens with each passing day; I wait for the campaign to advance so I may speak of going home.

sentences.zh: 荷慶雲之優渥，周雙七於此年。

translations.literal: I was blessed with the abundant favor of auspicious clouds and marked a double seventh in this year.
translations.idiomatic: I was blessed with the abundant favor of auspicious clouds and marked a double seventh in this year.

sentences.zh: 陶逸豫於京甸，違險難於行川。

translations.literal: I had tasted ease and pleasure in the capital district, yet still faced danger and hardship on the river road.
translations.idiomatic: I had tasted ease and pleasure in the capital district, yet still faced danger and hardship on the river road.

sentences.zh: 轉歸弦而眷戀，望脩檣而流漣。

translations.literal: As the homeward moon turned I lingered in longing, gazing at the tall masts until tears flowed.
translations.idiomatic: As the homeward moon turned I lingered in longing, gazing at the tall masts until tears flowed.

sentences.zh: 願關鄴之遄清，遲華鑾之凱旋。

translations.literal: I prayed that the passes and Ye would soon be cleared, and awaited the imperial carriage's triumphant return.
translations.idiomatic: I prayed that the passes and Ye would soon be cleared, and awaited the imperial carriage's triumphant return.

sentences.zh: 穆淳風於六合，溥洪澤於八埏。

translations.literal: May pure customs prevail throughout the six directions and great bounty spread across the eight boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: May pure customs prevail throughout the realm and great bounty spread to every corner of the land.

sentences.zh: 頒賢愚於大小，順規矩於方圓。

translations.literal: May sage and simple each find their place, great and small, and square and circle accord with their measure.
translations.idiomatic: May sage and simple each find their place, great and small, and square and circle accord with their measure.

sentences.zh: 固四民之獲所，宜稅稷於萊田。

translations.literal: Surely the four classes will each have their rightful place; it is meet to reap millet from the border fields.
translations.idiomatic: Surely the four classes will each have their rightful place, and it is meet to reap millet from the border fields.

sentences.zh: 苦邯鄲之難步，庶行迷之易痊。

translations.literal: Though I suffer the awkward gait learned at Handan, perhaps a wandering path may yet be set right.
translations.idiomatic: Though I suffer the awkward gait learned at Handan, perhaps a wandering path may yet be set right.

sentences.zh: 長守樸以終稔，亦拙者之政焉。

translations.literal: To long hold to simplicity until the harvest is complete—that too is the policy of the plain man.
translations.idiomatic: To long hold to simplicity until the harvest is complete—that is the way of the plain man as well.

sentences.zh: 靈運父祖竝葬始寧縣，并有故宅及墅，遂移籍會稽，脩營別業，傍山帶江，盡幽居之美。

translations.literal: Lingyun's father and grandfather were both buried in Shining County, and there were old residences and villas; he then moved his registration to Kuaiji, built and managed a separate estate beside mountains and girdled by rivers, embodying all the beauty of secluded dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun's father and grandfather were both buried in Shining County, and old homes and villas remained there; he moved his household registration to Kuaiji, built a separate estate nestled against mountains and beside rivers, and enjoyed all the splendor of a secluded life.

sentences.zh: 與隱士王弘之、孔淳之等縱放為娛，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: With the recluses Wang Hongzhi, Kong Chunzhi, and others he roamed freely for amusement, having the resolve to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: With the recluses Wang Hongzhi, Kong Chunzhi, and others he roamed freely for pleasure, resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 每有一詩至都邑，貴賤莫不競寫，宿昔之間，士庶皆徧，遠近欽慕，名動京師。

translations.literal: Whenever a poem of his reached the capital, nobles and commoners alike competed to copy it; within a night, gentry and townsfolk all had it; near and far admired him, and fame shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever one of his poems reached the capital, high and low competed to copy it; within a single night it spread among scholars and commoners alike; admiration poured in from far and near, and his fame shook the capital.

sentences.zh: 作《山居賦》并自注，以言其事。

translations.literal: He composed "Rhapsody on Mountain Dwelling" together with self-annotation, to speak of these matters.
translations.idiomatic: He composed "Rhapsody on Mountain Dwelling" with his own annotations to set forth these things.

sentences.zh: 曰：

translations.literal: It says:
translations.idiomatic: It says:

sentences.zh: 古巢居穴處曰岩棲，棟宇居山曰山居，在林野曰丘園，在郊郭曰城傍，四者不同，可以理推。

translations.literal: In antiquity, dwelling in nests and caves was called cliff dwelling; building houses on mountains was called mountain dwelling; life in forests and wilds was called hill-and-garden; life in outer suburbs was called dwelling beside a city—the four are not the same, yet their logic can be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, dwelling in nests and caves was called cliff dwelling; building houses on mountains was called mountain dwelling; life in forests and wilds was called hill-and-garden; life in outer suburbs was called dwelling beside a city—the four are not the same, yet their logic can be inferred.

sentences.zh: 言心也，黃屋實不殊於汾陽；

translations.literal: As for the heart, the yellow-canopied throne is in truth no different from Fenyang.
translations.idiomatic: As for the heart, the imperial throne is in truth no different from life at Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 即事也，山居良有異乎市廛。

translations.literal: As for affairs, mountain dwelling is indeed quite different from the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In outward circumstance, life in the mountains is truly unlike the bustle of the market town.

sentences.zh: 抱疾就閑，順從性情，敢率所樂，而以作賦。

translations.literal: Ill, I sought leisure; following my temperament, I dare to lead with what I delight in and compose this rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: Ailing, I turned to quiet ease; true to my nature, I venture to speak from what I love and write this rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 揚子雲云：「詩人之賦麗以則。」

translations.literal: Yang Ziyun said: "The poet's rhapsody is beautiful yet within measure."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong said: "The poet's fu is splendid yet governed by rule."

sentences.zh: 文體宜兼，以成其美。

translations.literal: Literary form should combine both, to achieve its beauty.
translations.idiomatic: The style of writing should embrace both qualities to realize its full beauty.

sentences.zh: 今所賦既非京都宮觀、遊獵聲色之盛，而敘山野草木、水石穀稼之事，才乏昔人，心放俗外，詠於文則可勉而就之，求麗邈以遠矣。

translations.literal: What I rhapsodize now is neither the splendor of capital palaces and towers nor hunting, music, and sensual display, but recounts wild mountains, grasses and trees, water and stone, grain and crops. My talent falls short of the ancients; my heart drifts beyond the vulgar world—in verse I may strive to manage it, but to seek ornate beauty is far beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: This rhapsody treats neither the grandeur of the capital's palaces and towers nor the pomp of hunts, music, and pleasure, but the grasses and trees, streams and stones, and grain of the wild hills. My gift is less than the masters of old; my mind lives outside worldly affairs. I can perhaps manage plain song in words, but to pursue resplendent ornament lies far beyond me.

sentences.zh: 覽者廢張、左之豔辭，尋臺、皓之深意，去飾取素，儻值其心耳。

translations.literal: Let readers discard the gorgeous language of Zhang and Zuo, seek the deep meaning of Tai and the Four Elders, remove ornament and take simplicity—perhaps then they will meet its heart.
translations.idiomatic: I ask my readers to put aside the sumptuous phrasing of Zhang Heng and Zuo Si, and to seek instead the profound spirit of Tai Xiaowei and the Four White-haired Elders of Shangshan—to strip ornament and embrace plainness, if perchance they can meet this work in its true intent.

sentences.zh: 意實言表，而書不盡，遺跡索意，託之有賞。

translations.literal: The meaning is truly what words express, yet writing cannot exhaust it; by traces left behind one seeks the meaning—I entrust appreciation to those who can receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Meaning dwells in words, yet no writing can fully contain it; one must trace what remains and search out the intent—I leave the reward of understanding to those who can receive it.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: 謝子臥疾山頂，覽古人遺書，與其意合，悠然而笑曰：夫道可重，故物為輕；

translations.literal: Master Xie, ill, rested atop the mountain, perused the surviving books of the ancients, found his mind in accord with them, and smiled leisurely, saying: "The Way may be honored, therefore things are light;
translations.idiomatic: Xie, ailing on the mountain summit, read the books the ancients had left behind and found his own thoughts in harmony with theirs. At ease he smiled and said: "When the Way is held weighty, worldly things grow light;

sentences.zh: 理宜存，故事斯忘。

translations.literal: principle should endure, therefore affairs are then forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: when principle is preserved, mundane affairs fall away."

sentences.zh: 古今不能革，質文咸其常。

translations.literal: Past and present cannot be altered; substance and ornament each have their constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: Past and present cannot be changed; plainness and ornament each keep their proper place.

sentences.zh: 合宮非縉雲之館，衢室豈放勳之堂。

translations.literal: The Grand Palace was not the lodge at Jinyun; the Crossroads Hall was not the hall of Fangxun.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Palace was no dwelling at Cloud-Girded Peak; the Crossroads Chamber was no hall of the Radiant Merit.

sentences.zh: 邁深心於鼎湖，送高情於汾陽。

translations.literal: One moved his deep heart to Ding Lake; one sent his lofty feeling to Fen Yang.
translations.idiomatic: The deep heart went onward to Ding Lake; the lofty spirit was given over to Fen Yang.

sentences.zh: 嗟文成之卻粒，願追松以遠遊。

translations.literal: I sighed at Wencheng's abstention from grain, wishing to follow the pine and wander far.
translations.idiomatic: I marvel at Lord Wen's renunciation of grain, yearning to follow the pine immortal on a distant journey.

sentences.zh: 嘉陶朱之鼓棹，乃語種以免憂。

translations.literal: I praised Taozhu's beating the oars, admonishing Zhong to escape worry.
translations.idiomatic: I praise Tao Zhu as he beats his oars, warning Wen Zhong away from future grief.

sentences.zh: 判身名之有辨，權榮素其無留。

translations.literal: Distinguishing body and name, they weighed glory against plainness and left nothing behind.
translations.idiomatic: They knew body and fame must part; they weighed honor against simplicity and held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 孰如牽犬之路既寡，聽鶴之途何由哉！

translations.literal: How sparse is the path of leading the dog on a leash; by what road might one hear the crane again!
translations.idiomatic: How few are those who have walked the path of leading the hound—and what way remains to hear the crane's cry!

sentences.zh: 〈理以相得為適，古人遺書，與其意合，所以為笑。

translations.literal: 〈When principles align, that is fitting; the ancients' surviving books accorded with his mind—hence the smile.
translations.idiomatic: 〈He smiled because his reading matched the ancients' words—when reason meets understanding, that is the fit state.

sentences.zh: 孫權亦謂周瑜「公瑾與孤意合」。

translations.literal: Sun Quan also told Zhou Yu, "Gongjin agrees with my mind."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan likewise said to Zhou Yu, "Gongjin's mind is one with mine."

sentences.zh: 夫能重道則輕物，存理則忘事，古今質文可謂不同，而此處不異。

translations.literal: To honor the Way is to lighten things; to preserve principle is to forget affairs. Past and present, substance and ornament may differ, yet here they do not.
translations.idiomatic: To hold the Way weighty is to treat things lightly; to keep principle is to set affairs aside. Age and ornament may change with time, yet this point does not.

sentences.zh: 縉雲、放勳不以天居為所樂，故合宮、衢室，皆非淹留，鼎湖、汾陽，乃是所居。

translations.literal: Jinyun and Fangxun did not take heavenly dwellings as their delight; therefore the Grand Palace and Crossroads Hall were not where they lingered—Ding Lake and Fen Yang were their true abodes.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Cloud-Girded Peak nor Radiant Merit took delight in celestial halls; the Grand Palace and Crossroads Chamber were not places to linger—Ding Lake and Fen Yang were where they belonged.

sentences.zh: 文成，張良。

translations.literal: Wencheng: Zhang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: "Wencheng" refers to Zhang Liang.

sentences.zh: 卻粒棄人間事，從赤松子遊。

translations.literal: Abstaining from grain, he cast off human affairs and wandered with Master Red Pine.
translations.idiomatic: He gave up grain and worldly affairs to roam with Master Red Pine.

sentences.zh: 陶朱，范蠡。

translations.literal: Taozhu: Fan Li.
translations.idiomatic: "Taozhu" refers to Fan Li.

sentences.zh: 臨去之際，亦語文種云云。

translations.literal: At the moment of departure, he also spoke thus to Wen Zhong, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his departure, he likewise addressed Wen Zhong with words of warning.

sentences.zh: 謂二賢既權榮素，故身名有判也。

translations.literal: Meaning that these two worthies weighed glory against plainness, therefore body and name were divided.
translations.idiomatic: This means both sages balanced honor against simplicity, and so preserved their lives while leaving fame behind.

sentences.zh: 牽犬，李斯之歎；

translations.literal: "Leading the dog"—Li Si's lament;
translations.idiomatic: "Leading the hound" refers to Li Si's dying sigh;

sentences.zh: 聽鶴，陸機領成都眾大敗後，云「思聞華亭鶴唳，不可復得」。〉

translations.literal: "Hearing the crane"—after Lu Ji led the Chengdu army to great defeat, he said, "I long to hear the cranes of Huating cry again—it cannot be regained."〉
translations.idiomatic: "Hearing the crane" refers to Lu Ji, after his army was routed at Chengdu, saying, "I think of the cranes calling at Huating—I shall never hear them again."〉

sentences.zh: 若夫巢穴以風露貽患，則《大壯》以棟宇袪弊；

translations.literal: Now if nests and caves bring affliction from wind and dew, then the hexagram Dazhuang uses roof and walls to dispel such ills;
translations.idiomatic: If nest and burrow expose one to wind and dew, the hexagram Great Strength prescribes beams and walls to remedy the harm;

sentences.zh: 宮室以瑤琁致美，則白賁以丘園殊世。

translations.literal: if palaces and chambers achieve beauty through jade halls, then White Adornment uses hill gardens to distinguish this world.
translations.idiomatic: if palace halls achieve splendor through jade chambers, the hexagram White Simplicity exalts garden-and-hill retreat as a world apart.

sentences.zh: 惟上□於岩壑，幸兼善而罔滯。

translations.literal: Only the superior [lacuna] in mountain ravines—fortunate to combine excellence without stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: Only the highest virtue [lacuna] unto mountain ravines—blessed to unite excellence without being bound.

sentences.zh: 雖非市朝而寒暑均和，雖是築構而餝朴兩逝。

translations.literal: Though not the marketplace and court, cold and heat are equally tempered; though built structures, ornament and plainness both depart.
translations.idiomatic: Though no market or court, winter and summer are evenly mild; though walled dwellings stand, gaudy ornament and crude plainness alike fall away.

sentences.zh: 〈《易》云，上古穴居野處，後世聖人易之以宮室，上棟下宇，以蔽風雨，蓋取諸《大壯》。

translations.literal: 〈The Book of Changes says: In antiquity people dwelt in caves in the wild; later sages changed this to palaces and chambers, rafters above and walls below, to shelter from wind and rain—this is taken from Dazhuang.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Changes states that in high antiquity men lived in caves and open country; later sages replaced this with houses, roof beams above and eaves below, to shield against wind and rain—drawing this from Great Strength.

sentences.zh: 琁堂自是素，故曰白賁最是上爻也。

translations.literal: A jade hall is by nature plain, hence the White Adornment hexagram's upper line is meant.
translations.idiomatic: A jade hall is inherently simple; hence White Adornment refers chiefly to its topmost line.

sentences.zh: 此堂世異矣。

translations.literal: This hall differs from the age.
translations.idiomatic: Such halls belong to another age entirely.

sentences.zh: 謂岩壑道深於丘園，而不為巢穴，斯免□□得寒暑之適，雖是築構，無妨非朝市云云。〉

translations.literal: Meaning that the Way of mountain ravines runs deeper than hill gardens, yet without becoming nest-caves—thus escaping [lacuna][lacuna], attaining the comfort of cold and heat; though built structures, it does not hinder being no market-court, and so on.〉
translations.idiomatic: He means that life in deep mountain ravines surpasses garden-and-hill retreat, yet avoids mere burrows in cliffs—thus freed from [lacuna], one enjoys the ease of every season; though walls are built, one need not be bound to market or court, and so forth.〉

sentences.zh: 昔仲長願言，流水高山；

translations.literal: Long ago Zhongchang made a vow of words—flowing water, lofty mountains;
translations.idiomatic: In former days Zhongchang Suben spoke his wish—for flowing streams and towering peaks;

sentences.zh: 應璩作書，邙阜洛川。

translations.literal: Ying Qu wrote a letter—Mount Mang, River Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Qu wrote in a letter—of Mount Mang and the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 勢有偏側，地闕周員。

translations.literal: Their terrain sloped on one side; the land lacked full roundness.
translations.idiomatic: Their sites were uneven and one-sided; the ground did not form a full circle.

sentences.zh: 銅陵之奧，卓氏充釽摫之端；

translations.literal: The depths of Copper Mound—the Zhuo clan excelled at the craft of carved wood and split cloth;
translations.idiomatic: In the hidden reaches of Copper Ridge, the Zhuo clan mastered the arts of carved wood and split cloth;

sentences.zh: 金谷之麗，石子致音徽之觀。

translations.literal: The splendor of Golden Valley—Master Stone brought forth sights of music and refinement.
translations.idiomatic: At the splendor of Golden Valley, Shi Chong contrived vistas of music and refined pleasure.

sentences.zh: 徒形域之薈蔚，惜事異於棲盤。

translations.literal: Mere outward domains lush and dense—I regret their purpose differs from dwelling on the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They boast only outward landscapes in verdant profusion—yet their intent falls short of mountain dwelling in contemplative stillness.

sentences.zh: 至若鳳、叢二臺，雲夢、青丘，漳渠、淇園，橘林、長洲，雖千乘之珍苑，孰嘉遁之所遊。

translations.literal: As for the two terraces of Phoenix and Cong, Yunmeng and Qingqiu, Zhang Canal and Qi Garden, orange groves and Long Isle—though precious parks of rulers commanding a thousand chariots, who of reclusive worthies would choose them for wandering?
translations.idiomatic: Phoenix Terrace and Cong Terrace, Yunmeng and Qingqiu, the Zhang Canal and Qi Garden, orange groves and Long Isle—though prized domains of kings who ruled a thousand chariots, none is ground fit for those who honor blessed retreat.

sentences.zh: 且山川之未備，亦何議於兼求。

translations.literal: Moreover, when mountains and rivers are not complete, what talk is there of seeking all at once?
translations.idiomatic: When landscape itself is incomplete, what point is there in demanding it all at once?

sentences.zh: 〈仲長子云：「欲使居有良田廣宅，在高山流川之畔。

translations.literal: 〈Zhongchangzi said: "I wish to have good fields and a broad dwelling beside flowing streams on lofty mountains.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhongchang Suben wrote: "Let one's home have fertile fields and a spacious estate at the foot of lofty mountains beside running streams.

sentences.zh: 溝池自環，竹木周布，場囿在前，果園在後。」

translations.literal: Ditches and ponds encircle themselves; bamboo and trees spread all around; paddocks lie in front, orchards behind."
translations.idiomatic: Channels and ponds loop about; bamboo and trees spread on every side; open paddocks ahead, fruit orchards behind."

sentences.zh: 應璩與程文信書云：「故求道田，在關之西，南臨洛水，北據邙山，託崇岫以為宅，因茂林以為廕。」

translations.literal: Ying Qu wrote to Cheng Wenxin: "My field of seeking the Way lies west of the Pass: south it faces the Luo River, north it holds Mount Mang; I entrust lofty peaks as my dwelling and take dense woods as my shade."
translations.idiomatic: In his letter to Cheng Wenxin, Ying Qu wrote: "My field for seeking the Way lies west of the Pass—bordering the Luo to the south, anchored by Mount Mang to the north—making lofty peaks my home and deep woods my canopy."

sentences.zh: 謂二家山居，不得周員之美。

translations.literal: Meaning that these two families' mountain dwellings lacked the beauty of full roundness.
translations.idiomatic: This means both men's mountain retreats lacked the perfection of a complete, all-around landscape.

sentences.zh: 揚雄《蜀都賦》云：「銅陵衍。」

translations.literal: Yang Xiong's "Rhapsody on the Shu Capital" says: "Copper Mound spreads."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong's Rhapsody on the Shu Capital reads: "Copper Ridge extends."

sentences.zh: 卓王孫採山鑄銅，故《漢書•貨殖傳》云：「卓氏之臨邛，公擅山川。」

translations.literal: Zhuo Wangsun mined mountains to cast copper; hence the Book of Han, "Treatise on Profit-Making," says: "The Zhuo clan at Linqiong—his lordship monopolized mountains and rivers."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Wangsun mined the hills for copper; therefore the Book of Han, Treatise on Profit and Trade, records: "The Zhuo household at Linqiong—the lord of the house held sway over the mountains and streams."

sentences.zh: 揚雄《方言》：「梁、益之間裁木為器曰釽，裂帛為衣曰摫。」

translations.literal: Yang Xiong's "Dialects" says: "Between Liang and Yi, cutting wood to make utensils is called pi; tearing silk to make clothing is called gui."
translations.idiomatic: In Yang Xiong's Dialects: "Between Liang and Yi, carving wood into vessels is called pi, and splitting silk for garments is called gui."

sentences.zh: 金谷，石季倫之別廬，在河南界，有山川林木池沼水碓。

translations.literal: Golden Valley was Shi Jilun's detached villa, within the Henan border, with mountains, rivers, forests, ponds, and water-powered mills.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Valley was the country retreat of Shi Jilun, situated on the Henan frontier, graced with hills and streams, woodland, ponds, and water mills.

sentences.zh: 其鎮下邳時，過遊賦詩，一代盛集。

translations.literal: When he was stationed at Xiapi, passing visitors toured and composed poetry—a great gathering of the age.
translations.idiomatic: While he held command at Xiapi, guests came and went composing verses—it became the grand literary rendezvous of an entire generation.

sentences.zh: 謂二地雖珍麗，然制作非棲盤之意也。

translations.literal: It means that although both places are rare and beautiful, their construction was not in the spirit of dwelling on Pan.
translations.idiomatic: This means that though both estates were splendid rarities, their design fell short of the spirit of quiet retreat on Pan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 鳳臺，秦穆公時秦女所居，以致簫史。

translations.literal: Phoenix Terrace—where a Qin maiden dwelt in Duke Mu of Qin's time, to attract Xiao Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Phoenix Terrace was where a daughter of Qin lived during the reign of Duke Mu of Qin, that she might win the flute-master Xiao Shi.

sentences.zh: 叢臺，趙之崇館。

translations.literal: Cong Terrace—Zhao's lofty pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Cong Terrace was Zhao's towering pleasure-pavilion.

sentences.zh: 張衡謂趙築叢臺於前，楚建章華於後。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng said Zhao built Cong Terrace in front, Chu built Zhanghua in back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng observed that Zhao first raised Cong Terrace, while Chu afterward built Zhanghua.

sentences.zh: 楚之雲夢，大中□居《長飲賦》：楚靈王遊雲夢之中，息於荊臺之上。

translations.literal: Chu's Yunmeng—Da Zhong [lacuna] Ju's "Long Drink Rhapsody" says: King Ling of Chu wandered in the midst of Yunmeng and rested above Jing Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's Yunmeng—Da Zhong [lacuna] Ju's Rhapsody on Long Drinking records: King Ling of Chu roamed the heart of Yunmeng and paused atop Jing Terrace.

sentences.zh: 前方淮之水，左洞庭之波，右顧彭蠡之濤，南望巫山之阿，遂造章華之台。

translations.literal: Ahead lay the waters of the Huai; to the left, the waves of Dongting; to the right, gazing upon the surges of Poyang; southward viewing the slopes of Wu Mountain—thereupon he built Zhanghua Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Before him flowed the Huai; to his left rolled the waves of Dongting; to his right he turned to the tides of Poyang; southward he gazed upon the foothills of Wu Mountain—and so raised Zhanghua Terrace.

sentences.zh: 亦見諸史。

translations.literal: This is also found in various histories.
translations.idiomatic: This too appears in the historical records.

sentences.zh: 淮南青丘，齊之海外，皆獵所。

translations.literal: Huainan's Qingqiu and Qi's lands beyond the sea—all were hunting grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Qingqiu in Huainan and the overseas reaches of Qi were all devoted to the chase.

sentences.zh: 司馬相如云：「秋田乎青丘，彷徨乎海外。」

translations.literal: Sima Xiangru said: "Autumn hunting at Qingqiu, wandering upon the sea beyond."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiangru wrote: "To hunt in autumn at Qingqiu, to roam at leisure beyond the sea."

sentences.zh: 漳渠，史起為魏文侯所起，溉水之所。

translations.literal: The Zhang Canal—Shi Qi built it for Duke Wen of Wei; a place for irrigating waters.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang Canal was constructed by Shi Qi at the behest of Duke Wen of Wei as a conduit for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 淇園，衛之竹園，在淇水之澳，詩人所載。

translations.literal: Qi Garden—Wei's bamboo grove, at the bend of the Qi River, recorded by the poets.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Garden was Wei's bamboo plantation, set at a bend of the Qi River as celebrated in the Book of Songs.

sentences.zh: 橘林，蜀之園林，揚子雲《蜀都賦》亦云橘林。

translations.literal: Orange Grove—Shu's garden orchard; Yang Ziyun's "Rhapsody on the Shu Capital" also mentions Orange Grove.
translations.idiomatic: Orange Grove was a garden estate of Shu; Yang Xiong's Rhapsody on the Shu Capital likewise speaks of orange groves.

sentences.zh: 左太沖謂戶有橘柚之園。

translations.literal: Zuo Taiji said every household had an orange and pomelo orchard.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Si noted that every household kept orchards of oranges and pomelos.

sentences.zh: 長洲，吳之苑囿，左亦謂長洲之茂苑，因江海洲渚以為苑囿□。

translations.literal: Long Isle—Wu's park enclosure; Zuo also speaks of Long Isle's lush park, making river-sea islets and sandbars into a park enclosure [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: Long Isle was Wu's pleasure park; Zuo Si also praises its lush demesne, fashioning river islets and sea sandbars into a garden enclosure [lacuna].

sentences.zh: □□□□□□□□故□表此園之珍靜。

translations.literal: [lacuna], therefore [lacuna] expresses this garden's rare tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: Where the text is lost, it nonetheless shows this garden's singular beauty and seclusion.

sentences.zh: 千乘宴嬉之所，非□□憩止之□，且山川亦不能兼茂，隨地勢所遇耳。〉

translations.literal: A place for banquets and sport among rulers of a thousand chariots—not a [lacuna] resting place [lacuna]; moreover mountains and rivers cannot all flourish together—it depends on what the terrain offers.〉
translations.idiomatic: A venue for revelry among lords who command a thousand chariots—not a homeland where [lacuna] may rest [lacuna]; and no landscape can boast every excellence at once—it yields only what its ground provides.〉

sentences.zh: 覽明達之撫運，乘機緘而理默。

translations.literal: Observing the perspicacious in governing fortune, riding the moment in silence while principle works quietly.
translations.idiomatic: I contemplated how the wise steer the turnings of fate, seizing fortune's tide in guarded silence while letting principle speak for itself.

sentences.zh: 指歲暮而歸休，詠宏徽於刊勒。

translations.literal: Pointing to year's end to retire and rest, singing great virtues in carved inscription.
translations.idiomatic: I fixed my gaze on the year's close as a time to withdraw and rest, and sang of lofty merit in words meant for stone.

sentences.zh: 狹三閭之喪江，矜望諸之去國。

translations.literal: Narrow is the Three Gorges' loss of the Jiang; one pities Wang Zhu's departure from his state.
translations.idiomatic: How narrow the grief of Qu Yuan drowned in the Jiang; how pitiable Yue Yi's exile from his homeland.

sentences.zh: 選自然之神麗，盡高棲之意得。

translations.literal: Choosing nature's divine beauty, fully attaining the intent of lofty dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: I chose ground where nature's spirit shines most fair, and so fulfilled the dream of dwelling on high.

sentences.zh: 〈余祖車騎建大功淮、肥，江左得免橫流之禍。

translations.literal: 〈My ancestor the General of Chariots and Cavalry achieved great merit at Huai and Fei; the lands east of the Yangzi thereby escaped the calamity of sweeping chaos.
translations.idiomatic: 〈My grandfather, General of Chariots and Cavalry, won great victories on the Huai and at Fei, and the south of the Yangzi was spared the flood of ruin.

sentences.zh: 後及太傅既薨，建圖已輟，於是便求解駕東歸，以避君側之亂。

translations.literal: Later, when the Grand Tutor had passed away and the founding plan was already halted, he thereupon sought release from office and returned east, to avoid turmoil at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after the Grand Tutor died and the great design was abandoned, he asked to resign his post and return east, seeking refuge from the turmoil at court.

sentences.zh: 廢興隱顯，當是賢達之心，故選神麗之所，以申高棲之意。

translations.literal: Rise and fall, obscurity and prominence—these surely belong to the mind of the worthy and eminent; therefore he chose a place of divine beauty to express the intent of lofty dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune's turn and one's season in the light or in hiding—these are concerns of every worthy mind; hence he chose a landscape graced by nature's spirit to give voice to his wish for dwelling on high.

sentences.zh: 經始山川，實基於此。〉

translations.literal: Initiating his dwelling among mountains and rivers truly began from this.〉
translations.idiomatic: The founding of his mountain retreat took root in this decision.〉

sentences.zh: 仰前哲之遺訓，俯性情之所便。

translations.literal: Looking up to the legacy teachings of former sages, looking down to what one's nature finds convenient.
translations.idiomatic: I looked up to the counsel of sages past and looked down upon what my own temperament prefers.

sentences.zh: 奉微軀以宴息，保自事以乘閑。

translations.literal: Serving with a slight frame to rest at ease, preserving personal affairs to seize leisure.
translations.idiomatic: With this frail body I surrender to restful repose, and tend my own concerns that I may claim my leisure.

sentences.zh: 愧班生之夙悟，慚尚子之晚研。

translations.literal: Ashamed before Master Ban's early enlightenment, abashed before Master Shang's late study.
translations.idiomatic: I felt shame before Ban Sheng's early awakening, and regret beside Shang Zi's late striving.

sentences.zh: 年與疾而偕來，志乘拙而俱旋。

translations.literal: Age and illness arrive together; aspiration, bearing simplicity, turns back together.
translations.idiomatic: Age and ailment came hand in hand, and with them my wish to embrace plainness and turn homeward.

sentences.zh: 謝平生於知遊，棲清曠於山川。

translations.literal: Bidding farewell to a lifetime among friends and travels, dwelling in clarity and openness among mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: I took leave of lifelong companions and wandering, and made my home in the clear expanse of mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 〈謂經始此山，遺訓於後也。

translations.literal: 〈This means initiating this mountain leaves a legacy teaching for those who follow.
translations.idiomatic: 〈He means that founding this mountain retreat bequeaths an example to posterity.

sentences.zh: 性情各有所便，山居是其宜也。

translations.literal: Nature and disposition each have their own convenience; mountain dwelling suits him best.
translations.idiomatic: Every temperament has its proper bent, and for him life in the mountains was the fitting choice.

sentences.zh: 《易》云：「向晦入宴息。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "As dusk approaches, enter rest and repose."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes reads: "When evening comes, withdraw to rest."

sentences.zh: 莊周云：「自事其心。」

translations.literal: Zhuang Zhou says: "Attend to one's own heart."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi says: "Look after your own mind."

sentences.zh: 此二是其所處。

translations.literal: These two are his conditions of dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: These two passages describe the life he chose.

sentences.zh: 班嗣本不染世，故曰夙悟；

translations.literal: Ban Si was never stained by the world, hence 'early enlightenment';
translations.idiomatic: Ban Si had never been tainted by worldly affairs, hence 'early enlightenment';

sentences.zh: 尚平未能去累，故曰晚研。

translations.literal: Shang Ping had not yet cast off encumbrances, hence 'late study.'
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ping had not yet freed himself from worldly burdens, hence 'late striving.'

sentences.zh: 想遲二人，更以年衰疾至。

translations.literal: Thinking of these two men, I am further delayed by the arrival of age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on those two men, I find myself still behind—and now age and sickness have overtaken me as well.

sentences.zh: 志寡求拙曰乘，並可山居。

translations.literal: A mind of few desires and seeking simplicity is called cheng—both suit mountain dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: A will content with little and cleaving to plainness is called cheng—either suits a life in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 曰與知遊別，故曰謝平生；

translations.literal: Saying farewell to friends and travels, hence 'bidding farewell to a lifetime';
translations.idiomatic: Parting from companions and wanderings, hence 'farewell to a lifetime of friendship';

sentences.zh: 就山川，故曰棲清曠。〉

translations.literal: Approaching mountains and rivers, hence 'dwelling in clarity and openness.'〉
translations.idiomatic: Taking refuge among mountains and rivers, hence 'dwelling in clear expanse.'〉

sentences.zh: 其居也，左湖右江，往渚還汀。

translations.literal: As to the dwelling: lake to the left, river to the right; going to islets, returning to sandbars.
translations.idiomatic: The site lay with a lake on the left and a river on the right, with islets near at hand and sandbars within reach.

sentences.zh: 面山背阜，東阻西傾。

translations.literal: Facing mountains, backed by hills; blocked in the east, sloping westward.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains faced it and hills rose behind; the east was walled off and the ground fell away to the west.

sentences.zh: 抱含吸吐，款跨紆縈。

translations.literal: Embracing, containing, inhaling, exhaling; extending across winding curves.
translations.idiomatic: Waters gathered and released, drew in and flowed out, spreading through sinuous bends.

sentences.zh: 綿聯邪亙，側直齊平。

translations.literal: Continuously linked, crooked and stretched; leaning, straight, level alike.
translations.idiomatic: Channels linked in crooked reach, now askew, now straight, now level together.

sentences.zh: 〈枚乘曰：「左江右湖，其樂無有。」

translations.literal: 〈Mei Cheng said: "River to the left, lake to the right—its joy is boundless."
translations.idiomatic: 〈Mei Cheng wrote: "With the river on the left and the lake on the right, pleasure knows no limit."

sentences.zh: 此吳客說楚公子之詞。

translations.literal: These are words with which a guest of Wu persuaded the prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: This was a Wu visitor's speech to the prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 當謂江都之野，彼雖有江湖而乏山巖，此憶江湖左右與之同，而山嶽形勢，池城所無也。

translations.literal: It should refer to the wilds of Jiangdu—though there are rivers and lakes, they lack mountains and cliffs; here one recalls rivers and lakes on both sides in like fashion, yet the mountain peaks and terrain are what cities by ponds cannot have.
translations.idiomatic: He likely meant the countryside of Jiangdu—though rivers and lakes abound there, cliffs and peaks are scarce; here, rivers and lakes likewise flank both sides, but the mountain ridgelines and contours are what no walled pond-city can offer.

sentences.zh: 往渚還汀，謂四面有水；

translations.literal: "Going to islets and returning to sandbars" means water on all four sides;
translations.idiomatic: "Going to islets and returning to sandbars" means that water surrounds the dwelling on every side;

sentences.zh: 面山背阜，亦謂東西有山，便是四水之裏也。

translations.literal: "Facing mountains and backing onto mounds" also means mountains east and west—it is thus within four waters.
translations.idiomatic: "Facing mountains and backing onto mounds" likewise means mountains to east and west; the site lies enclosed within four waters.

sentences.zh: 抱含吐吸，謂中央復有川。

translations.literal: "Embracing, containing, exhaling, and inhaling" means that in the center there is again a stream.
translations.idiomatic: "Embracing, containing, exhaling, and inhaling" means that a stream runs through the center as well.

sentences.zh: 款跨紆縈，謂邊背相連帶。

translations.literal: "Spanning gracefully and winding about" means the margins and backs are linked together.
translations.idiomatic: "Spanning gracefully and winding about" means that the shores and backs of the waters are joined in one continuous circuit.

sentences.zh: 迂回處謂之邪亙，平正處謂之側直。〉

translations.literal: Winding places are called oblique spans; level and straight places are called lateral directness.〉
translations.idiomatic: Where the terrain winds, he calls it an oblique span; where it is level and straight, he calls it lateral directness.〉

sentences.zh: 近東則上田、下湖，西豁、南谷，石堟、石滂，閔硎、黃竹。

translations.literal: To the near east are Upper Field, Lower Lake, West Pass, South Valley, Stone Barrier, Stone Cascade, Min Gorge, and Yellow Bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: To the east lie Upper Field and Lower Lake, West Pass and South Valley, Stone Barrier and Stone Cascade, Min Gorge and Yellow Bamboo.

sentences.zh: 決飛泉於百仞，森高薄於千麓。

translations.literal: Unleashing flying springs from hundred-ren cliffs; densely towering peaks pressing against thousand foothills.
translations.idiomatic: Flying springs burst from cliffs a hundred ren high; dense peaks tower and press against a thousand foothills.

sentences.zh: 寫長源於遠江，泒深毖於近瀆。

translations.literal: Drawing the long source from the distant river; branching the deep flow into nearby channels.
translations.idiomatic: The long source is drawn from the distant river; the deep current branches into nearby irrigation ditches.

sentences.zh: 〈上田在下湖之水口，名為田口。

translations.literal: 〈Upper Field is at the water mouth of Lower Lake, named Field Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Upper Field stands at the outlet of Lower Lake and is called Field Mouth.

sentences.zh: 下湖在田之下下處，並有名山川。

translations.literal: Lower Lake lies at the lowest part below the fields; both have famed mountains and streams.
translations.idiomatic: Lower Lake lies at the lowest reach below the fields; both places boast celebrated mountains and streams.

sentences.zh: 西谿、南谷分流，谷鄣水畎入田口。

translations.literal: The West Stream and South Valley divide the flow; valley barrier waters irrigate into Field Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The West Stream and South Valley split the current; waters from the valley barrier are channeled by irrigation ditches into Field Mouth.

sentences.zh: 西谿水出始寧縣西谷鄣，是近山之最高峰者，西谿便是□之背。

translations.literal: The West Stream rises from West Valley Barrier in Shining county—the highest peak among the nearby mountains; the West Stream is the back of [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: The West Stream issues from West Valley Barrier in Shining county, the highest of the nearby peaks; the West Stream lies on the far side of [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 入西谿之裏，得石堟，以石為阻，故謂為堟。

translations.literal: Entering within the West Stream, one reaches Stone Barrier; stone forms the obstruction, hence it is called a barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Farther within the West Stream one comes to Stone Barrier; stone blocks the way, and so the place is named for its barrier.

sentences.zh: 石滂在西谿之東，從縣南入九里，兩面峻峭數十丈，水自上飛下。

translations.literal: Stone Cascade is east of the West Stream; nine li south from the county seat, cliffs on both sides rise steeply several dozen zhang, and water flies down from above.
translations.idiomatic: Stone Cascade lies east of the West Stream. Nine li south of the county seat, cliffs on either side soar several dozen zhang, and water plunges from above.

sentences.zh: 比至外谿，封墱十數里，皆飛流迅激，左右岩壁綠竹。

translations.literal: By the time one reaches the outer stream, for ten-odd li of embankments, all are flying currents rushing swiftly; green bamboo clings to cliff walls on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: By the outer stream, embankments stretch for more than ten li, all alive with rushing cascades; green bamboo drapes the cliff walls on either side.

sentences.zh: 閔硎，在石滂之東谿，逶迤下注良田。

translations.literal: Min Gorge is on the eastern stream of Stone Cascade; winding down it irrigates fertile fields.
translations.idiomatic: Min Gorge lies on the eastern stream below Stone Cascade; its waters wind down to irrigate fertile fields.

sentences.zh: 黃竹與其連，南界莆中也。〉

translations.literal: Yellow Bamboo connects with it; to the south it borders Pu Village.〉
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bamboo joins it, and to the south the district reaches Pu Village.〉

sentences.zh: 近南則會以雙流，縈以三洲。

translations.literal: To the near south, twin streams meet; three islets encircle them.
translations.idiomatic: To the south, twin streams converge, ringed by three islets.

sentences.zh: 表裏回游，離合山川。

translations.literal: Inner and outer circuits flow back and forth; streams and mountains part and join.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer waters circle back upon one another; streams and mountains divide and reunite.

sentences.zh: 崿崩飛於東峭，槃傍薄於西阡。

translations.literal: A perilous cliff seems to collapse and fly from the eastern precipice; Pan rests close beside the western fields.
translations.idiomatic: A crumbling cliff looms from the eastern bluff; Pan Hill presses close against the western fields.

sentences.zh: 拂青林而激波，揮白沙而生漣。

translations.literal: Brushing green groves and stirring waves; scattering white sand and raising ripples.
translations.idiomatic: Waters brush green groves and stir the waves; they scatter white sand and raise ripples.

sentences.zh: 〈雙流，謂剡江及小江，此二水同會于山南，便合流注下。

translations.literal: 〈Twin Streams refers to the Shining River and the Little River—these two waters meet together south of the mountain, then join as one and flow downward.
translations.idiomatic: 〈"Twin Streams" means the Shining River and the Little River. The two waters meet south of the mountain, merge, and flow on together.

sentences.zh: 三洲在二水之口，排沙積岸，成此洲漲。

translations.literal: The Three Islets are at the mouth of the two rivers; sand piled along the banks formed these islet expansions.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Islets stand where the two rivers meet; sand piled along the banks built up these islet reaches.

sentences.zh: 表裏合，是其貌狀也。

translations.literal: Inner and outer together—that is its appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer waters joined—that is the scene he describes.

sentences.zh: 崿者，謂回江岑，在其山居之南界，有石跳出，將崩江中，行者莫不駭慄。

translations.literal: Perilous cliff: it means the bending river ridge—at the southern boundary of the dwelling on the mountain, a stone juts out, about to collapse into the river; passersby are all struck with dread.
translations.idiomatic: "Perilous cliff" refers to the bending river ridge. At the southern edge of the mountain dwelling, a boulder thrusts out as if about to crash into the river; every traveler who passes is seized with dread.

sentences.zh: 槃者，是縣故治之所，在江之□□用槃石竟渚，並帶青林而連白沙也。〉

translations.literal: Pan: this was the site of the county's former seat of government, on the river's [lacuna]; boulder-stones reach the sandbars, all girdled with green groves and linked to white sand.〉
translations.idiomatic: "Pan" was the site of the county's old seat of government, on the river's [lacuna]; boulder-stones reach the sandbars, girdled with green groves and linked to white sand.〉

sentences.zh: 近西則楊、賓接峰，唐皇連縱。

translations.literal: To the near west, Yang and Bin meet peaks; Tang and Huang extend in succession.
translations.idiomatic: To the west, Yang and Bin meet the peaks; Tang and Huang stretch on in succession.

sentences.zh: 室、壁帶谿，曾、孤臨江。

translations.literal: Shi and Bi girdle streams; Zeng and Gu stand overlooking the river.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Bi girdle the streams; Zeng and Gu stand overlooking the river.

sentences.zh: 竹緣浦以被綠，石照澗而映紅。

translations.literal: Bamboo along the shore spreads green; stone reflecting the stream gleams red.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo lines the shore in green; red stone gleams in the reflected stream.

sentences.zh: 月隱山而成陰，木鳴柯以起風。

translations.literal: The moon hiding behind mountains casts shade; trees rattling their branches stir the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains hide the moon and cast shade; trees clatter their branches and raise the wind.

sentences.zh: 〈楊中、元賓，並小江之近處，與山相接也。

translations.literal: 〈Yangzhong and Yuanbin are both places near the Little River, connecting with the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yangzhong and Yuanbin are both spots near the Little River where the water meets the mountains.

sentences.zh: 唐皇便從北出。

translations.literal: Tang and Huang extend northward from there.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Huang run northward from there.

sentences.zh: 室，石室，在小江口南岸。

translations.literal: Shi is Stone Chamber, on the south bank at the mouth of the Little River.
translations.idiomatic: Shi is Stone Chamber, on the south bank at the mouth of the Little River.

sentences.zh: 壁，小江北岸。

translations.literal: Bi is on the north bank of the Little River.
translations.idiomatic: Bi lies on the north bank of the Little River.

sentences.zh: 並在楊中之下。

translations.literal: Both lie below Yangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Both lie downstream from Yangzhong.

sentences.zh: 壁高四十丈，色赤，故曰照澗而映紅。

translations.literal: The cliff is forty zhang high and red in color—hence the phrase "stone reflecting the stream gleams red."
translations.idiomatic: The cliff rises forty zhang and is red in hue—hence his line about stone gleaming red in the reflected stream.

sentences.zh: 曾山之西，孤山之南，王子所經始，並臨江，皆被以綠竹。

translations.literal: West of Mount Zeng, south of Mount Gu—estates begun by the Prince—all overlook the river and are clothed in green bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: West of Mount Zeng and south of Mount Gu lie estates the Prince first established; all face the river and are draped in green bamboo.

sentences.zh: 山高月隱，便謂為陰；

translations.literal: When mountains are high the moon is hidden—thus it is called shade;
translations.idiomatic: When the mountains are high the moon is hidden—hence he speaks of shade;

sentences.zh: 鳥集柯嗚，便謂為風也。〉

translations.literal: Birds gather on branches and cry—thus it is called wind.〉
translations.idiomatic: when birds gather on the branches and cry—hence he speaks of wind.〉

sentences.zh: 近北則二巫結湖，兩軿通沼。

translations.literal: To the near north, the Twin Wu Lakes join; two embankments connect marshes.
translations.idiomatic: To the north, the Twin Wu Lakes join; two embankments link the marshes.

sentences.zh: 橫、石判盡，休、周分表。

translations.literal: Heng and Shi stand entirely apart; Xiu and Zhou mark separate sides.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and Shi stand wholly apart; Xiu and Zhou mark opposite sides.

sentences.zh: 引脩堤之逶迤，吐泉流之浩溔。

translations.literal: Drawing the long winding dike; issuing the vast surge of spring streams.
translations.idiomatic: Long dikes wind outward; spring streams pour forth in broad flood.

sentences.zh: 山磯下而回澤，瀨石上而開道。

translations.literal: Rocky shoals below the mountains turn back into marshes; rapids over stone open a channel.
translations.idiomatic: Rocky shoals below the mountains spread into marshes; rapids over stone cut open a passage.

sentences.zh: 〈大小巫湖，中隔一山。

translations.literal: 〈Great and Little Wu Lakes, separated by a mountain in between.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Great and Little Wu Lakes, with a mountain between them.

sentences.zh: 外軿周回，在圻西北。

translations.literal: The outer embankment circles round, northwest of the dyke.
translations.idiomatic: The outer embankment loops around, northwest of the dyke.

sentences.zh: 邊浦出江，竝是美處。

translations.literal: Shores opening onto the river—all are fine places.
translations.idiomatic: Shores that open onto the river—all are fine spots.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，王穆之居大巫湖，經始處所猶在。

translations.literal: In the Yixi era, Wang Muzhi dwelt at Great Wu Lake; the site he first established still remains.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yixi era Wang Muzhi lived at Great Wu Lake; the place he first built still stands.

sentences.zh: 兩軿皆長溪，外軿出山之後四五里許，裏軿亦隔一山，出新堟。

translations.literal: Both embankments are long streams; the outer embankment emerges four or five li beyond the mountain; the inner embankment also crosses a mountain and opens at New Barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Both embankments are long streams. The outer one runs four or five li beyond the mountain; the inner one also crosses a mountain and opens at New Barrier.

sentences.zh: 橫山，野舍之北面。

translations.literal: Heng Mountain is north of the country retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Mountain lies north of the country retreat.

sentences.zh: 常石，野舍之西北。

translations.literal: Chang Stone is northwest of the country retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Stone lies northwest of the country retreat.

sentences.zh: 巫湖舊唐，故曰脩堤。

translations.literal: Wu Lake was formerly a pond (Tang), hence "repairing the dike."
translations.idiomatic: The Wu lakes were once an old reservoir—hence his line about winding dikes.

sentences.zh: 長谿甚遠，故曰泉流。

translations.literal: The long stream is very far, hence "spring streams."
translations.idiomatic: The long creek runs very far—hence "spring streams pouring forth."

sentences.zh: 常石磯□□□□故曰下磯而回澤。

translations.literal: Chang Stone shoal [lacuna][lacuna][lacuna][lacuna]—hence "shoals below and turning marshes."
translations.idiomatic: At Chang Stone shoal [lacuna]—hence "rocky shoals below spreading into marshes."

sentences.zh: 裏軿漫石數里，水從上過，故曰瀨石上而開道。

translations.literal: The inner embankment floods over stone for several li; water passes from above—hence "rapids over stone and opening a channel."
translations.idiomatic: The inner stream spreads over stones for miles, water running over the top—hence "rapids cutting over stone and opening a passage."

sentences.zh: 休山東北，周里山在休之南，竝是北邊。〉

translations.literal: Mount Xiu is to the northeast; Mount Zhouli lies south of Xiu—both mark the northern side.〉
translations.idiomatic: Mount Xiu stands to the northeast, Zhouli Mountain south of Xiu—both define the northern boundary.〉

sentences.zh: 遠東則天台、桐柏，方石、太平，二韭、四明，五奧、三菁。

translations.literal: Far east: Tiantai, Tongbai, Fangshi, Taiping, Two-Leek, Four-Bright, Five-Depths, Three-Jing.
translations.idiomatic: To the far east lie Tiantai and Tongbai, Fangshi and Taiping, the Twin Leeks and Four-Bright Peak, the Five Depths and Three Jing.

sentences.zh: 表神異於緯牒，驗感應于於靈。

translations.literal: Manifesting marvels in weft chronicles, verifying responsiveness in numinous proof.
translations.idiomatic: Marvels recorded in apocryphal texts, responsiveness attested in numinous signs.

sentences.zh: 淩石橋之莓苔，越楢谿之紆縈。

translations.literal: Crossing the stone bridge's moss; traversing Nan Creek's winding course.
translations.idiomatic: Moss covers the stone bridge one crosses; Nan Creek winds in serpentine loops one traverses.

sentences.zh: 〈天台、桐柏，七縣餘地，南帶海。

translations.literal: 〈Tiantai and Tongbai—lands spanning seven counties, bordering the sea to the south.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Tiantai and Tongbai—these peaks preside over more than seven counties, the sea bordering them to the south.

sentences.zh: 二韭、四明、五奧，皆相連接，奇地所無，高於五嶽，便是海中三山之流。

translations.literal: Two-Leek, Four-Bright, and Five-Depths all connect together—a wonder nowhere else found, higher than the Five Peaks, of the line of the Three Mountains in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Twin Leeks, Four-Bright, and Five Depths all connect in one chain—a marvel unmatched elsewhere, rising higher than the Five Sacred Peaks, kin to the Three Isles of the sea.

sentences.zh: 韭以菜為名。

translations.literal: Leek takes its name from the vegetable.
translations.idiomatic: "Leek" takes its name from the vegetable.

sentences.zh: 四明、方石，四面自然開窗也。

translations.literal: Four-Bright and Fangshi naturally open windows on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Four-Bright and Fangshi—their four faces naturally open like windows to the sky.

sentences.zh: 五奧者，曇濟道人、蔡氏、郗氏、謝氏、陳氏各有一奧，皆相掎角，並是奇地。

translations.literal: The Five Depths: Daoist Tanji, the Cai clan, the Xi clan, the Xie clan, and the Chen clan each have one depth; all interlock at angles—each is a marvelous place.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Depths—Tanji the Daoist, the Cai, Xi, Xie, and Chen families each hold one ravine; they interlock like strategic corners, and every one is a wondrous site.

sentences.zh: 三菁，太平之北。

translations.literal: Three-Jing lies north of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Three Jing stands north of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 太平，天台之始。

translations.literal: Taiping is the beginning of Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping marks the foot of Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 方石，直上萬丈，下有長谿，亦是縉雲之流云。

translations.literal: Fangshi rises straight up ten thousand zhang; below is a long stream—also of the line of Jinyun, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Fangshi shoots straight upward ten thousand zhang; a long stream runs below—it too belongs to the Jinyun chain.

sentences.zh: 此諸山並見圖緯，神仙所居。

translations.literal: All these mountains appear in chart-weft texts, abodes of immortals.
translations.idiomatic: All these peaks appear in apocryphal geographies—dwellings of immortals.

sentences.zh: 往來要徑石橋，過楢谿，人跡之艱，不復過此也。〉

translations.literal: The essential route runs through Stone Bridge, crossing Nan Creek—no track harder for human passage; one does not pass beyond this point.〉
translations.idiomatic: The vital route crosses Stone Bridge and passes Nan Creek—nowhere is human passage harder; travelers do not go beyond here.〉

sentences.zh: 遠南則松箴、棲雞，唐嵫、漫石。

translations.literal: Far south: Song Needle, Roosting Cock, Tang Mound, Man Stone.
translations.idiomatic: To the far south lie Song Needle, Roosting Cock, Tang Mound, and Man Stone.

sentences.zh: 崪、嵊對嶺，釐、孟分隔。

translations.literal: Cu and Sheng face each other across ridges; Li and Meng stand apart.
translations.idiomatic: Cu and Sheng face off across the ridges; Li and Meng mark separate domains.

sentences.zh: 入極浦而邅回，迷不知其所適。

translations.literal: Entering the farthest shore and winding back, lost without knowing where one goes.
translations.idiomatic: One enters the outermost inlets and circles back, lost without knowing the way.

sentences.zh: 上嶔崎而蒙籠，下深沉而澆激。

translations.literal: Above, perilous peaks enshrouded in gloom; below, deep waters brawling and churning.
translations.idiomatic: Above loom jagged peaks shrouded in mist; below lie deep waters, churning and savage.

sentences.zh: 〈棲雞，在保口之上，別浦入其中，周回甚深，四山之裏。

translations.literal: 〈Roosting Cock lies above Baokou; a separate inlet enters it, circling very deep within four mountains.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Roosting Cock stands above Baokou; a side channel enters it, winding deep within the heart of four mountains.

sentences.zh: 松箴在棲雞之上，緣江。

translations.literal: Song Needle lies above Roosting Cock, along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Song Needle rises above Roosting Cock, hugging the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 唐嵫入太平水路，上有瀑布數百丈。

translations.literal: Tang Mound enters the Taiping water route; above it are waterfalls of several hundred zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Mound joins the waterway to Taiping; above it cascades a waterfall hundreds of zhang high.

sentences.zh: 漫石在唐嵫下，郗景興經始精舍，亦是名山之流。

translations.literal: Man Stone lies below Tang Mound; Xi Jingxing first established a refined retreat there—it too belongs to the famous mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Man Stone lies below Tang Mound, where Xi Jingxing founded a mountain retreat—it too belongs among the celebrated peaks.

sentences.zh: 崪、嵊與分界，去山八十里，故曰遠南。

translations.literal: Cu and Sheng mark the boundary, eighty li from the mountain—hence "far south."
translations.idiomatic: Cu and Sheng form the boundary line, eighty li from the mountain—hence "the far south."

sentences.zh: 前嶺鳥道，正當五十里高，左右所無，就下地形高，乃當不稱。

translations.literal: The bird path over the front ridge is said to be fifty li high; nothing to left or right compares—measured against the terrain below, the height does not match.
translations.idiomatic: The bird track over the forward ridge is claimed to reach fifty li in height, unmatched to left or right—yet compared with the land below, the figure does not add up.

sentences.zh: 遠望釐山甚奇，謂白爍尖者最高，下有良田，王敬弘經始精舍。

translations.literal: Gazing afar, Li Mountain is very marvelous; White Gleam Peak is said to be highest; below are fine fields—Wang Jinghong first established a refined retreat there.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mountain looks marvelous from afar; White Gleam Peak is said to be the highest, with fine fields below—where Wang Jinghong built a mountain retreat.

sentences.zh: 曇濟道人住孟山，名曰孟埭，羊署之疁田。

translations.literal: Daoist Tanji dwelt on Meng Mountain, called Meng Embankment—the flooded fields of Yang Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Tanji the Daoist lived on Meng Mountain, at a place called Meng Embankment—Yang Shu's polder fields.

sentences.zh: 清溪秀竹，回開巨石，有趣之極。

translations.literal: Clear streams and elegant bamboo; winding openings among giant stones—the utmost in charm.
translations.idiomatic: Clear streams and graceful bamboo, boulders parting in great arcs—charm in its purest form.

sentences.zh: 此中多諸浦澗，傍依茂林，迷不知所通，嶔崎深沉，處處皆然，不但一處。〉

translations.literal: Here are many inlets and ravines, flanked by dense forest—one loses the way not knowing where they lead; jagged peaks and deep waters—everywhere alike, not in one place alone.〉
translations.idiomatic: Countless inlets and streams wind through dense woods until one loses all sense of direction; jagged cliffs and deep pools appear everywhere—not in this spot alone.〉

sentences.zh: 遠西則

translations.literal: As for the far west, then—
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the distant west—

sentences.zh: 〈下闕〉。

translations.literal: 〈Text below [lacuna].〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The passage below is [lacuna].〉

sentences.zh: 遠北則長江永歸，巨海延納。

translations.literal: Far north: the Long River forever returns; the vast sea receives and holds.
translations.idiomatic: To the far north the Yangzi flows ever seaward; the great ocean gathers and holds it.

sentences.zh: 崐漲緬曠，島嶼綢沓。

translations.literal: Kun islets, rising shoals, boundless expanse; islands layered thick.
translations.idiomatic: Isolated islets and swelling sandbars stretch without end; islands pile one upon another.

sentences.zh: 山縱橫以布護，水回沉而縈浥。

translations.literal: Mountains cross and spread in protective array; waters sink back and coil, soaking the banks.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains array themselves in sheltering ranks; waters sink and swirl, soaking the shores.

sentences.zh: 信荒極之綿眇，究風波之睽合。

translations.literal: Truly the remote extremity's vast remoteness; exploring wind and waves' discord and union.
translations.idiomatic: Here lies the boundless edge of the wild east—where wind and wave meet in restless union and strife.

sentences.zh: 〈江從山北流，窮上虞界，謂之三江口，便是大海。

translations.literal: 〈The river flows from the north of the mountains, reaching the border of Shangyu—called Three-River Mouth; there it is the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The river runs north of the mountains to the Shangyu boundary—the Three-River Mouth—where it meets the ocean.

sentences.zh: 老子謂海為百谷王，以其善處下也。

translations.literal: Laozi said the sea is king of the hundred valleys because it is good at placing itself below.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi called the sea king of all valleys because it dwells below them all.

sentences.zh: 海人謂孤山為崐。

translations.literal: Sea folk call an isolated mountain Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Seafaring people call a lone hill a Kun.

sentences.zh: 薄洲有山，謂之島嶼，即洲也。

translations.literal: Where a thin shoal has a mountain, it is called an island—islet; that is, a sandbar.
translations.idiomatic: Where sandbars rise into hills, people call them islands—islets, in other words.

sentences.zh: 漲者，沙始起將欲成嶼，縱橫無常，於一處回沉相縈擾也。

translations.literal: A shoal-rise is sand just beginning to rise, about to become an islet—running crosswise without fixity, in one place sinking back and tangling together.
translations.idiomatic: A shoal-rise is sand just lifting, about to become an islet—shifting without pattern, swirling and sinking in restless coils.

sentences.zh: 大荒東極，故為荒極。

translations.literal: The Great Wilderness's eastern extremity—hence "wilderness's extremity."
translations.idiomatic: The eastern edge of the Great Wilderness—hence "the remote extremity."

sentences.zh: 風波不恆，為睽合也。〉

translations.literal: Wind and waves are not constant—hence "discord and union."〉
translations.idiomatic: Wind and waves never hold steady—hence "union and strife."〉

sentences.zh: 徒觀其南術之□，□□生磯，□□成衍。

translations.literal: Merely viewing his southern lane's [lacuna], [lacuna][lacuna] producing shoals, [lacuna][lacuna] forming expanse.
translations.idiomatic: Only to gaze upon his southern lane's [lacuna], where [lacuna][lacuna] births rocky shoals and [lacuna][lacuna] opens into broad marsh.

sentences.zh: □岸測深，相渚知淺。

translations.literal: [lacuna] banks gauge depth; facing shoals one knows shallows.
translations.idiomatic: From [lacuna] banks one sounds the depth; from sandbars one reads the shallows.

sentences.zh: 洪濤滿則曾石沒，清瀾減則沉沙顯。

translations.literal: When great swells fill, Zeng Stone is submerged; when clear ripples recede, sunken sand appears.
translations.idiomatic: When surging tides rise, Zeng Rock disappears; when the clear flood withdraws, hidden sand emerges.

sentences.zh: 及風興濤作，水勢奔壯。

translations.literal: When wind rises and waves form, the water's force charges mighty.
translations.idiomatic: When wind stirs and waves build, the water surges with terrifying force.

sentences.zh: 于歲春秋，在月朔望。

translations.literal: In the year's spring and autumn, at the month's new and full moons.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and autumn, at the new moon and the full.

sentences.zh: 湯湯驚波，滔滔駭浪。

translations.literal: Surging, startling waves; rolling, dreadful breakers.
translations.idiomatic: Waves surge in startled thunder; breakers roll in endless dread.

sentences.zh: 電激雷崩，飛流灑漾。

translations.literal: Lightning strikes, thunder collapses; flying streams splash and ripple.
translations.idiomatic: Lightning lashes; thunder breaks; torrents leap and spray in every direction.

sentences.zh: 淩絕壁而起岑，橫中流而連薄。

translations.literal: Leaping from sheer cliffs to rise into peaks, spanning midstream in linked sheets.
translations.idiomatic: They vault sheer cliffs into jagged crests and stretch across the current in unbroken sheets.

sentences.zh: 始迅轉而騰天，終倒底而見壑。

translations.literal: At first spinning swiftly and soaring to heaven; finally plunging to the bottom to reveal gorges.
translations.idiomatic: First they whirl upward and vault toward the sky; then they plunge to the depths and lay bare the gorges below.

sentences.zh: 此楚貳心醉於吳客，河靈懷慚於海若。

translations.literal: Hence the Chu heir's heart was intoxicated by the Wu guest; the River Spirit felt shame before the Lord of the Sea.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the heir of Chu lost his heart to the guest from Wu, and why the River Spirit felt abashed before the Lord of the Sea.

sentences.zh: 〈南術是其臨江舊宅，門前對江，三轉曾山，路窮四江，對岸西面常石。

translations.literal: 〈Nanshu was his old riverside dwelling; before the gate it faced the river. After three turns around Zeng Mountain, the road ended at Sijiang; across the river to the west lay Chang Stone.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Nanshu was his former home on the river: the gate opened straight onto the water. Three bends around Zeng Mountain brought the road to its end at Sijiang; on the opposite bank to the west stood Chang Stone.

sentences.zh: 此二山之間，西南角岸孤山，此二山皆是狹處，故曰生磯。

translations.literal: Between these two mountains, on the southwest corner of the bank stood a lone hill; both mountains were narrow places, hence the name Shengji.
translations.idiomatic: Between the two mountains, a solitary hill rose on the southwest corner of the bank. Both peaks were pinched and narrow—hence the name Shengji, "Rising Reef."

sentences.zh: 勇門以南上便大閬，故曰成衍。

translations.literal: South of Yong Gate, going upward one immediately reached broad open country; hence the name Chengyan.
translations.idiomatic: South of Yong Gate the ascent opened at once onto broad flats—hence the name Chengyan, "Spreading Reach."

sentences.zh: 岸高測深，渚下知淺也。

translations.literal: From the high bank one gauges depth; from the islet below one knows shallowness.
translations.idiomatic: From the high bank one measures the depths; from the sandbar below one reads the shallows.

sentences.zh: 江中有孤石沉沙，隨水增減，春秋朔望，是其盛時。

translations.literal: In the river were lone stones and submerged sand, rising and falling with the water; spring and autumn, new moon and full moon—these were its peak times.
translations.idiomatic: Lone stones and sunken sandbars lay in the river, swelling and shrinking with the water. Spring and autumn, at the new moon and the full—these were the tides at their height.

sentences.zh: 故枚乘云，楚太子有疾，吳客問之，舉秋濤之美，得以瘳病。
