translations.literal: Therefore Mei Sheng says: the Crown Prince of Chu fell ill; a guest from Wu visited him and, praising the beauty of the autumn surges, cured his sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Sheng tells how the crown prince of Chu fell ill and a visitor from Wu, by extolling the splendor of the autumn tides, healed him of his affliction.

sentences.zh: 太子，國之儲貳，故曰楚貳。

translations.literal: The crown prince is the state's reserve second; hence "Chu Second."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is the state's designated second; hence the phrase "Chu Second."

sentences.zh: 河靈，河伯居河，所謂河靈。

translations.literal: The River Spirit—the River Lord dwelling in the river; this is what is meant by the River Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The River Spirit is the River Lord who dwells in the stream—this is the being called the River Spirit.

sentences.zh: 懼於海若，事見莊周《秋水篇》。〉

translations.literal: Fearful before the Lord of the Sea—the matter appears in Zhuang Zhou's "Autumn Waters."〉
translations.idiomatic: Abashed before the Lord of the Sea—the story is told in Zhuangzi's chapter "Autumn Waters."〉

sentences.zh: 爾其舊居，曩宅今園，枌□□槿尚援，基井具存。

translations.literal: As for the old dwelling—once a house, now a garden; the fen-tree [lacuna][lacuna] and hibiscus still climb in support; foundations and wells remain intact.
translations.idiomatic: The old home—yesterday's house, today's garden—where fen-tree [lacuna][lacuna] and hibiscus still twine upward; foundations and wells stand as they were.

sentences.zh: 曲術周乎前後，直陌矗其東西。

translations.literal: Winding paths encircle front and back; straight lanes rise east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Curving lanes ring it fore and aft; straight paths run east and west.

sentences.zh: 豈伊臨谿而傍沼，迺抱阜而帶山。

translations.literal: Is it not beside a stream and marsh, embracing mounds and girding mountains?
translations.idiomatic: Does it not look upon streams and marshes, embrace low hills, and belt the mountains round?

sentences.zh: 考封域之靈異，實茲境之最然。

translations.literal: Examining the numinous marvels of the enclosed domain, this borderland is indeed the foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Survey the spirit-haunted wonders of these bounds, and this country is their crown.

sentences.zh: 葺駢梁於巖麓，棲孤棟於江源。

translations.literal: Thatched paired beams at the mountain foot; a lone ridgepole dwelling at the river's source.
translations.idiomatic: Paired eaves are thatched at the mountain's foot; a solitary ridgepole stands where the river begins.

sentences.zh: 敞南戶以對遠嶺，闢東窗以矚近田。

translations.literal: Opening the south door to face distant peaks; cutting an east window to gaze upon nearby fields.
translations.idiomatic: The south door opens on distant ridges; the east window frames the fields at hand.

sentences.zh: 田連岡而盈疇，嶺枕水而通阡。

translations.literal: Fields link ridge to ridge and fill the plots; peaks rest upon water and paths connect through the paddies.
translations.idiomatic: Fields climb ridge upon ridge until the plots brim full; peaks lie along the water, and footpaths thread the paddies.

sentences.zh: 〈葺室在宅裏山之東麓。

translations.literal: 〈The thatched chamber stood on the eastern slope of Zaili Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The thatched hall stood on the eastern slope of Zaili Mountain.

sentences.zh: 東窗矚田，兼見江山之美。

translations.literal: The east window gazed upon fields, taking in together the beauty of river and mountains.
translations.idiomatic: From the east window one looked out over the fields and took in together the splendor of river and hills.

sentences.zh: 三間故謂之駢梁。

translations.literal: Three bays, hence it was called Paired Beams.
translations.idiomatic: Three bays in a row—hence the name Paired Beams.

sentences.zh: 門前一棟，枕磯上，存江之嶺，南對江上遠嶺。

translations.literal: Before the gate stood a lone ridgepole, resting upon the reef, preserving the river's ridge; southward it faced distant peaks above the river.
translations.idiomatic: Before the gate stood a solitary hall, set upon the reef, keeping the river's ridge in view; to the south it faced distant peaks along the river.

sentences.zh: 此二館屬望，殆無優劣也。〉

translations.literal: These two lodges faced each other in prospect; scarcely any difference in merit.〉
translations.idiomatic: These two halls looked out upon each other, and between them there was scarcely anything to choose.〉

sentences.zh: 阡陌縱橫，塍埒交經。

translations.literal: Footpaths run lengthwise and crosswise; field borders intersect and weave.
translations.idiomatic: Paths crisscross the land; field margins weave and cross.

sentences.zh: 導渠引流，脈散溝并。

translations.literal: Channels are led and waters drawn; veins spread and ditches merge.
translations.idiomatic: Channels guide the flow; irrigation veins branch and ditches join as one.

sentences.zh: 蔚蔚豐秫，苾苾香秔。

translations.literal: Lush, lush—the rich millet; fragrant, fragrant—the scented rice.
translations.idiomatic: Millet stands lush and full; rice breathes fragrance on every stalk.

sentences.zh: 送夏蚤秀，迎秋晚成。

translations.literal: Seeing off summer, it flowers early; greeting autumn, it ripens late.
translations.idiomatic: Before summer ends it already flowers; into autumn it ripens at leisure.

sentences.zh: 兼有陵陸，麻麥粟菽。

translations.literal: There are also uplands and lowlands: hemp, wheat, millet, and beans.
translations.idiomatic: Upland and lowland alike yield hemp, wheat, millet, and beans.

sentences.zh: 候時覘節，遞藝遞孰。

translations.literal: Watching the seasons and observing the nodes, crop follows crop and ripeness follows ripeness.
translations.idiomatic: Reading season and solar term, one crop succeeds another and harvest follows harvest.

sentences.zh: 供粒食與漿飲，謝工商與衡牧。

translations.literal: It supplies grain food and fermented drink, and dispenses with merchants, craftsmen, and market herdsmen.
translations.idiomatic: It provides grain and drink enough for the table, and makes merchants, craftsmen, and market folk unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 生何待於多資，理取足於滿腹。

translations.literal: What need has life for abundant goods? By principle, sufficiency lies in a full belly.
translations.idiomatic: What need has life for great store? Reason teaches that enough is a belly well filled.

sentences.zh: 〈許由云：「偃鼠飲河，不過滿腹。」

translations.literal: 〈Xu You said: "The mole-rat drinking from the river fills no more than its belly."
translations.idiomatic: 〈Xu You said: "When the mole-rat drinks from the river, it fills no more than its belly."

sentences.zh: 謂人生食足，則歡有餘，何待多須邪？

translations.literal: He meant that when a man's food is sufficient, joy has surplus—what need for many wants?
translations.idiomatic: He meant that once a man's food is enough, contentment overflows—what need for endless wants?

sentences.zh: 工商衡牧，似多須者，若少私寡欲，充命則足。

translations.literal: Merchants, craftsmen, and market herdsmen seem to be those with many wants; if one reduces selfishness and curbs desire, filling one's allotted span is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants, craftsmen, and market folk seem always to want more; yet with modest desires, a life lived out is enough.

sentences.zh: 但非田無以立耳。〉

translations.literal: Only without fields is there no footing at all.〉
translations.idiomatic: Only without fields can one find no footing at all.〉

sentences.zh: 自園之田，自田之湖。

translations.literal: From the garden's fields, from the fields to the lake.
translations.idiomatic: From the garden to its fields, from the fields to the lake.

sentences.zh: 氾濫川上，緬邈水區。

translations.literal: Spreading upon the river's surface, a far-reaching water realm.
translations.idiomatic: Waters spread across the river's face into a distant realm of lakes.

sentences.zh: 濬潭澗而窈窕，除菰洲之紆餘。

translations.literal: Deepening pools and stream-gorges in graceful winding; clearing the winding margins of rush islets.
translations.idiomatic: Pools and stream-gorges are dredged into graceful bends; the tangled margins of rush islets are cleared away.

sentences.zh: 毖溫泉於春流，馳寒波而秋徂。

translations.literal: Pure warm springs in the spring current; cold waves racing as autumn departs.
translations.idiomatic: Warm springs run pure in the spring flood; cold waves race away with autumn's going.

sentences.zh: 風生浪於蘭渚，日倒景於椒塗。

translations.literal: Wind raises waves at the orchid islet; the sun casts inverted shadows on the pepper path.
translations.idiomatic: Wind stirs waves at the orchid islet; the sun throws inverted light along the pepper-scented path.

sentences.zh: 飛漸榭於中沚，取水月之歡娛。

translations.literal: A soaring waterside pavilion on the mid-islet; drawing the joy of water and moon together.
translations.idiomatic: A waterside pavilion rises on the mid-islet, where one gathers the delight of water and moon together.

sentences.zh: 旦延陰而物清，夕棲芬而氣敷。

translations.literal: At dawn, shade lengthens and things grow clear; at evening, fragrance settles and qi spreads.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn shade lengthens and all grows clear; at dusk fragrance gathers and the air is sweet.

sentences.zh: 顧情交之永絕，覬雲客之暫如。

translations.literal: Turning to see friendship forever severed, hoping for cloud-wandering guests to come briefly like.
translations.idiomatic: One turns and finds old friendships forever lost, yet still hopes cloud-wandering guests may come, if only for a moment.

sentences.zh: 〈此皆湖中之美，但患言不盡意，萬不寫一耳。

translations.literal: 〈All these are beauties of the lake, but I fear words cannot exhaust meaning—not one in ten thousand is written.
translations.idiomatic: 〈These are only a few of the lake's beauties; I fear words can never say enough—not one part in ten thousand is set down here.

sentences.zh: 諸澗出源入湖，故曰濬潭澗。

translations.literal: The various stream-gorges issue from their sources and enter the lake; hence "deepening pools and stream-gorges."
translations.idiomatic: Stream-gorges rise from their sources and pour into the lake—hence the phrase "deepening pools and stream-gorges."

sentences.zh: 澗長是以窈窕。

translations.literal: The stream-gorges are long; hence the graceful winding.
translations.idiomatic: The stream-gorges run long—that is why they wind so gracefully.

sentences.zh: 除菰以作洲，言所以紆餘也。〉

translations.literal: Wild rice is cleared to shape islets—that is what is meant by "winding margins."〉
translations.idiomatic: Rush is cleared away to form islets—that is what "winding margins" refers to.〉

sentences.zh: 水草則萍藻蕰菼，雚蒲芹蓀，蒹菰蘋蘩，蕝荇菱蓮。

translations.literal: As for water plants, there are duckweed and algae, smartweed and reeds, cattails and celery and fragrant calamus, rush and wild rice, marsilea and ferns, water chestnuts, water shield, water caltrop, and lotus.
translations.idiomatic: Among the water plants are duckweed and algae, smartweed and reed, cattail and celery and calamus, rush and wild rice, marsilea and fern, water chestnut, water shield, caltrop, and lotus.

sentences.zh: 雖備物之偕美，獨扶渠之華鮮。

translations.literal: Though all things share in beauty together, only the lotus channel's blossoms are fresh and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Though every plant here has its grace, only the lotus-filled channel blooms with such vivid splendor.

sentences.zh: 播綠葉之鬱茂，含紅敷之繽翻。

translations.literal: Spreading lush green leaves, embracing red blossoms in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: Green leaves spread in dense luxuriance; red blossoms open in riotous bloom.

sentences.zh: 怨清香之難留，矜盛容之易闌。

translations.literal: It grieves that clear fragrance is hard to keep, and prides itself that full splendor fades so easily.
translations.idiomatic: It laments how swiftly clear fragrance fades, yet takes pride in how soon full splendor passes away.

sentences.zh: 必充給而後搴，豈蕙草之空殘。

translations.literal: One must wait until it is fully provided before plucking—how could it be like orchid grass left hollow and withered?
translations.idiomatic: It must be fully grown before one plucks it—unlike orchid grass, which is stripped bare and left to wither.

sentences.zh: 卷《敂弦》之逸曲，感《江南》之哀歎。

translations.literal: Collecting the leisurely melody of "Striking the Strings," moved by the mournful sigh of "Jiangnan."
translations.idiomatic: One gathers the idle strains of "Striking the Strings" and is moved by the sorrowful sigh of "Jiangnan."

sentences.zh: 秦箏倡而溯游往，《唐上》奏而舊愛還。

translations.literal: The Qin zither sings and one goes upstream in memory; "Tang Shang" is played and old love returns.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin zither sings, and memory drifts upstream; "Tang Shang" is played, and old love comes back.

sentences.zh: 〈搴出《離騷》。

translations.literal: 〈This is taken from the "Li Sao."
translations.idiomatic: 〈This passage is drawn from the "Li Sao."

sentences.zh: 《叩弦》是《采菱歌》。

translations.literal: "Striking the Strings" is the "Song of Gathering Water Chestnuts."
translations.idiomatic: "Striking the Strings" is the "Song of Gathering Water Chestnuts."

sentences.zh: 《江南》是《相和曲》，云江南採蓮。

translations.literal: "Jiangnan" is a Xianghe melody, saying "picking lotus in Jiangnan."
translations.idiomatic: "Jiangnan" is a harmonized air whose words run, "Picking lotus in Jiangnan."

sentences.zh: 秦箏倡《蒹茄篇》，《唐上》奏《蒲生》詩，皆感物致賦。

translations.literal: The Qin zheng sings "The Jianjia Chapter," and "Tang Shang" plays the "Pu Sheng" poem—all stirred by things to compose rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin zheng sings "The Jianjia Chapter," and "Tang Shang" plays the "Pu Sheng" poem—each moved by what it sees to inspire a rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 魚藻蘋繁荇亦有詩人之詠，不復具敘。〉

translations.literal: Fish, algae, duckweed, ferns, and water shield also have poets' songs—I will not narrate them all in detail.〉
translations.idiomatic: Fish, algae, duckweed, ferns, and water shield have their poets too, but I will not recount them all here.〉

sentences.zh: 《本草》所載，山澤不一。

translations.literal: What the "Ben Cao" records—mountains and marshes are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The "Ben Cao" lists many drugs, but mountain and marsh yields are not the same.

sentences.zh: 靁、桐是別，和、緩是悉。

translations.literal: Lei and Tong are the ones who distinguish; He and Huan are those who know all.
translations.idiomatic: Lei and Tong were masters of distinction; He and Huan knew every drug thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 參核六根，五華九實。

translations.literal: Paired kernels, six roots, five flowers, and nine fruits.
translations.idiomatic: There are paired kernels, six roots, five flowers, and nine fruits.

sentences.zh: 二冬竝稱而殊性，三建異形而同出。

translations.literal: The two "dong" share a name yet differ in nature; the three "jian" differ in form yet come from the same source.
translations.idiomatic: The two "dong" plants share a name but not the same nature; the three "jian" plants differ in form yet spring from one source.

sentences.zh: 水香送秋而擢蒨，林蘭近雪而揚猗。

translations.literal: Water orchid sees off autumn and lifts its crimson; forest orchid near snow spreads its fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Water orchid bids autumn farewell and lifts crimson blooms; forest orchid near the snow sends its fragrance abroad.

sentences.zh: 卷柏萬代而不殞，伏苓千歲而方知。

translations.literal: Selaginella for ten thousand generations without perishing; fu ling only recognized after a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Selaginella lives through ten thousand generations without dying; fu ling is known only after a thousand years have passed.

sentences.zh: 映紅葩於綠蔕，茂素蕤於紫枝。

translations.literal: Red blossoms mirrored on green calyxes; white tufts lush on purple branches.
translations.idiomatic: Red blossoms shine against green calyxes; white clusters flourish on purple boughs.

sentences.zh: 既住年而增靈，亦驅妖而斥疵。

translations.literal: They both prolong years and increase numinous power, and also drive away demons and expel flaws.
translations.idiomatic: They prolong life and add to one's numinous force, and they drive off evil and banish illness.

sentences.zh: 〈《本草》所出藥處，於今不復依，隨土所生耳。

translations.literal: 〈The places where the "Ben Cao" says medicines come from are no longer followed today; one simply takes what the local soil produces.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The places of origin given in the "Ben Cao" are no longer strictly followed today; one simply uses whatever grows in the local soil.

sentences.zh: 此境出藥甚多，靁公、桐君，古之採藥。

translations.literal: This region produces very many medicines; Lei Gong and Tong Jun were ancient gatherers of drugs.
translations.idiomatic: This region yields a great many drugs. Lei Gong and Tong Jun were the ancient gatherers of medicine.

sentences.zh: 醫緩，古之良工，故曰別悉。

translations.literal: Physician Huan, an ancient master craftsman—hence "distinguish and know all."
translations.idiomatic: Physician Huan was an ancient master of the art—hence the phrase "distinguish and know all."

sentences.zh: 參核者，雙核桃杏仁也。

translations.literal: "Paired kernels" are paired walnuts and almonds.
translations.idiomatic: The "paired kernels" are walnuts and almonds taken in pairs.

sentences.zh: 六根者，苟七根、五茄根、葛根、野葛根、□□根也。

translations.literal: The "six roots" are gouqi root, wuqie root, kudzu root, wild kudzu root, and [lacuna] root.
translations.idiomatic: The "six roots" are gouqi root, wuqie root, kudzu root, wild kudzu root, and [lacuna] root.

sentences.zh: 五華者，堇華、芫華、檖華、菊華、旋覆華也。

translations.literal: The "five flowers" are violet flower, daphne flower, hawthorn flower, chrysanthemum flower, and inula flower.
translations.idiomatic: The "five flowers" are violet, daphne, hawthorn, chrysanthemum, and inula blossoms.

sentences.zh: 九實者，連前實、槐實、柏實、兔絲實、女貞實、蛇床實、蔓荊實、蓼實、□□也。

translations.literal: The "nine fruits" are lotus seed, sophora fruit, cypress fruit, dodder seed, privet fruit, cnidium fruit, vitex fruit, smartweed seed, and [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: The "nine fruits" are lotus seed, sophora fruit, cypress fruit, dodder seed, privet fruit, cnidium fruit, vitex fruit, smartweed seed, and [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 二冬者，天門、麥門冬。

translations.literal: The "two dong" are asparagus root and ophiopogon root.
translations.idiomatic: The "two dong" are asparagus root and ophiopogon root.

sentences.zh: 三建者，附子、天雄、烏頭。

translations.literal: The "three jian" are aconite, tianxiong, and wutou.
translations.idiomatic: The "three jian" are aconite, tianxiong, and wutou.

sentences.zh: 水香，蘭草。

translations.literal: "Water fragrance" is orchid grass.
translations.idiomatic: "Water fragrance" is orchid grass.

sentences.zh: 林蘭，支子。

translations.literal: "Forest orchid" is gardenia.
translations.idiomatic: "Forest orchid" is gardenia.

sentences.zh: 卷柏、伏苓，並皆仙物。

translations.literal: Selaginella and fu ling are both immortal substances.
translations.idiomatic: Selaginella and fu ling are both substances of immortality.

sentences.zh: 凡此眾藥，事悉見於《神農》。〉

translations.literal: All these many medicines—their particulars are fully set out in the "Shennong Ben Cao."〉
translations.idiomatic: All these drugs are fully described in the "Shennong Ben Cao."〉

sentences.zh: 其竹則二箭殊葉，四苦齊味。

translations.literal: As for bamboo, there are two arrow types with different leaves and four bitter ones with matching flavor.
translations.idiomatic: As for bamboo, two arrow bamboos differ in leaf, and four bitter bamboos share one taste.

sentences.zh: 水石別谷，巨細各匯。

translations.literal: Water and stone bamboo in separate valleys, large and small each gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: Water bamboo and stone bamboo grow in separate valleys, and great and small kinds alike are gathered here.

sentences.zh: 既脩竦而便娟，亦蕭森而蓊蔚。

translations.literal: Both tall and slender yet graceful, and also desolate and dense.
translations.idiomatic: They stand tall and slender yet gracefully bent, desolate in their depth and lush in their crowding.

sentences.zh: 露夕沾而悽陰，風朝振而清氣。

translations.literal: Evening dew moistens them in mournful shade; morning wind stirs fresh qi.
translations.idiomatic: Evening dew leaves them dark and drenched with sorrow; morning wind shakes fresh clarity through them.

sentences.zh: 捎玄雲以拂杪，臨碧潭而挺翠。

translations.literal: Brushing dark clouds to touch the tips, overlooking green pools and thrusting up emerald.
translations.idiomatic: Their tips brush the dark clouds; above green pools they rise in jade-green splendor.

sentences.zh: 蔑上林與淇澳，驗東南之所遺。

translations.literal: Disdaining Shanglin and Qi'ao, proving what the southeast leaves behind.
translations.idiomatic: It puts Shanglin and Qi'ao to shame and proves what the southeast still preserves.

sentences.zh: 企山陽之游踐，遲鸞鷖之棲託。

translations.literal: Longing for the wanderings at Shanyang, lingering where luan and yi roost and settle.
translations.idiomatic: One longs for the wanderings at Shanyang and lingers where luan and yi birds come to roost.

sentences.zh: 憶昆園之悲調，慨伶倫之哀籥。

translations.literal: Recalling Kun Garden's mournful tune, sighing at Ling Lun's sad pipe.
translations.idiomatic: One recalls the mournful air of Kun Garden and sighs over Ling Lun's sorrowful flute.

sentences.zh: 衛女行而思歸詠，楚客放而防露作。

translations.literal: The Wei maiden traveling composes a song of longing to return; the Chu exile banished makes "Fang Lu."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei maiden, traveling far from home, sings of her longing to return; the Chu exile, cast out, composes "Fang Lu."

sentences.zh: 〈二箭，一者苦箭，大葉；

translations.literal: 〈The "two arrows": one is bitter arrow, with large leaves;
translations.idiomatic: 〈The "two arrow bamboos": one is bitter arrow, with broad leaves;

sentences.zh: 一者笄箭，細葉。

translations.literal: one is hairpin arrow, with fine leaves.
translations.idiomatic: the other is hairpin arrow, with slender leaves.

sentences.zh: 四苦，青苦、白苦、紫苦、黃苦。

translations.literal: The four bitters are green bitter, white bitter, purple bitter, and yellow bitter.
translations.idiomatic: The four bitter bamboos are green bitter, white bitter, purple bitter, and yellow bitter.

sentences.zh: 水竹，依水生，甚細密，吳中以為宅援。

translations.literal: Water bamboo grows by water, very fine and dense; in Wu it is used as trellis for houses.
translations.idiomatic: Water bamboo grows beside the water in very fine, dense clumps; in Wu it is used as latticework for dwellings.

sentences.zh: 石竹，本科叢大，以充屋榱，巨者竿挺之屬，細者無箐之流也。

translations.literal: Stone bamboo—this category grows in large clumps and is used to fill roof rafters; the large ones belong to the pole-straight kind, the small ones to the sheathless sort.
translations.idiomatic: Stone bamboo grows in thick clumps of this kind and serves to fill roof rafters; the large sort are straight poles, the small sort lack sheaths.

sentences.zh: 脩竦、便娟、蕭森、蓊蔚，皆竹貌也。

translations.literal: Tall-slender, graceful, desolate-dense, and lush—all are descriptions of bamboo's appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and slender, gracefully bent, desolate and dense, lush and crowding—all describe the look of bamboo.

sentences.zh: 上林，關中之禁苑，淇澳，衛地之竹園，方此皆不如。

translations.literal: Shanglin is the forbidden park in Guanzhong; Qi'ao is the bamboo garden in Wei's land—compared with this, none match.
translations.idiomatic: Shanglin was the imperial park in Guanzhong, and Qi'ao the bamboo grove in Wei—neither can compare with this place.

sentences.zh: 東南會稽之竹箭，唯此地最富焉。

translations.literal: The bamboo arrows of Kuaiji in the southeast—only here are they most abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Among the famed arrow bamboo of Kuaiji in the southeast, none is richer than what grows here.

sentences.zh: 山陽，竹林之游；

translations.literal: Shanyang—roaming in bamboo groves;
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang is where one roams among bamboo groves;

sentences.zh: 鸞鷖，棲食之所。

translations.literal: Luan and yi birds—the place where they nest and feed.
translations.idiomatic: the domain where egrets and herons nest and feed.

sentences.zh: 昆山之竹任為笛，黃帝時，伶倫斬其厚均者吹之，為黃鐘之宮。

translations.literal: Bamboo of Kun Mountain could serve as flutes; in the time of the Yellow Emperor, Ling Lun cut those of equal thickness and blew them, making the note of the Yellow Bell palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo from Mount Kun could be made into flutes. In the age of the Yellow Emperor, Ling Lun selected stalks of even thickness, cut them, and blew them to produce the pitch of the Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 衛女思歸，作《竹竿》之詩，楚人放逐，東方朔感江潭而作《七諫》。〉

translations.literal: A maiden of Wei, thinking of returning home, composed the poem "Bamboo Poles"; a man of Chu, exiled—Dongfang Shuo, moved by river and pool, composed the "Seven Admonitions."〉
translations.idiomatic: The Wei maiden, homesick, wrote the "Bamboo Poles"; the Chu exile Dongfang Shuo, stirred by river and marshland, wrote the "Seven Admonitions."〉

sentences.zh: 其木則松柏檀櫟，□□桐榆。

translations.literal: As for trees, there are pine, cypress, sandalwood, oak, [lacuna], paulownia, and elm.
translations.idiomatic: Its trees include pine and cypress, sandalwood and oak, [lacuna], paulownia, and elm.

sentences.zh: 檿柘穀棟，楸梓檉樗。

translations.literal: Mulberry thorn, paper mulberry, and dong; catalpa, Chinese catalpa, tamarisk, and ailanthus.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry and thorn, paper mulberry and dong tree, catalpa and Chinese catalpa, tamarisk and tree of heaven.

sentences.zh: 剛柔性異，貞脆質殊。

translations.literal: Hard and soft natures differ; steadfast and brittle qualities are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Some are hard, some soft; some steadfast, some brittle—each nature is its own.

sentences.zh: 卑高沃塉，各隨所如。

translations.literal: Low and high, fertile and thin, each according to where it goes.
translations.idiomatic: Low or high, rich soil or poor, each grows where conditions suit it.

sentences.zh: 幹合抱以隱岑，杪千仞而排虛。

translations.literal: Trunks embrace-thick to conceal peaks; treetops a thousand ren pierce the void.
translations.idiomatic: Trunks, arm-span thick, vanish into crags; crowns, a thousand ren high, thrust into the open sky.

sentences.zh: 夌岡上而喬竦，蔭澗下而扶疏。

translations.literal: Ascending ridges they tower tall; shading valleys below they spread branch and leaf.
translations.idiomatic: They rise tall atop steep ridges and cast shade in the valleys below, branches spreading in profusion.

sentences.zh: 沿長谷以傾柯，攢積石以插衢。

translations.literal: Along long valleys they lean their boughs; gathered at piled stones they insert into pathways.
translations.idiomatic: Along long valleys their boughs lean; where stones pile up, they thrust into the paths.

sentences.zh: 華映水而增光，氣結風而回敷。

translations.literal: Blossoms reflect in water and add brightness; fragrance gathers with wind and wafts about.
translations.idiomatic: Blossoms mirror the water and brighten its surface; fragrance gathers on the breeze and drifts everywhere.

sentences.zh: 當嚴勁而蔥倩，承和煦而芬腴。

translations.literal: Facing stern cold they stand fresh and lush; receiving warm harmony they grow fragrant and rich.
translations.idiomatic: In bitter cold they stand green and luxuriant; in mild warmth they grow fragrant and rich.

sentences.zh: 送墜葉於秋晏，遲含萼於春初。

translations.literal: Sending fallen leaves at autumn's close; tardily holding bud-calyx at spring's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: They shed leaves at autumn's end and tarry with bud and calyx at spring's first thaw.

sentences.zh: 〈皆木之類，選其美者載之。

translations.literal: 〈All are types of tree; the finest are selected and recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: 〈These are all kinds of trees—the finest are chosen and described here.

sentences.zh: 山脊曰岡。

translations.literal: A mountain ridge is called a gang.
translations.idiomatic: A mountain ridge is called a "gang."

sentences.zh: 岡之間下，長谷積石，各隨其方。

translations.literal: Between ridges and below, long valleys and piled stones—each according to its direction.
translations.idiomatic: Between ridges, in the lower ground, long valleys and piled stones each take their own direction.

sentences.zh: 《離騷》云：「青春受謝。

translations.literal: Encountering Sorrow says: "Spring's youth receives its farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Encountering Sorrow says: "Youth's spring accepts farewell.

sentences.zh: 白日昭只。」

translations.literal: The bright sun shines in splendor."
translations.idiomatic: The bright sun shines clear."

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「萼不韡韡」也。〉

translations.literal: The Odes says: "The calyx is not radiant," and so on.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says: "The calyx is not resplendent."〉

sentences.zh: 植物既載，動類亦繁。

translations.literal: Plants having been recorded, moving kinds are also numerous.
translations.idiomatic: With the plants already described, the animals are no less various.

sentences.zh: 飛泳騁透，胡可根源。

translations.literal: Flying, swimming, galloping, leaping—how can one trace them to a root?
translations.idiomatic: Things that fly, swim, gallop, or leap—how could one trace them all to their origins?

sentences.zh: 觀皃相音，備列山川。

translations.literal: Observing their forms and attending to their sounds, they are fully arrayed in mountain and stream.
translations.idiomatic: Observe their forms and listen to their cries—they fill the hills and waters.

sentences.zh: 寒燠順節，隨宜匪敦。

translations.literal: Cold and warmth follow the seasons; suiting conditions, not to be constrained.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and warmth follow the seasons; each thrives as nature intends, not by human rule.

sentences.zh: 〈草、木、竹，植物。

translations.literal: 〈Grass, trees, and bamboo are plants.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Grass, trees, and bamboo are plants.

sentences.zh: 魚、鳥、獸、動物。

translations.literal: Fish, birds, and beasts are animals.
translations.idiomatic: Fish, birds, and beasts are animals.

sentences.zh: 獸有數種，有騰者，有走者。

translations.literal: Beasts are of several kinds; some leap, some run.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts come in many kinds—some leap, some run.

sentences.zh: 走者騁，騰者透。

translations.literal: Runners gallop; leapers penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: Runners gallop; leapers bound.

sentences.zh: 謂種類既繁，不可根源，但觀其貌狀，相其音聲，則知山川之好。

translations.literal: This means kinds are already numerous and cannot be traced to roots; merely observe their form and appearance, attend to their calls and sounds, and one knows the goodness of mountain and stream.
translations.idiomatic: The kinds are too many to trace to a source; but observe their forms and listen to their voices, and you will know how fine these hills and waters are.

sentences.zh: 興節隨宜，自然之數，非可敦戒也。〉

translations.literal: Rising by season as conditions suit is nature's reckoning—not something to be constrained by instruction.〉
translations.idiomatic: Each season brings what it will—that is nature's way, not something commandments can enforce.〉

sentences.zh: 魚則[魚憂]鱧鮒鱮，鱒鯇鰱鯿，魴鮪魦鱖，鱨鯉鯔鱣。

translations.literal: As for fish, there are fish of a damaged name in the source, snakehead, crucian, bream, trout, grass carp, silver carp, flat bream, bream, sturgeon, sand-fish, mandarin fish, catfish, carp, mullet, and long-finned sturgeon.
translations.idiomatic: Fish include a species whose name is damaged in the text, snakehead and crucian, bream and trout, grass and silver carp, flatfish and bream, sturgeon and sand-perch, mandarin fish, catfish, carp, mullet, and long-finned sturgeon.

sentences.zh: 輯采雜色，錦爛雲鮮。

translations.literal: Gathering colors mixed, brocade-bright and cloud-fresh.
translations.idiomatic: Their mingled hues gleam like brocade, fresh as cloudlight.

sentences.zh: 唼藻戲浪，汎苻流淵。

translations.literal: Pecking at algae and sporting in waves, floating duckweed drifts in deep pools.
translations.idiomatic: They peck at algae and sport in the waves, duckweed drifting over the deep pools.

sentences.zh: 或皷鰓而湍躍，或掉尾而波旋。

translations.literal: Some beat gills and leap in rapids; some lash tails and spin in waves.
translations.idiomatic: Some flare their gills and leap in the rapids; others lash their tails and wheel through the waves.

sentences.zh: 鱸鮆乘時以入浦，鱤[魚迅]沿瀨以出泉。

translations.literal: Sea bass and sturgeon enter the inlets as seasons allow; long-finned fish of a damaged name follow rapids to emerge from springs.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bass and sturgeon enter the shallows in season; long-finned fish ride the rapids out from spring-fed pools.

sentences.zh: 〈[魚憂]音優。

translations.literal: [the cited text] is pronounced you.
translations.idiomatic: The character [the cited text] is pronounced you.

sentences.zh: 鱧音禮。

translations.literal: Snakehead (li) is pronounced li.
translations.idiomatic: Snakehead (li) is pronounced li.

sentences.zh: 鮒音附。

translations.literal: Crucian (fu) is pronounced fu.
translations.idiomatic: Crucian (fu) is pronounced fu.

sentences.zh: 鱮音敘。

translations.literal: Bream (xu) is pronounced xu.
translations.idiomatic: Bream (xu) is pronounced xu.

sentences.zh: 鱒音寸袞反。

translations.literal: Trout (zun): fanqie reading cun-gun.
translations.idiomatic: Trout (zun): fanqie reading cun-gun.

sentences.zh: 鯇音皖。

translations.literal: Grass carp (huan) is pronounced wan.
translations.idiomatic: Grass carp (huan) is pronounced wan.

sentences.zh: 鰱音連。

translations.literal: Silver carp (lian) is pronounced lian.
translations.idiomatic: Silver carp (lian) is pronounced lian.

sentences.zh: 鯿音毖仙反。

translations.literal: Flat bream (bian): fanqie reading bi-xian.
translations.idiomatic: Flat bream (bian): fanqie reading bi-xian.

sentences.zh: 魴音房。

translations.literal: Bream (fang) is pronounced fang.
translations.idiomatic: Bream (fang) is pronounced fang.

sentences.zh: 鮪音痏。

translations.literal: Sturgeon (wei) is pronounced wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sturgeon (wei) is pronounced wei.

sentences.zh: 魦音沙。

translations.literal: Sand-fish (sha) is pronounced sha.
translations.idiomatic: Sand-fish (sha) is pronounced sha.

sentences.zh: 鱖音居綴反。

translations.literal: Mandarin fish (gui): fanqie reading ju-zhui.
translations.idiomatic: Mandarin fish (gui): fanqie reading ju-zhui.

sentences.zh: 鱨音上羊反。

translations.literal: Catfish (chang): fanqie reading shang-yang.
translations.idiomatic: Catfish (chang): fanqie reading shang-yang.

sentences.zh: 鯔音比之反。

translations.literal: Mullet (zi): fanqie reading bi-zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mullet (zi): fanqie reading bi-zhi.

sentences.zh: 鱣音竹屳反。

translations.literal: Long-finned sturgeon (the cited text): fanqie reading zhu-wei.
translations.idiomatic: Long-finned sturgeon (the cited text): pronounced by fanqie zhu-wei.

sentences.zh: 皆《說文》、《字林》音。

translations.literal: All are pronunciations from the Shuowen and Zilin.
translations.idiomatic: These are all readings given in the Shuowen and Zilin.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「錦衾有爛。」

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: "The brocade coverlet has splendor."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says: "The brocade coverlet gleams.

sentences.zh: 故云錦爛。

translations.literal: Hence the phrase "brocade-bright."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the phrase "brocade-bright."

sentences.zh: 鱸鮆一時魚。

translations.literal: Sea bass and sturgeon are fish of the same season.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bass and sturgeon are seasonal fish of the same time.

sentences.zh: 鱤音感。

translations.literal: Long-finned fish (the cited text) is pronounced gan.
translations.idiomatic: The fish gan (the cited text) is pronounced gan.

sentences.zh: [魚迅]音迅。

translations.literal: [lacuna] is pronounced xun.
translations.idiomatic: [lacuna] is pronounced xun.

sentences.zh: 皆出谿中石上，恆以為翫。〉

translations.literal: All emerge from rocks in stream beds and are constantly kept as ornaments.〉
translations.idiomatic: They all come from rocks in the streams and are always kept as curiosities.〉

sentences.zh: 鳥則鵾鴻鶂鵠，鶖鷺鴇[相鳥]。

translations.literal: As for birds: kun swans, wild swans, yi birds, white swans, ospreys, egrets, bustards, and [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: Birds include kun swans, wild swans, yi birds, white swans, ospreys, egrets, bustards, and [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 雞鵲繡質，鶷鸐綬章。

translations.literal: Jiqu birds with brocade substance, xiaozhi birds with ribbon-pattern markings.
translations.idiomatic: The jiqu bird wears brocade in its plumage; the xiaozhi bird bears ribbon-like stripes.

sentences.zh: 晨鳧朝集，時鷮山梁。

translations.literal: Morning ducks gather at dawn; timely pheasants on mountain bridges.
translations.idiomatic: Wild ducks assemble at daybreak; long-tailed pheasants appear on the mountain bridge in season.

sentences.zh: 海鳥違風，朔禽避涼。

translations.literal: Sea birds defy the wind; northern birds flee the cold.
translations.idiomatic: Sea birds ride against the wind; northern birds turn away from the chill.

sentences.zh: 荑生歸北，霜降客南。

translations.literal: When grass sprouts, they return north; when frost falls, guests go south.
translations.idiomatic: When tender shoots appear, geese head north; when frost descends, they depart south as guests.

sentences.zh: 接響雲漢，侶宿江潭。

translations.literal: Echoing calls reach the River of Heaven; mates roost together by river pools.
translations.idiomatic: Their answering cries rise to the Milky Way; paired birds lodge together on the river shallows.

sentences.zh: 聆清哇以下聽，載王子而上參。

translations.literal: Listening to clear twittering below, bearing princely notes upward to Canopus.
translations.idiomatic: They listen to clear chirping below and carry noble song upward toward the stars.

sentences.zh: 薄回涉以弁翰，映明壑而自耽。

translations.literal: Skimming turns with crested plumes, reflecting in bright ravines and delighting in themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They skim and wheel on crested wings, mirrored in sunlit gorges, lost in self-admiration.

sentences.zh: 〈鵾音昆。

translations.literal: The kun bird (the cited text) is pronounced kun.
translations.idiomatic: The kun bird (the cited text) is pronounced kun.

sentences.zh: 鴻音洪。

translations.literal: Hong (wild swan) is pronounced hong.
translations.idiomatic: Hong (wild swan) is pronounced hong.

sentences.zh: 鶂音溢。

translations.literal: Yi is pronounced yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi is pronounced yi.

sentences.zh: 《左傳》云：「六鶂退飛」，字如此。

translations.literal: The Zuozhuan says: "Six yi birds flew back"—the character is written thus.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuozhuan reads, "Six yi birds flew backward"—the character is written this way.

sentences.zh: 鵠音下竺反。

translations.literal: White swan (the cited text): fanqie reading xia-zhu.
translations.idiomatic: White swan (the cited text): pronounced by fanqie xia-zhu.

sentences.zh: 鶖音秋。

translations.literal: Qiu (osprey) is pronounced qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu (osprey) is pronounced qiu.

sentences.zh: 鷺音路。

translations.literal: Lu (egret) is pronounced lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu (egret) is pronounced lu.

sentences.zh: 鴇音保。

translations.literal: Bao (bustard) is pronounced bao.
translations.idiomatic: Bao (bustard) is pronounced bao.

sentences.zh: [相鳥]音相。

translations.literal: [lacuna] is pronounced xiang.
translations.idiomatic: [lacuna] is pronounced xiang.

sentences.zh: 唐公之馬，與此鳥色同，故謂為[相鳥]，音相。

translations.literal: Duke Tang's horse had the same color as this bird, hence it is called [lacuna], pronounced xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Tang's horse was the same color as this bird, so the bird is called [lacuna], pronounced xiang.

sentences.zh: 雞鵲鶷鸐，見張茂先《博物志》。

translations.literal: The jiqu and xiaozhi birds appear in Zhang Maoxian's Browsing the Myriad Things.
translations.idiomatic: The jiqu and xiaozhi birds are recorded in Zhang Hua's Browsing the Myriad Things.

sentences.zh: 鸐音翟，亦雉之美者，此四鳥竝美采質。

translations.literal: Zhi is pronounced di; it is also a fine pheasant; these four birds all have beautiful colors and substance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi is pronounced di; it is also a fine pheasant; these four birds all have beautiful colors and substance.

sentences.zh: 鳧音符，野鴨也，常待晨而飛。

translations.literal: Fu (duck) is pronounced fu; it is the wild duck and always waits for dawn before flying.
translations.idiomatic: Fu (duck) is pronounced fu; it is the wild duck and always waits for dawn before flying.

sentences.zh: 鷮音已消反，長尾雉也。

translations.literal: Jiao: fanqie reading yi-xiao; a long-tailed pheasant.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao: fanqie reading yi-xiao; a long-tailed pheasant.

sentences.zh: 《論語》云：「山梁雌雉，時哉時哉！」

translations.literal: The Analects says: "A hen pheasant on the mountain bridge—timely! timely!"
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says: "A hen pheasant on the mountain bridge—how timely! how timely!

sentences.zh: 海鳥爰居，臧文仲不知其鳥，以為神也。

translations.literal: The sea bird Aiju—Zang Wenzhong did not know this bird and took it for a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The sea bird Aiju was unknown to Zang Wenzhong, who took it for a divine omen.

sentences.zh: 事見《左傳》。

translations.literal: The matter appears in the Zuozhuan.
translations.idiomatic: The story is recorded in the Zuozhuan.

sentences.zh: 朔禽，雁也，寒月轉往衡陽。

translations.literal: Northern birds are wild geese; in cold months they turn toward Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: "Northern birds" means wild geese; in the cold months they fly toward Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》，霜始降，雁來賓。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites: when frost first falls, geese arrive as guests.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says that when frost first descends, geese come as visiting guests.

sentences.zh: 歲莫云，雁北向。

translations.literal: At year's end it is said that geese turn north.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end people say the geese turn northward.

sentences.zh: 政是陽初生時，荑生歸北，霜降客南。

translations.literal: It is precisely when yang first rises: when grass sprouts, return north; when frost falls, guests go south.
translations.idiomatic: This marks the moment when yang first stirs: tender shoots mean heading north; frost means departing south as guests.

sentences.zh: 山雞映水自玩其羽儀者。〉

translations.literal: The mountain pheasant reflects in water, admiring its own plumage.〉
translations.idiomatic: The mountain pheasant mirrors itself in the water, delighting in its own finery.〉

sentences.zh: 山上則猨[犭軍]貍貛，犴獌猰[犭盈]。

translations.literal: On the mountains are gibbons, [lacuna], raccoon dogs, badgers, an, man, ya, and [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: In the high hills live gibbons, [lacuna], raccoon dogs, badgers, an, man, ya, and [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 山下則熊羆豺虎，羱鹿麕麖。

translations.literal: Below the mountains are bears, pandas, jackals, tigers, wild goats, muntjacs, and musk deer.
translations.idiomatic: On the lower slopes are bears and pandas, jackals and tigers, wild goats, muntjacs, and musk deer.

sentences.zh: 擲飛枝於窮崖，踔空絕於深硎。

translations.literal: They hurl flying branches from sheer cliffs and leap across voids over deep gorges.
translations.idiomatic: They cast branches from precipitous cliffs and bound across chasms over deep ravines.

sentences.zh: 蹲谷底而長嘯，攀木杪而哀鳴。

translations.literal: Crouching in valley bottoms they long howl; climbing treetops they wail in grief.
translations.idiomatic: They crouch in the valley depths and roar; they climb to the treetops and cry mournfully.

sentences.zh: 〈猨音袁。

translations.literal: 〈Yuan (gibbon) is pronounced yuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yuan (gibbon) is pronounced yuan.

sentences.zh: [犭軍]音魂。

translations.literal: [lacuna] is pronounced hun.
translations.idiomatic: [lacuna] is pronounced hun.

sentences.zh: 貍音力之反。

translations.literal: Li (raccoon dog): fanqie reading li-zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Li (raccoon dog): fanqie reading li-zhi.

sentences.zh: 貛音火丸反。

translations.literal: Huan (badger): fanqie reading huo-wan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan (badger): fanqie reading huo-wan.

sentences.zh: 犴音五懸反。

translations.literal: An: fanqie reading wu-xuan.
translations.idiomatic: An: fanqie reading wu-xuan.

sentences.zh: 獌音曼，似貛而長，狼之屬，一曰貙。

translations.literal: Man is pronounced man; it resembles the badger but is longer, belongs to the wolf kind, and is also called chou.
translations.idiomatic: Man is pronounced man; it resembles the badger but is longer, belongs to the wolf kind, and is also called chou.

sentences.zh: 猰音安黠反。

translations.literal: Ya: fanqie reading an-xia.
translations.idiomatic: Ya: fanqie reading an-xia.

sentences.zh: [犭盈]音弋生反，貍之黃黑者，一曰似[犭分]。

translations.literal: [lacuna]: fanqie reading yi-sheng; the yellow-black raccoon dog, also said to resemble [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: [lacuna]: pronounced by fanqie yi-sheng; a yellow-and-black raccoon dog, also said to resemble [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 豺音在皆反。

translations.literal: Jackal (chai): fanqie reading zai-jie.
translations.idiomatic: Jackal (chai): fanqie reading zai-jie.

sentences.zh: 羱音元，野羊大角。

translations.literal: Wild goat (yuan) is pronounced yuan; a wild sheep with large horns.
translations.idiomatic: Wild goat (yuan) is pronounced yuan; a wild sheep with large horns.

sentences.zh: 麕音鬼珉反。

translations.literal: Muntjac (jun): fanqie reading gui-min.
translations.idiomatic: Muntjac (jun): fanqie reading gui-min.

sentences.zh: 麖音京，能踔擲。

translations.literal: Elk (jing) is pronounced jing; it can leap and cast itself.
translations.idiomatic: Elk (jing) is pronounced jing; it can leap and cast itself.

sentences.zh: 虎長嘯，猿哀鳴，鳴聲可翫。〉

translations.literal: Tigers roar long; apes cry mournfully—their cries are delightful to hear.〉
translations.idiomatic: Tigers give long roars and apes cry mournfully—calls worth lingering over.〉

sentences.zh: 緡綸不投，置羅不披。

translations.literal: Fishing lines and nets are not cast; snares are not spread.
translations.idiomatic: He casts neither line nor net, nor spreads any snare.

sentences.zh: 磻弋靡用，蹄筌誰施。

translations.literal: Neither bow nor arrow is used; who would set out deer snares or fish traps?
translations.idiomatic: Bow and retrieving arrow lie idle—who would deploy snares or fish baskets?

sentences.zh: 鑒虎狼之有仁，傷遂欲之無崖。

translations.literal: Reflecting that tigers and wolves have benevolence, grieving that unchecked desire has no limit.
translations.idiomatic: He sees that even tigers and wolves know kinship, and grieves that indulged desire knows no bound.

sentences.zh: 顧弱齡而涉道，悟好生之咸宜。

translations.literal: Looking back on youth when he entered the Way, he realized that cherishing life suits all alike.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling the path he took from youth, he grasped that love of life befits every living thing.

sentences.zh: 率所由以及物，諒不遠之在斯。

translations.literal: Leading from what one follows to extend to other things—I trust that 'not going far to return' lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Extend from one's own path to all things—I believe 'returning without going far' is found in this.

sentences.zh: 撫鷗[魚攸]而悅豫，杜機心於林池。

translations.literal: Stroking gulls and fish of a damaged name in contentment, shutting out scheming minds in woods and ponds.
translations.idiomatic: He strokes gulls and water birds in easy delight, barring crafty intent from grove and pool.

sentences.zh: 〈八種皆是魚獵之具。

translations.literal: 〈All eight kinds are tools for fishing and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: 〈These eight items are all gear for fishing and the chase.

sentences.zh: 自少不殺，至乎白首，故在山中，而此歡永廢。

translations.literal: From youth he did not kill; until white-haired old age—therefore in the mountains this pleasure is forever abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He has not taken life since boyhood, even to hoary age—so in these hills that sport is forever laid aside.

sentences.zh: 莊周云，虎狼仁獸，豈不父子相親。

translations.literal: Zhuangzi says: 'Tigers and wolves are benevolent beasts—do they not love kinship between father and son?'
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi wrote that tigers and wolves are 'benevolent beasts'—do they not cherish bond between sire and offspring?

sentences.zh: 世云虎狼暴虐者，政以其如禽獸，而人物不自悟其毒害，而言虎狼可疾之甚，苟其遂欲，豈復崖限。

translations.literal: The world calls tigers and wolves brutal, precisely because, like beasts, people do not themselves realize their own harm and speak of tigers and wolves as objects of extreme hatred; yet if desire runs its course, what limit remains?
translations.idiomatic: Men call tigers and wolves cruel only because, no wiser than beasts, they fail to see their own poison and reserve their fiercest hatred for wolf and tiger—yet when appetite runs free, what shore can hold it?

sentences.zh: 自弱齡奉法，故得免殺生之事。

translations.literal: From youth he observed the precepts, and so was spared deeds of taking life.
translations.idiomatic: From early years he kept the prohibitions, and so was kept from killing.

sentences.zh: 苟此悟萬物好生之理。

translations.literal: If through this one realizes the principle that all things love life—
translations.idiomatic: Once one sees through this that every creature loves life—

sentences.zh: 《易》云：「不遠復，無祇悔。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: 'Returning without going far—no great regret.'
translations.idiomatic: The Yijing says: 'Return, and do not go far—no deep remorse.'

sentences.zh: 庶乘此得以入道。

translations.literal: One may hope by this to enter the Way.
translations.idiomatic: —one may hope by this to enter the Way.

sentences.zh: 莊周云，海人有機心，鷗鳥舞而不下。

translations.literal: Zhuangzi says: 'When a man of the sea harbors a scheming mind, gulls dance but will not alight.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi says that when a seafarer keeps a calculating heart, gulls wheel in the air but refuse to come down.

sentences.zh: 今無害彼之心，各說豫於林池也。〉

translations.literal: Now, with no mind to harm them, each finds contentment in woods and ponds.〉
translations.idiomatic: Now, with no intent to harm them, each finds ease in grove and pool.〉

sentences.zh: 敬承聖誥，恭窺前經。

translations.literal: Reverently receiving the sage's edicts, respectfully perusing the scriptures of old.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently I receive the holy injunctions and humbly pore over the scriptures of old.

sentences.zh: 山野昭曠，聚落羶腥。

translations.literal: Mountains and wilds are open and bright; settlements are rank with slaughter and blood.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and wilderness lie open and clear; towns reek of blood and butchery.

sentences.zh: 故大慈之弘誓，拯群物之淪傾。

translations.literal: Therefore the great vow of great compassion rescues all beings from ruin and collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the vast vow of great compassion, to lift all beings from ruin and fall.

sentences.zh: 豈寓地而空言，必有貸以善成。

translations.literal: How could it dwell only in empty words on this earth? There must be lending to bring goodness to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Surely compassion is not mere words on earth—there must be grace lent to bring good to fruition.

sentences.zh: 欽鹿野之華苑，羨靈鷲之名山。

translations.literal: I revere the splendid garden of the Deer Park; I envy the famous mountain of Vulture Peak.
translations.idiomatic: I honor the splendid deer park where the truth was first spoken; I long for Vulture Peak, that mountain of renown.

sentences.zh: 企堅固之貞林，希菴羅之芳園。

translations.literal: I long for the steadfast pure grove; I hope for the fragrant garden of Amra.
translations.idiomatic: I aspire to the steadfast grove of purity; I yearn for Amra's fragrant garden.

sentences.zh: 雖綷容之緬邈，謂哀音之恆存。

translations.literal: Though splendor is distant and remote, I believe the plaintive teaching sound ever abides.
translations.idiomatic: Though that splendor lies far off, I trust the mournful Dharma-voice still endures.

sentences.zh: 建招提於幽峰，冀振錫之息肩。

translations.literal: Build monasteries on secluded peaks; hope that those who shake their staffs may rest their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: Raise chapels on hidden peaks, hoping wandering monks may here set down their burdens.

sentences.zh: 庶鐙王之贈席，想香積之惠餐。

translations.literal: Perhaps receive the Lamp King's gift of a seat; think of the fragrant meal from the Realm of Accumulated Fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps to share the Lamp King's offered seat, or taste the blessed meal of Fragrant Accumulation.

sentences.zh: 事在微而思通，理匪絕而可溫。

translations.literal: Affairs lie in the subtle yet thought can penetrate; principle is not severed but may be warmed anew.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is slight, yet mind may pierce it; truth is never cut off, only waiting to be warmed again.

sentences.zh: 〈賈誼《弔屈》云：「恭承嘉惠。」

translations.literal: 〈Jia Yi's 'Lament for Qu Yuan' says: 'Respectfully receiving your gracious favor.'
translations.idiomatic: 〈In Jia Yi's Lament for Qu Yuan we read: 'I respectfully receive your gracious gift.'

sentences.zh: 敬承，亦此之流。

translations.literal: Reverently receiving' is of this same kind.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently receiving' belongs to the same turn of phrase.

sentences.zh: 聚落是墟邑，謂歌哭諍訟，有諸諠譁，不及山野為僧居止也。

translations.literal: Settlements are market towns—meaning singing, weeping, lawsuits, and all kinds of clamor; they are not as suited for monks to dwell in as mountains and wilds.
translations.idiomatic: By 'settlements' he means market towns—singing, mourning, quarrels, and every kind of noise—ill suited to monastic life compared with mountain wilds.

sentences.zh: 經教欲令在山中，皆有成文。

translations.literal: The canonical teachings all wish one to dwell in the mountains—there are authoritative texts on this throughout.
translations.idiomatic: The sutras everywhere enjoin dwelling in the hills; the written teachings on this are ample.

sentences.zh: 老子云：「善貸且善成。」

translations.literal: Laozi says: 'Good at lending and good at completing.'
translations.idiomatic: Laozi says: 'Skilled at lending, and skilled at bringing to completion.'

sentences.zh: 此道惠物也。

translations.literal: This Way benefits all things.
translations.idiomatic: This is the Way that nourishes all beings.

sentences.zh: 鹿苑，說《四真諦》處。

translations.literal: The Deer Park—where the Four Noble Truths were preached.
translations.idiomatic: The Deer Park—where the Four Noble Truths were taught.

sentences.zh: 靈鷲山，說《般若法華》處。

translations.literal: Vulture Peak—where the Prajna and Lotus Sutras were preached.
translations.idiomatic: Vulture Peak—where the Prajna and Lotus Sutras were expounded.

sentences.zh: 堅固林，說泥洹處。

translations.literal: The Steadfast Grove—where nirvana was preached.
translations.idiomatic: The Steadfast Grove—where nirvana was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 菴羅園，說不思議處。

translations.literal: The Amra Garden—where the inconceivable was preached.
translations.idiomatic: The Amra Garden—where the inconceivable was revealed.

sentences.zh: 今旁林藝園制苑，仿佛在昔，依然託想，雖綷容緬邈，哀音若存也。

translations.literal: Now, with groves and cultivated gardens fashioned like parks on every side, as if recalling times past, still entrusting one's thoughts to them—though splendor is distant and remote, the plaintive teaching seems still to abide.
translations.idiomatic: Now he lays out groves and ordered gardens in their likeness; though memory stretches far back and splendor is remote, the sorrowful teaching-voice seems still near.

sentences.zh: 招提，謂僧不能常住者，可持作坐處也。

translations.literal: 'Monastery' means that for monks who cannot dwell permanently, one may establish a place to sit and rest.
translations.idiomatic: Chatiya denotes a resting place set up for monks who cannot stay long in one spot.

sentences.zh: 所謂息肩。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by 'resting one's shoulders.'
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by 'easing the shoulders.'

sentences.zh: 鐙王、香積，事出《維摩經》。

translations.literal: The Lamp King and Accumulated Fragrance—these matters come from the Vimalakirti Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: The Lamp King and Fragrant Accumulation—accounts drawn from the Vimalakirti Sutra.

sentences.zh: 《論語》云：「溫故知新。」

translations.literal: The Analects says: 'Review the old and know the new.'
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says: 'Warm what is old and know what is new.'

sentences.zh: 理既不絕，更宜復溫，則可待為己之日用也。〉

translations.literal: Since principle is not severed, one should warm it again—then it may await one as daily use.〉
translations.idiomatic: Truth is never broken off; go over it again and it becomes one's daily bread.〉

sentences.zh: 爰初經略，杖策孤征。

translations.literal: At first when surveying the terrain, staff in hand he traveled alone.
translations.idiomatic: When first he explored the land, he went alone, staff in hand.

sentences.zh: 入澗水涉，登嶺山行。

translations.literal: Entering streams and wading through water, climbing ridges and walking the heights.
translations.idiomatic: He waded stream beds and crossed waters, climbed ridges and walked the high trails.

sentences.zh: 陵頂不息，窮泉不停。

translations.literal: Mounting summits without cease, reaching deep springs without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: He scaled peaks without rest and would not halt at the deepest springs.

sentences.zh: 櫛風沐雨，犯露乘星。

translations.literal: Combed by wind and bathed by rain; encountering dew and riding the stars.
translations.idiomatic: Wind-combed and rain-bathed, he braved the dew and traveled by starlight.

sentences.zh: 研其淺思，罄其短規。

translations.literal: He polished his shallow thoughts and exhausted his short plans.
translations.idiomatic: He tested his modest ideas and spent every bit of his limited design.

sentences.zh: 非龜非筮，擇良選奇。

translations.literal: Neither turtle nor milfoil divination; choosing the good and selecting the extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Without turtle shells or milfoil omens, he chose the finest and most remarkable sites.

sentences.zh: 翦榛開徑，尋石覓崖。

translations.literal: Cut brambles and opened paths; sought stones and searched out cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared brush to open trails and searched out rocks and cliff faces.

sentences.zh: 四山周回，雙流逶迤。

translations.literal: Four mountains encircled all around; twin streams wound far away.
translations.idiomatic: Four mountains ringed the scene; two streams meandered away.

sentences.zh: 面南嶺，建經臺；

translations.literal: Facing the southern ridge, he built a sutra platform;
translations.idiomatic: Facing the southern ridge, he raised a platform for the scriptures;

sentences.zh: 倚北阜，築講堂。

translations.literal: Leaning against the northern mound, he constructed a lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: Against the northern hill he built a hall for teaching.

sentences.zh: 傍危峰，立禪室；

translations.literal: Beside perilous peaks, he erected a meditation chamber;
translations.idiomatic: Beside sheer peaks he set up a meditation cell;

sentences.zh: 臨浚流，列僧房。

translations.literal: Overlooking deep-flowing waters, he arranged the monks' quarters in a row.
translations.idiomatic: Overlooking the deep stream, he lined up the monks' quarters.

sentences.zh: 對百年之高木，納萬代之芬芳。

translations.literal: Facing century-old lofty trees, receiving the fragrance of ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He faced towering trees of a hundred years and drew in fragrance lasting ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 抱終古之泉源，美膏液之清長。

translations.literal: Embracing primordial spring sources, admiring the clear abundance of their rich waters.
translations.idiomatic: He held fast to springs ancient as time, savoring their pure, abundant flow.

sentences.zh: 謝麗塔於郊郭，殊世間於城傍。

translations.literal: He declined ornate pagodas in the outer suburbs and kept apart from the worldly beside the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: He forswore splendid pagodas in the outer suburbs and kept apart from the bustle at the city wall.

sentences.zh: 欣見素以抱樸，果甘露於道場。

translations.literal: Rejoicing in plainness and embracing simplicity, he attained sweet dew at the Dharma field.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in plain sincerity and simple integrity, and reaped heaven's sweet dew upon his sacred ground.

sentences.zh: 〈云初經略，躬自履行，備諸苦辛也。

translations.literal: 〈It says: when first surveying the terrain, he personally carried it out, embracing every hardship.
translations.idiomatic: 〈This means that when he first explored the site, he went himself and endured every hardship.

sentences.zh: 罄其淺短，無假於龜筮，貧者既不以麗為美，所以即安茅茨而已。

translations.literal: He exhausted his shallow shortcoming; without relying on turtle and milfoil divination; since the poor do not take splendor as beauty, he therefore settled for thatched huts alone.
translations.idiomatic: He gave all he had though his means were slight and asked no omen of turtle or milfoil; the poor cannot afford magnificence, so he was content with simple thatched dwellings.

sentences.zh: 是以謝郊郭而殊城傍。

translations.literal: Therefore he declined the outer suburbs and kept apart from beside the city.
translations.idiomatic: That is why he turned from the suburbs and kept his distance from the city wall.

sentences.zh: 然清虛寂寞，實是得道之所也。〉

translations.literal: Yet purity, emptiness, and solitude are truly the place where the Way is attained.〉
translations.idiomatic: Yet clarity, emptiness, and quiet are truly where one may attain the Way.〉

sentences.zh: 苦節之僧，明發懷抱。

translations.literal: Monks of bitter discipline, at dawn opening their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Monks of stern austerity, who at daybreak reveal their deepest resolve.

sentences.zh: 事紹人徒，心通世表。

translations.literal: In affairs continuing the lineage of the teacher; in mind penetrating beyond the world.
translations.idiomatic: They carry on their master's line in deed, yet their hearts reach beyond the world's bounds.

sentences.zh: 是遊是憩，倚石構草。

translations.literal: Whether traveling or resting, leaning on stone and building with grass.
translations.idiomatic: Whether roaming or at rest, they lean on rock and roof themselves with grass.

sentences.zh: 寒暑有移，至業莫矯。

translations.literal: Cold and heat shift and change; supreme practice is never altered.
translations.idiomatic: Seasons turn from cold to heat, yet their highest calling never wavers.

sentences.zh: 觀三世以其夢，撫六度以取道。

translations.literal: Viewing the three ages as dreams; stroking the six perfections to take the Way.
translations.idiomatic: They see the three ages as a dream and tread the Way through the six perfections.

sentences.zh: 乘恬知以寂泊，含和理之窈窕。

translations.literal: Riding tranquil knowledge in still calm; embracing harmonious principle in hidden depth.
translations.idiomatic: They dwell in tranquil insight and still repose, holding within them the hidden harmony of truth.

sentences.zh: 指東山以冥期，實西方之潛兆。

translations.literal: Pointing to the Eastern Peak as a dim expectation; in truth a hidden sign of the Western Pure Land.
translations.idiomatic: They set their secret hope on Mount Dong, which in truth foretells rebirth in the Western Paradise.

sentences.zh: 雖一日以千載，猶恨相遇之不早。

translations.literal: Though one day is reckoned as a thousand years, still they regret that the meeting was not sooner.
translations.idiomatic: Though a single day seems a thousand years, they still rue that they did not meet sooner.

sentences.zh: 〈謂曇隆、法流二法師也。

translations.literal: 〈This refers to the two Dharma masters Tanlong and Faliu.
translations.idiomatic: 〈This refers to the two masters Tanlong and Faliu.

sentences.zh: 二公辭恩愛，棄妻子，輕舉入山，外緣都絕，魚肉不入口，糞掃必在體，物見之絕歎，而法師處之夷然。

translations.literal: The two lords renounced affection, abandoned wives and children, lightly entered the mountains, cut off all external ties, did not let fish or meat pass their lips, wore only refuse-sweepings on their bodies; creatures who saw them sighed in wonder, yet the Dharma masters bore it with composure.
translations.idiomatic: Both men renounced earthly love, left wives and children, and lightly took to the hills, severing every outer tie. No fish or flesh crossed their lips; they wore only cast-off rags. Beasts that saw them marveled, yet the masters remained utterly unmoved.

sentences.zh: 詩人西發不勝造道者，其亦如此。

translations.literal: The poet who set out westward, unable to bear not attaining the Way—these men were much the same.
translations.idiomatic: Like the poet who set out westward, unable to rest until he found the Way, they were no different.

sentences.zh: 往石門瀑布中路高棲之游，昔告離之始。

translations.literal: On a former journey of lofty dwelling midway at the Stone Gate waterfall, at the beginning when he first told of parting.
translations.idiomatic: On an earlier retreat midway at the Stone Gate waterfall, when he first spoke of leaving them behind.

sentences.zh: 期生東山，沒存西方。

translations.literal: They hoped to be born on the Eastern Peak and that at death they would abide in the West.
translations.idiomatic: They hoped to be reborn on Mount Dong and at death to find rest in the West.

sentences.zh: 相遇之欣，實以一日為千載，猶慨恨不早。〉

translations.literal: The joy of meeting—truly taking one day as a thousand years—still stirred regret that it was not sooner.〉
translations.idiomatic: The joy of their meeting made a single day feel like a thousand years, yet still they grieved that it had not come sooner.〉

sentences.zh: 賤物重己，棄世希靈。

translations.literal: Valuing self above things, abandoning the world and hoping for the numinous.
translations.idiomatic: They scorned worldly goods and prized their own souls, forsaking the world to seek the spirit.

sentences.zh: 駭彼促年，愛是長生。

translations.literal: Shocked by that brief span of years, they loved this long life.
translations.idiomatic: Appalled by life's short span, they cherished the promise of longevity.

sentences.zh: 冀浮丘之誘接，望安期之招迎。

translations.literal: Hoping for Lord Floating Hill's guidance and reception; looking for Master Anqi's summons and welcome.
translations.idiomatic: They longed for Lord Fuqiu to lead them onward and hoped Master Anqi would come to greet them.

sentences.zh: 甘松桂之苦味，夷皮褐以頹形。

translations.literal: Sweet were pine and cassia's bitter flavors; they wore plain skins and hemp until their forms withered.
translations.idiomatic: They savored the bitter taste of pine and cassia and wore coarse hides and hemp until their bodies wasted away.

sentences.zh: 羨蟬蛻之匪日，撫雲蜺其若驚。

translations.literal: Envious of the cicada's casting off its shell—not in a day; stroking cloud-rainbows as if startled.
translations.idiomatic: They envied the cicada's quick sloughing of its shell and trembled at the touch of rainbow clouds.

sentences.zh: 陵名山而屢憩，過巖室而披情。

translations.literal: Crossing famous mountains and often resting; passing rock chambers and laying bare their feelings.
translations.idiomatic: They scaled famous peaks and often paused to rest, and in cliffside caves laid bare their inmost hearts.

sentences.zh: 雖未階於至道，且緬絕於世纓。

translations.literal: Though they had not yet ascended to the ultimate Way, they had already cast off the world's tethering ties from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Though they had not yet reached the highest Way, they had already snapped the world's entangling cords.

sentences.zh: 指松菌而興言，良未齊於殤彭。

translations.literal: Pointing to pine fungus they spoke; truly they had not yet equaled Shang Zai and Peng Zu.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of pine fungus and longevity, they knew they still fell short of even Shang Zai and Peng Zu.

sentences.zh: 〈此一章敘仙學者雖未及佛道之高，然出於世表矣。

translations.literal: 〈This section relates that though students of immortality have not reached the height of the Buddhist Way, they yet rise above the world's surface.
translations.idiomatic: 〈This passage tells how seekers of immortality, though not risen to the Buddhist Way's summit, have already stepped beyond the world.

sentences.zh: 浮丘公是王子喬師，安期先生是馬明生師，二事出《列仙傳》。

translations.literal: Lord Floating Hill was Master Wang Ziqiao's teacher; Master Anqi was Master Ma Mingsheng's teacher; both accounts come from the Biographies of Arrayed Immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Fuqiu was teacher to Wang Ziqiao; Master Anqi was teacher to Ma Mingsheng—both stories come from the Biographies of Arrayed Immortals.

sentences.zh: 《洞直經》云：「今學仙者亦明師以自發悟，故不辭苦味頹形也。」

translations.literal: The Scripture of Straightness in the Grotto says: "Today those who study immortality also rely on a clear teacher for self-enlightenment; therefore they do not decline bitter flavors or withered forms."
translations.idiomatic: The Scripture of Straightness in the Grotto says: "Students of immortality today also need an enlightened master to awaken them—hence they do not shrink from bitter herbs or wasted flesh."

sentences.zh: 莊周云：「和以天兒。」

translations.literal: Zhuang Zhou says: "Harmonize with heaven's cliff."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi says: "Harmonize with heaven's heights."

sentences.zh: 兒者，崖也。

translations.literal: "Cliff" (the particle pronounced ér) means a precipice.
translations.idiomatic: Here the particle pronounced ér means a cliff face.

sentences.zh: 數經歷名山，遇余巖室，披露其情性，且獲長生。

translations.literal: Repeatedly traversing famous mountains, encountering cliff chambers, laying bare their dispositions, and moreover attaining long life.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again they crossed famous peaks, found caverns in the cliffs, revealed their inmost nature, and so won long life.

sentences.zh: 方之松菌殤彭，邈然有間也。〉

translations.literal: Compared with pine fungus, Shang Zai, and Peng Zu, there is still a vast gap.〉
translations.idiomatic: Compared with pine fungus or the lifespans of Shang Zai and Peng Zu, the distance remains immense.〉

sentences.zh: 山作水役，不以一牧。

translations.literal: Mountains perform water's tasks; one cannot rely on a single overseer.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains serve the waters' needs—you cannot put one man in charge of it all.

sentences.zh: 資待各徒，隨節競逐。

translations.literal: Supplies and needs—each group has its followers; according to season they compete in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Each kind of provision has its own crew, who vie with the seasons to gather what is needed.

sentences.zh: 陟嶺刊木，除榛伐竹。

translations.literal: Ascending ridges to cut timber, clearing brambles and felling bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: They climb the ridges to hew timber, clear thorn brush, and cut bamboo.

sentences.zh: 抽筍自篁，擿篛于谷。

translations.literal: Pulling shoots from bamboo groves, plucking rush leaves in the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: They pull young shoots from the bamboo groves and pick rush leaves in the valleys.

sentences.zh: 揚勝所拮，秋冬[艹片畐]獲。

translations.literal: They gather carambola where it excels, and in autumn and winter [lacuna] the harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Where carambola thrives they pluck it, and when autumn turns to winter they store the gathered yield.

sentences.zh: 野有蔓草，獵涉蘡薁。

translations.literal: In the wild are creeping grasses; wading through them one gathers wild grapes.
translations.idiomatic: Creepers spread through the wild, and by wading among them one collects wild grapes.

sentences.zh: 亦醖山清，介爾景福。

translations.literal: They also brew clear mountain wine, and may great blessing be granted you.
translations.idiomatic: They brew clear mountain wine as well, and may great blessing be yours.

sentences.zh: 苦以朮成，甘以[扌審]熟。

translations.literal: Bitterness is made from atractylodes wine; sweetness is ripened from [lacuna] wine.
translations.idiomatic: Bitterness comes from atractylodes wine, sweetness from [lacuna] wine matured to perfection.

sentences.zh: 慕椹高林，剝芨巖椒。

translations.literal: In the tall forest they make mu from bark; on cliff-side zanthoxylum they peel paper-mulberry bark.
translations.idiomatic: In the high woods they strip bark for mu, and on cliff-side zanthoxylum they peel paper-mulberry for paper.

sentences.zh: 掘蒨陽崖，擿[扌鮮]陰摽。

translations.literal: On sunny cliffs they dig madder; from shady heights they pick [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: On sunlit cliffs they dig madder, and from shaded heights they gather [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 晝見搴茅，宵見索綯。

translations.literal: By day one sees them pulling thatch; by night, seeking rope.
translations.idiomatic: By day they pull thatch; by night they hunt for cord.

sentences.zh: 芟菰翦蒲，以薦以茭。

translations.literal: They cut wild rice and trim cattails—for mats and for edible shoots.
translations.idiomatic: They mow wild rice and trim cattails, for mats and for edible shoots.

sentences.zh: 既坭既埏，品收不一。

translations.literal: Both raw clay and fired pottery—the kinds gathered are not alike.
translations.idiomatic: Raw clay and fired ware alike—what is gathered comes in many kinds.

sentences.zh: 其灰其炭，咸各有律。

translations.literal: Ashes and charcoal each have their proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Ashes and charcoal, too, each follow their own season.

sentences.zh: 六月采蜜，八月樸栗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they gather honey; in the eighth they strip chestnuts.
translations.idiomatic: Honey is gathered in the sixth month, chestnuts stripped in the eighth.

sentences.zh: 備物為繁，略載靡悉。

translations.literal: Provisions are many; what is briefly recorded is not complete.
translations.idiomatic: The store of goods is vast, and this brief account cannot exhaust it.

sentences.zh: 〈此一章謂山水採拾諸事也。

translations.literal: 〈This section describes the gathering of things from mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: 〈This section treats the gathering of produce from mountain and stream.

sentences.zh: 然漁獵之事皆不載。

translations.literal: Hunting and fishing activities, however, are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Fishing and hunting, however, are not included.

sentences.zh: 楊，楊桃也。

translations.literal: Yang means carambola.
translations.idiomatic: Yang refers to carambola.

sentences.zh: 山間謂之木子。

translations.literal: In the mountains it is called muzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the hills it is called muzi.

sentences.zh: [艹片畐]音覆，字出《字林》。

translations.literal: [lacuna] is pronounced fu; the character comes from the Zilin.
translations.idiomatic: [lacuna] is read fu; the character appears in the Zilin.

sentences.zh: 詩人云：「六月食鬱及薁。」

translations.literal: The poet says: "In the sixth month we eat yu and ao."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says: "In the sixth month we eat yu and ao."

sentences.zh: 獵涉字出《爾雅》。

translations.literal: The word lie she comes from the Erya.
translations.idiomatic: The term lie she comes from the Erya.

sentences.zh: 術，術酒，味苦。

translations.literal: Shu is atractylodes wine; its flavor is bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is atractylodes wine, and it tastes bitter.

sentences.zh: [扌審]，[扌審]酒，味甘，竝至美，兼以療病。

translations.literal: [lacuna] is [lacuna] wine; its flavor is sweet. Both are exquisite and also used to treat illness.
translations.idiomatic: A plant name lost in the text yields a wine, sweet to the taste; both are superb and also serve as medicine.

sentences.zh: [扌審]治癰核，術治痰冷。

translations.literal: [lacuna] treats carbuncles and nodules; shu treats cold phlegm.
translations.idiomatic: That plant cures abscesses and hard swellings; shu cures cold phlegm.

sentences.zh: 椹音甚，味似菰菜而勝，刊木而作之，謂之慕。

translations.literal: Shen is pronounced shen; its flavor resembles wild rice shoots but is superior. Bark is stripped from trees to make it, and this is called mu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen is read shen; it tastes like wild rice shoots but finer. Bark is cut from trees to prepare it, and this dish is called mu.

sentences.zh: 芨音及，採以為紙。

translations.literal: Ji is pronounced ji; it is gathered to make paper.
translations.idiomatic: Ji is read ji; it is collected for papermaking.

sentences.zh: 蒨音倩，採以為渫。

translations.literal: Qian is pronounced qian; it is gathered to make dye.
translations.idiomatic: Qian is read qian; it is gathered to make dye.

sentences.zh: [扌鮮]音鮮，採以為飲。

translations.literal: [lacuna] is pronounced xian; it is gathered to make a drink.
translations.idiomatic: [lacuna] is read xian; it is gathered for brewing.

sentences.zh: 采蜜樸栗，各隨其月也。〉

translations.literal: Gathering honey and stripping chestnuts each follows its proper month.〉
translations.idiomatic: Honey-gathering and chestnut-stripping each keep to its own month.〉

sentences.zh: 若乃南北兩居，水通陸阻。

translations.literal: Now there are dwellings north and south; water connects them while land blocks the way.
translations.idiomatic: There are two dwellings, north and south: water links them, but land stands in the way.

sentences.zh: 觀風瞻雲，方知厥所。

translations.literal: Only when one watches the wind and gazes at the clouds does one learn where they lie.
translations.idiomatic: Only by watching wind and cloud does one learn where each lies.

sentences.zh: 〈兩居謂南北兩處，各有居止。

translations.literal: 〈The two dwellings mean two places, north and south, each with its own residence.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The two dwellings are the northern and southern sites, each with its own home.

sentences.zh: 峰崿阻絕，水道通耳。

translations.literal: Peaks and cliffs block the way; only the waterways connect.
translations.idiomatic: Peaks and cliffs cut off the land; only the watercourses link the two.

sentences.zh: 觀風瞻雲，然後方知其處所。〉

translations.literal: Only when one watches the wind and gazes at the clouds does one finally learn their locations.〉
translations.idiomatic: Only by reading wind and cloud can one finally tell where each stands.〉

sentences.zh: 南山則夾渠二田，周嶺三苑。

translations.literal: To the south, two fields flank the channels; three gardens ring the ridges.
translations.idiomatic: To the south, two fields lie between the channels, and three gardens encircle the ridges.

sentences.zh: 九泉別澗，五谷異巘。

translations.literal: Nine springs each form separate streams; the five grains grow on different slopes.
translations.idiomatic: Nine springs branch into separate brooks, and the five grains ripen on different hillsides.

sentences.zh: 群峰參差出其間，連岫椱陸成其阪。

translations.literal: Peaks rise irregularly among them; linked ranges overlay the flatlands to form their slopes.
translations.idiomatic: Peaks rise in uneven ranks among them, and linked ridges spread over the flats to shape the slopes.

sentences.zh: 眾流溉灌以環近，諸堤擁抑以接遠。

translations.literal: Many streams irrigate and encircle what is near; embankments check and channel them to reach what is far.
translations.idiomatic: Many streams irrigate and ring what lies near, while dikes restrain and carry the water to what lies far.

sentences.zh: 遠堤兼陌，近流開湍。

translations.literal: Distant dikes run alongside paths; nearby currents break into rapids.
translations.idiomatic: Far-off dikes run beside the paths; nearby currents burst into rapids.

sentences.zh: 淩阜泛波，水往步還。

translations.literal: Banks surmount the mounds as waves spread; one walks out with the water and returns with it.
translations.idiomatic: Banks rise over the mounds as waves spread; you walk out with the water and walk back with it.

sentences.zh: 還回往匝，枉渚員巒。

translations.literal: Round and back, turning and circling; bent islets and rounded peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Waters wheel and return, winding round and round; crooked islets and rounded peaks.

sentences.zh: 呈美表趣，胡可勝單。

translations.literal: Such beauty and charm displayed—how could one exhaust them in a list?
translations.idiomatic: Such beauty and charm on display—how could a single account exhaust them?

sentences.zh: 杭北頂以葺館，殷南峰以啟軒。

translations.literal: Thatched lodges roof the northern summit; south-facing halls open their windows toward the southern peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Lodges are thatched against the northern summit, and halls open their windows toward the southern peaks.

sentences.zh: 羅曾崖於戶裏，列鏡瀾於窗前。

translations.literal: Layered cliff faces are arrayed within the doorway; mirror-bright waters are lined up before the window.
translations.idiomatic: Tier upon tier of cliffs stand framed in the doorway; mirror-bright waters are ranged before the window.

sentences.zh: 因丹霞以赬楣，附碧雲以翠椽。

translations.literal: With red clouds for vermilion lintels, with azure clouds for green rafters.
translations.idiomatic: Red clouds serve as vermilion lintels, azure clouds as green rafters.

sentences.zh: 視奔星之俯馳，顧□□之未牽。

translations.literal: Gazing at shooting stars plunging past overhead, looking back at [lacuna] not yet tethered.
translations.idiomatic: One watches shooting stars plunge overhead, and looks back on [lacuna] not yet bound.

sentences.zh: 鵾鴻翻翥而莫及，何但燕雀之翩翾。

translations.literal: Great swans wheel upward beyond reach—how much more so the fluttering of swallows and sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: Great swans wheel upward beyond reach—how much more the darting flight of swallows and sparrows.

sentences.zh: 氿泉傍出，潺湲於東簷；

translations.literal: Side springs gush forth, murmuring along the eastern eaves;
translations.idiomatic: Side springs break out and murmur along the eastern eaves;

sentences.zh: 桀壁對歭，硿礲於西霤。
