translations.literal: Towering cliffs face each other upright, thundering at the western eaves-trough.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty cliffs stand face to face, thundering at the western eaves.

sentences.zh: 脩竹葳蕤以翳薈，灌木森沉以蒙茂。

translations.literal: Tall bamboo spreads luxuriantly to shade and screen; shrubs stand dense and deep, veiled in luxuriant growth.
translations.idiomatic: Tall bamboo spreads in luxuriant shade; shrubs stand dense and deep, draped in heavy growth.

sentences.zh: 蘿曼延以攀援，花芬薰而媚秀。

translations.literal: Creepers spread out in entwining tendrils; flowers breathe fragrance, charming and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Creepers spread in trailing tendrils; flowers breathe fragrance, lovely and bright.

sentences.zh: 日月投光於柯間，風露披清於隈岫。

translations.literal: Sun and moon cast their light among the branches; wind and dew spread clarity over hidden valleys and peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon pour light through the branches; wind and dew spread clarity over hidden valleys and peaks.

sentences.zh: 夏涼寒燠，隨時取適。

translations.literal: Summer cool, winter warm—each season suits one's comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Cool in summer, warm in winter—each season offers its own comfort.

sentences.zh: 階基回互，橑櫺乘隔。

translations.literal: Terrace foundations wind back and forth; rafters and lattices rise in layered separation.
translations.idiomatic: Terrace foundations wind back and forth; rafters and window lattices rise tier upon tier.

sentences.zh: 此焉卜寢，翫水弄石。

translations.literal: Here one chooses a place to dwell; playing with water and toying with stones.
translations.idiomatic: Here I chose a place to live, playing with water and rearranging stones.

sentences.zh: 邇即回眺，終歲罔斁。

translations.literal: From nearby one turns back to gaze; through the whole year, one never wearies.
translations.idiomatic: Step out nearby and turn to look back—the view never wearies all year long.

sentences.zh: 傷美物之遂化，怨浮齡之如借。

translations.literal: Grieving that beautiful things proceed to change; resenting that floating years are as if borrowed.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that beautiful things pass and change; I resent that fleeting years feel borrowed.

sentences.zh: 眇遯逸於人群，長寄心於雲霓。

translations.literal: Far and hidden, withdrawn from the crowd; long I entrust my heart to clouds and rainbows.
translations.idiomatic: Far withdrawn from the throng of men, I have long entrusted my heart to clouds and rainbows.

sentences.zh: 〈南山是開創卜居之處也。

translations.literal: 〈Southern Mountain is the place where dwelling was first chosen and established.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Southern Mountain was where I first chose and established my dwelling.

sentences.zh: 從江樓步路，跨越山嶺，綿亙田野，或升或降，當三里許。

translations.literal: From the river pavilion one walks the path, crossing mountain ridges, stretching across fields—now ascending, now descending—about three li.
translations.idiomatic: From the river pavilion, the path crosses ridges and runs through fields, rising and falling for about three li.

sentences.zh: 塗路所經見也，則喬木茂竹，緣畛彌阜，橫波疏石，側道飛流，以為寓目之美觀。

translations.literal: Along the path one passes and sees tall trees and lush bamboo, tracing field boundaries and covering hillocks; waves cross and stones lie scattered; side paths and flying streams—beauties for the eye to rest upon.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way one sees tall trees and thick bamboo lining the fields and hills, rippling water among scattered stones, side paths and rushing streams—sights to delight the eye.

sentences.zh: 及至所居之處，自西山開道，迄於東山，二里有餘。

translations.literal: Reaching the place of dwelling, a road is opened from West Mountain to East Mountain, more than two li.
translations.idiomatic: At the dwelling itself, a road runs from West Mountain to East Mountain—more than two li.

sentences.zh: 南悉連嶺疊鄣，青翠相接，雲煙霄路，殆無倪際。

translations.literal: To the south all are linked ridges and layered barriers, green and blue meeting; cloud and mist on the road to heaven—almost without boundary.
translations.idiomatic: To the south, ridge after ridge stacks in layers, green upon green; cloud and mist on the skyward paths stretch almost without end.

sentences.zh: 從逕入谷，凡有三口。

translations.literal: Following the path into the valley, there are three entrances in all.
translations.idiomatic: Three paths lead from the trail into the valley.

sentences.zh: 方壁西南石門世□南□池東南，皆別載其事。

translations.literal: Southwest of Square Cliff, Stone Gate [lacuna] south [lacuna] Pool to the southeast—all are recorded separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of Square Cliff, Stone Gate [lacuna], south [lacuna], and Pool to the southeast—each is treated in a separate account.

sentences.zh: 緣路初入，行於竹逕，半路闊，以竹渠澗。

translations.literal: Following the path at first entry, one walks a bamboo trail; halfway it widens, and bamboo channels the stream.
translations.idiomatic: Entering by the path, one walks a bamboo-lined trail; halfway it widens, and bamboo channels guide the stream.

sentences.zh: 既入東南傍山渠，輾轉幽奇，異處同美。

translations.literal: Having entered the southeast hillside channel, it winds in secluded marvel; different places share the same beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, the southeast hillside channel winds through quiet marvels—different spots, the same splendor.

sentences.zh: 路北東西路，因山為鄣。

translations.literal: North of the path, east-west roads; relying on the mountain as barrier.
translations.idiomatic: North of the path, east and west roads run, using the mountain as a natural barrier.

sentences.zh: 正北狹處，踐湖為池。

translations.literal: At the due-north narrow spot, one treads the lake to make a pool.
translations.idiomatic: At the narrow spot due north, they cut into the lake to form a pool.

sentences.zh: 南山相對，皆有崖岩。

translations.literal: Southern mountains face each other; both have cliff faces and rocks.
translations.idiomatic: The southern mountains face each other, each with its cliffs and crags.

sentences.zh: 東北枕壑，下則清川如鏡，傾柯盤石，被隩映渚。

translations.literal: To the northeast it rests against a ravine; below, the clear stream is like a mirror; leaning trees and coiled rocks, shaded bends reflecting on islets.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast it rests against a ravine; below, the clear stream mirrors the sky—tilted branches, coiled boulders, shaded coves reflecting on the islets.

sentences.zh: 西巖帶林，去潭可二十丈許，葺基構宇，在岩林之中，水衛石階，開窗對山，仰眺曾峰，俯鏡濬壑。

translations.literal: West cliff girdled with forest, about twenty zhang from the deep pool; repairing the foundation and building a dwelling amid cliff and forest; water guards the stone steps; opening windows facing the mountain—gazing up at layered peaks, looking down to mirror the deep ravine.
translations.idiomatic: On the west cliff, forested, about twenty zhang from the pool, they rebuilt the foundation and raised a dwelling among cliff and trees. Water laps the stone steps; windows open toward the mountain—looking up at tiered peaks, looking down into the mirrored depths of the ravine.

sentences.zh: 去巖半嶺，復有一樓。

translations.literal: Halfway up the cliff's slope, there is yet another tower.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway up the cliff there stands another pavilion.

sentences.zh: 回望周眺，既得遠趣，還顧西館，望對窗戶。

translations.literal: Turning back to gaze all around, one gains distant delight; looking back at the west lodge, the windows face each other across the view.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to look around brings distant vistas; glancing back at the west lodge, its windows stand face to face across the view.

sentences.zh: 緣崖下者，密竹蒙逕，從北直南，悉是竹園。

translations.literal: Following the cliff downward, dense bamboo veils the path; from north straight to south—all is bamboo grove.
translations.idiomatic: Descending along the cliff, dense bamboo shrouds the path; from north to south, all is bamboo grove.

sentences.zh: 東西百丈，南北百五十五丈。

translations.literal: East-west one hundred zhang; north-south one hundred fifty-five zhang.
translations.idiomatic: It measures one hundred zhang east to west and one hundred fifty-five zhang north to south.

sentences.zh: 北倚近峰，南眺遠嶺，四山周回，溪澗交過，水石林竹之美，岩岫隈曲之好，備盡之矣。

translations.literal: North it leans on nearby peaks; south it gazes at distant ridges; four mountains encircle; streams and ravines cross and pass—the beauty of water, stone, forest, and bamboo; the charm of cliff peaks and winding coves—all are fully present.
translations.idiomatic: It rests against nearby peaks to the north and looks out on distant ridges to the south; mountains surround it on every side, streams and ravines crossing through. The beauty of water, stone, forest, and bamboo, the charm of cliffs and winding coves—all are here in full.

sentences.zh: 刊翦開築，此焉居處，細趣密翫，非可具記，故較言大勢耳。

translations.literal: Cut and trimmed, opened and built—here is the place of dwelling; fine delights for close enjoyment cannot all be recorded, hence only the general outline is sketched.
translations.idiomatic: Cleared, trimmed, and built up, this is where I live. Its finer pleasures, enjoyed up close, cannot all be written down; I can only sketch the general form.

sentences.zh: 越山列其表側傍緬□□為異觀也。〉

translations.literal: Yue Mountain arrays its outer face; beside it, distant [lacuna] [lacuna] forms a singular sight.〉
translations.idiomatic: Yue Mountain lines the outer edge; beside it, [lacuna] [lacuna] makes a view unlike any other.〉

sentences.zh: 因以小湖，鄰於其隈。

translations.literal: Therefore a small lake, neighboring its cove.
translations.idiomatic: So a small lake lies beside its sheltered bend.

sentences.zh: 眾流所湊，萬泉所回。

translations.literal: Where many streams gather; where myriad springs return.
translations.idiomatic: Where countless streams converge and myriad springs circle back.

sentences.zh: 氿濫異形，首毖終肥。

translations.literal: Gui and lan of differing forms; at the head Bi, at the end Fei.
translations.idiomatic: The Gui and Lan take different shapes—at the head the Bi spring, at the end the Fei.

sentences.zh: 別有山水，路邈緬歸。

translations.literal: Separately there is mountain and water; the road distant and far, returning.
translations.idiomatic: Another landscape lies apart; the road winds far into the distance and back.

sentences.zh: 〈氿濫、肥毖，皆是泉名，事見於《詩》。

translations.literal: 〈Gui, lan, fei, and bi—all are names of springs; the matter appears in the Book of Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Gui, Lan, Fei, and Bi are all names of springs, as recorded in the Book of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 云此萬泉所湊，各有形勢。〉

translations.literal: It says these myriad springs gather here, each with its own terrain and form.〉
translations.idiomatic: The text says that here myriad springs converge, each with its own shape and setting.〉

sentences.zh: 求歸其路，迺界北山。

translations.literal: Seeking the return path, it then borders North Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When one seeks the way back, the path reaches the boundary of North Mountain.

sentences.zh: 棧道傾虧，蹬閣連卷。

translations.literal: Plank roads tilt and break; stone stair-towers link in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Plank roads sag and buckle; stone stairways link one flight to the next.

sentences.zh: 復有水逕，繚繞回圓。

translations.literal: Again there is a water path, winding and circling round.
translations.idiomatic: Again a waterway winds in looping circles.

sentences.zh: 瀰瀰平湖，泓泓澄淵。

translations.literal: Vast and spreading, the flat lake; deep and clear, the limpid pool.
translations.idiomatic: The lake spreads wide and flat; the pool lies deep and clear.

sentences.zh: 孤岸竦秀，長洲芊綿。

translations.literal: A solitary shore rises tall and fine; a long islet stretches lush and continuous.
translations.idiomatic: A lone shore rises in elegant grace; a long islet runs green and unbroken.

sentences.zh: 既瞻既眺，曠矣悠然。

translations.literal: Gazing and looking afar—open and spacious, serene.
translations.idiomatic: Looking out on every side—the view opens wide, calm and free.

sentences.zh: 及其二川合流，異源同口。

translations.literal: When the two streams join in flow, different sources share one mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Where two streams merge, different sources share a single mouth.

sentences.zh: 赴隘入險，俱會山首。

translations.literal: Rushing into narrows and entering peril, all meet at the mountain's head.
translations.idiomatic: They plunge through narrows and rough water and meet at the mountain's crown.

sentences.zh: 瀨排沙以積丘，峰倚渚以起阜。

translations.literal: Rapids push sand to pile mounds; peaks lean on islets to rise into hillocks.
translations.idiomatic: Rapids heap sand into mounds; peaks rise from islets into low hills.

sentences.zh: 石傾瀾而梢巖，木映波而結藪。

translations.literal: Stones lean into billows and touch cliff faces; trees reflect in waves and gather into thickets.
translations.idiomatic: Stones lean into the surf and brush the cliffs; trees mirror the waves and crowd into thickets.

sentences.zh: 逕南漘以橫前，轉北崖而掩後。

translations.literal: The path crosses the southern shore horizontally before; turning the northern cliff, it conceals behind.
translations.idiomatic: The path runs along the southern bank across the foreground, then turns behind the northern cliff.

sentences.zh: 隱叢灌故悉晨暮，託星宿以知左右。

translations.literal: Hidden in thickets and shrubs, one knows neither dawn nor dusk; relying on stars to know left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden among thickets, one loses track of day and night and must read the stars to tell east from west.

sentences.zh: 往反經過，

translations.literal: Going and returning, passing through,
translations.idiomatic: Passing back and forth,

sentences.zh: 〈自非岩澗，便是水逕，洲島相對，皆有趣也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Unless it is cliff and ravine, it is a water path; islets face each other—all have their charm.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Every stretch is either cliff and stream or waterway, with islets facing one another—each has its own appeal.〉

sentences.zh: 山川澗石，州岸草木。

translations.literal: Mountains, streams, ravines, stones; islet shores, grasses, trees.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains, streams, ravines, and stones; islet shores, grass, and trees.

sentences.zh: 既摽異於前章，亦列同於後牘。

translations.literal: Already marked differently from the previous section, also listed the same as the later accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Marked differently from the earlier section, yet listed the same way in the later records.

sentences.zh: 山匪砠而是岵，川有清而無濁。

translations.literal: Mountains are not stony hills but gentle slopes; streams have clarity and no turbidity.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains are not harsh crags but gentle slopes; the streams run clear, never muddy.

sentences.zh: 石傍林而插巖，泉協澗而下谷。

translations.literal: Stones beside forests pierce into cliffs; springs join ravines and descend to valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Stones rise from the woods into the cliffs; springs gather in the gullies and pour down into the valleys.

sentences.zh: 淵轉渚而散芳，岸靡沙而映竹。

translations.literal: Deep pools turn to islets and spread fragrance; shores stretch with sand and reflect bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Deep pools swirl into islets and release their fragrance; sandy shores unfurl and mirror the bamboo.

sentences.zh: 草迎冬而結葩，樹凌霜而振綠。

translations.literal: Grass greets winter and forms blossoms; trees brave frost and shake forth green.
translations.idiomatic: Grass meets winter with blossoms; trees face down the frost and still flare green.

sentences.zh: 向陽則在寒而納煦，面陰則當暑而含雪。

translations.literal: Facing the sun, even in cold one receives warmth; facing shade, even in summer one holds snow.
translations.idiomatic: Where the sun strikes, cold yields to warmth; where shade falls, summer still holds snow.

sentences.zh: 連岡則積嶺以隱嶙，舉峰則群竦以[山截][山薛]。

translations.literal: Linked ridges amass peaks in hidden crags; raised peaks cluster towering with [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: Linked ridges pile into hidden crags; lifted peaks stand clustered, steep and [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 浮泉飛流以寫空，沈波潛溢於洞穴。

translations.literal: Floating springs and flying streams trace the sky; deep waves seep quietly into caverns.
translations.idiomatic: Springs float and streams leap, sketching the open sky; deep waters seep in silence through the caves.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆異所而咸善，殊節而俱悅。

translations.literal: All these are different places yet equally fine; different seasons yet all delight.
translations.idiomatic: Each place differs, yet all are fine; each season differs, yet all delight.

sentences.zh: 〈土山載石曰砠，山有林曰岵。

translations.literal: 〈An earthen hill bearing stone is called ju; a mountain with forests is called hu.
translations.idiomatic: 〈An earthen hill topped with stone is called ju; a mountain clothed in forest is called hu.

sentences.zh: 此章謂山川眾美，亦不必有，故總敘其最。

translations.literal: This section speaks of many beauties of mountains and rivers—not all need be present, so it summarizes the finest.
translations.idiomatic: This section treats the many beauties of mountain and stream; not every one need be present, so he sums up the best.

sentences.zh: 居山之後事，亦皆有尋求也。〉

translations.literal: Matters after dwelling in the mountains also all have their pursuit.〉
translations.idiomatic: What comes after dwelling in the mountains also has its own pursuit.〉

sentences.zh: 春秋有待，朝夕須資。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn have their requirements; morning and evening need provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn each have their demands; morning and evening need their supplies.

sentences.zh: 既耕以飯，亦桑貿衣。

translations.literal: One plows for food and also trades mulberry for clothing.
translations.idiomatic: One plows for grain and trades mulberry for clothes.

sentences.zh: 藝菜當肴，採藥救頹。

translations.literal: One gardens vegetables for dishes and gathers herbs to rescue decline.
translations.idiomatic: One grows vegetables for the table and gathers herbs to ward off decline.

sentences.zh: 自外何事，順性靡違。

translations.literal: Beyond these, what affairs? Following one's nature without transgression.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, what need is there? One follows one's nature and does not stray.

sentences.zh: 法音晨聽，放生夕歸。

translations.literal: At dawn listen to the Dharma's sound; at dusk return from releasing life.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he listens to the Dharma; at dusk he returns from releasing captive life.

sentences.zh: 研書賞理，敷文奏懷。

translations.literal: Study books and savor principles; spread prose to voice one's thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: He reads books and savors their principles, and sets prose to paper to give voice to his heart.

sentences.zh: 凡厥意謂，揚較以揮。

translations.literal: All one's meanings are elucidated through Yang Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: All that he means to say is laid out through exposition and comparison.

sentences.zh: 且列于言，誡特此推。

translations.literal: And now set forth in words, let this admonition be applied accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He sets it down in words here, and this admonition may be applied in turn.

sentences.zh: 〈謂寒待綿纊，暑待絺綌，朝夕餐飲，設此諸業以待之。

translations.literal: 〈Meaning: cold awaits padded silk and cotton; heat awaits hemp and gauze; morning and evening meals—these undertakings are laid out to await them.
translations.idiomatic: 〈He means that cold calls for padded silk and cotton, heat for hemp and gauze, and morning and evening meals—these tasks are arranged to meet such needs.

sentences.zh: 藥以療疾，又在其外，事之相推，自不得不然。

translations.literal: Medicine treats illness, and lies beyond these; affairs following one upon another—how could it be otherwise?
translations.idiomatic: Medicine to treat illness lies beyond these; one thing leads to another—how could it be otherwise?

sentences.zh: 至於聽講放生，研書敷文，皆其所好。

translations.literal: As for listening to lectures, releasing life, studying books, and spreading prose—all are his favorites.
translations.idiomatic: As for listening to sermons, releasing life, reading books, and writing prose—these are all his delights.

sentences.zh: 韓非有《揚較》，班固亦云「揚較古今」，其義一也。

translations.literal: Han Feizi has "Yang Jiao"; Ban Gu also says "weighing past and present"—the meaning is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Han Feizi wrote Yang Jiao; Ban Gu likewise speaks of "weighing past and present"—the sense is one.

sentences.zh: 左思曰：「為左右揚較而陳之。」〉

translations.literal: Zuo Si says: "Expound and compare for those at one's side and lay it out."〉
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Si says: "Expound and compare for those beside you and set it forth."〉

sentences.zh: 北山二園，南山三苑。

translations.literal: North Mountain has two orchards; South Mountain three parks.
translations.idiomatic: North Mountain holds two orchards; South Mountain, three groves.

sentences.zh: 百果備列，乍近乍遠。

translations.literal: A hundred fruits all laid out, now near, now far.
translations.idiomatic: Every kind of fruit is planted, some near at hand, some farther off.

sentences.zh: 羅行布株，迎早候晚。

translations.literal: Arranged in rows and planted in clusters, greeting early ripening and awaiting late.
translations.idiomatic: They are set in rows and planted in clusters, welcoming early fruit and awaiting late.

sentences.zh: 猗蔚溪澗，森疏崖巘。

translations.literal: Lush along streams and ravines, dense then sparse on cliffs and peaks.
translations.idiomatic: They grow lush along brooks and gullies, dense or sparse on cliffs and peaks.

sentences.zh: 杏壇[木奈]園，橘林、栗圃。

translations.literal: Apricot altar, [lacuna] orchard, citrus groves, chestnut paddocks.
translations.idiomatic: There are apricot terraces, a [lacuna] orchard, citrus groves, and chestnut plots.

sentences.zh: 桃李多品，梨棗殊所。

translations.literal: Peach and plum of many kinds; pear and jujube from distinctive places.
translations.idiomatic: Peaches and plums come in many varieties; pears and jujubes from their own distinct regions.

sentences.zh: 枇杷林檎，帶谷映渚。

translations.literal: Loquats and Chinese pear-apples, girdling valleys and reflecting on islets.
translations.idiomatic: Loquats and hawthorn apples belt the valleys and mirror themselves on the islets.

sentences.zh: 椹梅流芬於回巒，椑柿被實於長浦。

translations.literal: Mulberry fruit and plums breathe fragrance on winding ridges; shadbush and persimmons bear fruit on long shores.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberries and plums send fragrance through the winding ridges; shadbush and persimmons hang heavy on the long shores.

sentences.zh: 〈莊周云：「漁父見孔子杏壇之上。」

translations.literal: 〈Zhuang Zhou says: "The fisherman saw Confucius on the apricot altar."
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhuang Zhou says: "A fisherman saw Confucius upon the apricot terrace."

sentences.zh: 《維摩詰經》[木奈]樹園。

translations.literal: The Vimalakirti Sutra [lacuna] tree garden.
translations.idiomatic: The Vimalakirti Sutra speaks of a [lacuna] tree garden.

sentences.zh: 揚雄《蜀都賦》云橘林。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong's Rhapsody on the Shu Capital mentions citrus groves.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong's Rhapsody on the Shu Capital mentions citrus groves.

sentences.zh: 左太沖亦云：「戶有橘柚之園。」

translations.literal: Zuo Taichong also says: "Each household has gardens of tangerines and pomelos."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Taichong likewise says: "Every household has its grove of tangerines and pomelos."

sentences.zh: 桃李所殖甚多，棗梨事出北河、濟之間，淮、潁諸處，故云殊所也。〉

translations.literal: Peaches and plums are planted in great abundance; jujubes and pears are matters of the lands between the North River and Ji, and the Huai and Ying regions—hence he says distinctive places.〉
translations.idiomatic: Peaches and plums are planted in great number; jujubes and pears belong to the lands between the North River and the Ji, and to the Huai and Ying regions—hence he speaks of distinctive places.〉

sentences.zh: 畦町所藝，含蕊藉芳，蓼蕺葼薺，葑菲蘇薑。

translations.literal: In plots and fields what is planted holds buds and spreads fragrance: polygonum, houttuynia, smartweed, shepherd's purse, turnip, celery, perilla, ginger.
translations.idiomatic: In the beds and plots he grows buds wrapped in fragrance—knotweed, houttuynia, smartweed, shepherd's purse, turnip, celery, perilla, and ginger.

sentences.zh: 綠葵眷節以懷露，白薤感時而負霜。

translations.literal: Green mallow cherishes the season and holds dew; white leeks feel the season and bear frost.
translations.idiomatic: Green mallow clings to the season and cradles the dew; white leeks answer the season and carry frost.

sentences.zh: 寒蔥摽倩以陵陰，春藿吐苕以近陽。

translations.literal: Cold scallions stand tall over shady slopes; spring fava shoots forth buds near the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Hardy scallions rise over the shady slopes; spring fava sends up shoots where the sun is near.

sentences.zh: 〈葑菲見《詩•柏舟》中。

translations.literal: 〈Fengfei appears in the "Cypress Boat" ode of the Book of Odes.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Fengfei appears in the "Cypress Boat" ode of the Book of Odes.

sentences.zh: 管子曰：「北伐山戎，得寒蔥。」

translations.literal: Guanzi says: "On northern campaign against the Mountain Rong, they obtained cold scallions."
translations.idiomatic: Guanzi says: "On a northern campaign against the Mountain Rong, they obtained hardy scallions."

sentences.zh: 庾闡云，寒蔥挺園。

translations.literal: Yu Kan says, cold scallions stand in the garden.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kan says hardy scallions stand tall in the garden.

sentences.zh: 灌蔬自供，不待外求者也。〉

translations.literal: Watered vegetables for one's own supply, not waiting on outside seeking.〉
translations.idiomatic: Watered vegetables supply one's own table, without waiting on anything from outside.〉

sentences.zh: 弱質難恆，頹齡易喪。

translations.literal: Frail substance is hard to keep constant; declining years easily perish.
translations.idiomatic: A frail body is hard to preserve; declining years slip away all too easily.

sentences.zh: 撫鬢生悲，視顏自傷。

translations.literal: Stroking one's temples gives rise to grief; looking at one's face brings self-pity.
translations.idiomatic: Touching one's temples brings grief; looking at one's face brings self-reproach.

sentences.zh: 承清府之有術，冀在衰之可壯。

translations.literal: Receiving from the pure storehouse that there are methods, hoping that in decline one may be strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting that the pure pharmacopoeia holds remedies, he hopes that even in decline one may be restored.

sentences.zh: 尋名山之奇藥，越靈波而憩轅。

translations.literal: Seeking rare drugs on famous mountains, crossing spirit waves to rest the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He seeks rare drugs on famous mountains, crosses spirit-dark waters, and rests his carriage.

sentences.zh: 採石上之地黃，摘竹下之天門。

translations.literal: Gathering rehmannia from upon stones, plucking asparagus from beneath bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: He gathers rehmannia from the stones and plucks asparagus from beneath the bamboo.

sentences.zh: 摭曾嶺之細辛，拔幽澗之溪蓀。

translations.literal: Picking asarum from layered ridges, pulling irises from hidden ravines.
translations.idiomatic: He picks asarum from the layered ridges and pulls irises from hidden ravines.

sentences.zh: 訪鐘乳於洞穴，訊丹陽於紅泉。

translations.literal: Seeking stalactites in caverns, inquiring after cinnabar yang at Red Spring.
translations.idiomatic: He seeks stalactites in the caves and inquires after cinnabar yang at Red Spring.

sentences.zh: 〈此皆駐年之藥，即近山之所出，有采拾，欲以消病也。〉

translations.literal: 〈These are all age-prolonging drugs, produced from the nearby mountains; they are gathered and picked, intending to dispel illness.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈All of these are drugs that prolong life, gathered from the mountains nearby and picked to cure illness.〉

sentences.zh: 安居二時，冬夏三月。

translations.literal: Two seasons of rains retreat, three months in winter and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Two rains-retreat seasons, three months each in winter and summer.

sentences.zh: 遠僧有來，近眾無闕。

translations.literal: Monks from afar come; the nearby assembly is never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Monks arrive from distant places, and the local congregation is never incomplete.

sentences.zh: 法鼓朗響，頌偈清發。

translations.literal: The Dharma drum rings clear; hymns and gathas rise bright.
translations.idiomatic: The Dharma drum sounds clear and bright; hymns and gathas ring out.

sentences.zh: 散華霏蕤，流香飛越。

translations.literal: Scattered flowers drift lush; flowing fragrance flies beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered flowers drift in lush profusion; incense flows and fragrance flies abroad.

sentences.zh: 析曠劫之微言，說像法之遺旨。

translations.literal: Unfolding subtle words from kalpas vast; expounding the remnant purport of the Semblance Dharma.
translations.idiomatic: They unfold subtle teachings from kalpas without end and expound the surviving purport of the Semblance Dharma.

sentences.zh: 乘此心之一豪，濟彼生之萬理。

translations.literal: With this mind's one trace, aiding those lives in their myriad principles.
translations.idiomatic: With this single trace of the mind, they aid those living beings in their myriad ways.

sentences.zh: 啟善趣於南倡，歸清暢於北機。

translations.literal: Opening the good path at the southern lecturer; returning to clarity at the northern Dharma seat.
translations.idiomatic: They open the good path at the southern lecturer and return to clarity at the northern Dharma seat.

sentences.zh: 非獨愜於予情，諒僉感於君子。

translations.literal: Not only does it satisfy my feelings; I trust all are moved, gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: This satisfies not my feelings alone—I trust every gentleman present is moved.

sentences.zh: 山中兮清寂，群紛兮自絕。

translations.literal: In the mountains—serene silence; the world's clamor—cut off of itself.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountains, all is serene and still; the world's clamor cuts itself off.

sentences.zh: 周聽兮匪多，得理兮俱悅。

translations.literal: Hearing all around—not too much; grasping the principle—all rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: One hears all around, yet not too much; grasp the principle, and all rejoice together.

sentences.zh: 寒風兮搔屑，面陽兮常熱。

translations.literal: Cold wind scratches and scatters; facing the sun, always warm.
translations.idiomatic: Cold wind scours and scatters—but face the sun, and warmth is constant.

sentences.zh: 炎光兮隆熾，對陰兮霜雪。

translations.literal: Blazing light burns intense; facing shade, frost and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Blazing light burns fierce and high—yet face the shade, and frost and snow remain.

sentences.zh: 愒曾臺兮陟雲根，坐澗下兮越風穴。

translations.literal: Resting on a lofty terrace, climbing to the cloud-roots; sitting below the stream, crossing the wind-gaps.
translations.idiomatic: One rests on a lofty terrace and climbs to the roots of the clouds; one sits below the stream and passes through the wind-gaps.

sentences.zh: 在茲城而諧賞，傳古今之不滅。

translations.literal: In this fastness find harmonious delight; hand down what from past to present does not perish.
translations.idiomatic: In this mountain fastness one finds harmonious delight, and passes down what from past to present never perishes.

sentences.zh: 〈眾僧冬夏二時坐，謂之安居，輒九十日。

translations.literal: 〈The assembly of monks sits through two seasons, winter and summer—this is called rains retreat, always ninety days.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The monks sit through two seasons, winter and summer—this is called rains retreat, always ninety days.

sentences.zh: 眾遠近聚萃，法鼓、頌偈、華、香四種，是齋講之事。

translations.literal: The assembly gathers from near and far; four things—the Dharma drum, hymns and gathas, flowers, and incense—are the business of retreat lectures.
translations.idiomatic: The congregation gathers from near and far; the Dharma drum, hymns and gathas, flowers, and incense—these four are the affairs of retreat lectures.

sentences.zh: 析說是齋講之議。

translations.literal: "Unfolding" and "expounding" refer to the discussions of this retreat lecture.
translations.idiomatic: "Unfolding" and "expounding" describe the discourse of these retreat lectures.

sentences.zh: 乘此之心，可濟彼之生。

translations.literal: With this mind one can aid those lives.
translations.idiomatic: With this mind one can aid those living beings.

sentences.zh: 南倡者都講，北機者法師。

translations.literal: "Southern lecturer" means the preacher; "northern Dharma seat" means the Dharma master.
translations.idiomatic: "Southern lecturer" means the preacher; "northern Dharma seat" means the Dharma master.

sentences.zh: 山中靜寂，實是講說之處。

translations.literal: The mountains are quiet and still—a fitting place for lectures.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains are quiet and still—the very place for preaching.

sentences.zh: 兼有林木，可隨寒暑，恆得清和，以為適也。〉

translations.literal: With trees and groves too, one can suit cold and heat, ever obtaining mild ease—that is the comfort.〉
translations.idiomatic: There are woods and groves as well, so one can suit cold and heat and always find mild ease—that is the comfort.〉

sentences.zh: 好生之篤，以我而觀。

translations.literal: Deep love of life—judge from myself.
translations.idiomatic: Deep love of life—judge it from myself.

sentences.zh: 懼命之盡，吝景之歡。

translations.literal: Fearing life's end, cherishing the joy of daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the end of life, cherishing the joy of daylight.

sentences.zh: 分一往之仁心，拔萬族之險難。

translations.literal: Devoting one steadfast heart of benevolence, rescuing myriad species from peril.
translations.idiomatic: With one steadfast heart of benevolence, one rescues myriad species from peril.

sentences.zh: 招驚魂於殆化，收危形於將闌。

translations.literal: Summoning startled souls from near dissolution; gathering endangered forms from the brink of extinction.
translations.idiomatic: One summons startled souls from the brink of death and gathers endangered forms from the edge of extinction.

sentences.zh: 漾水性於江流，吸雲物於天端。

translations.literal: Setting aquatic creatures free in the river's flow; drawing cloud-dwellers back to the sky's edge.
translations.idiomatic: One sets aquatic creatures free in the river's flow and returns sky-dwellers to the edge of heaven.

sentences.zh: 睹騰翰之頏頡，視皷鰓之往還。

translations.literal: Watching wingbeats rise and soar; watching gills swell as fish come and go.
translations.idiomatic: One watches wings rise and soar, and sees fish puff their gills as they come and go.

sentences.zh: 馳騁者儻能狂愈，猜害者或可理攀。

translations.literal: Those who gallop and hunt may perhaps be cured of madness; those who suspect and harm may perhaps grasp the principle.
translations.idiomatic: Those who gallop and hunt may yet be cured of their frenzy; those who suspect and harm may yet grasp the principle.

sentences.zh: 〈云物皆好生，但以我而觀，便可知彼之情。

translations.literal: 〈All created things love life; judge from oneself and you may know their feelings.
translations.idiomatic: 〈All living things cherish life; judge from yourself and you may know their hearts.

sentences.zh: 吝景懼命，是好生事也。

translations.literal: Cherishing daylight and fearing death—this is loving life.
translations.idiomatic: Cherishing daylight and fearing death—this is the love of life.

sentences.zh: 能放生者，但有一往之仁心，便可拔萬族之險難。

translations.literal: One who can release life need only have one steadfast heart of benevolence to rescue myriad species from peril.
translations.idiomatic: One who can release captive life need only have one steadfast heart of benevolence to rescue myriad species from peril.

sentences.zh: 水性雲物，各尋其生。

translations.literal: Aquatic beings and sky creatures each seek their own life.
translations.idiomatic: Aquatic creatures and sky-dwellers each seek life in their own way.

sentences.zh: 老子云，馳騁田獵，令人心發狂。

translations.literal: Laozi says: galloping and hunting in the fields make the heart run wild.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi says: "Galloping and hunting in the fields make the heart run wild."

sentences.zh: 猜害者恆以忍害為心，見放生之理，或可得悟也。〉

translations.literal: Those who suspect and harm always bear harm in mind; seeing the principle of releasing life, they may perhaps awaken.〉
translations.idiomatic: Those who suspect and harm always bear injury in mind; seeing the principle of releasing life, they may yet awaken.〉

sentences.zh: 哲人不存，懷抱誰質。

translations.literal: The sage is no more—whose bosom can I pour into?
translations.idiomatic: The sage is gone—whose heart can I confide in?

sentences.zh: 糟粕猶在，啟縢剖帙。

translations.literal: The dregs remain—he opens the sealed bundles and splits the scroll cases.
translations.idiomatic: The dregs remain—he opens the sealed bundles and splits open the scroll cases.

sentences.zh: 見柱下之經二，睹濠上之篇七。

translations.literal: He sees two scrolls of the Man Below the Pillar; he views seven chapters of the Man on the Mound above the Moat.
translations.idiomatic: He finds two scrolls of the Man Below the Pillar and seven chapters of the Man on the Mound above the Moat.

sentences.zh: 承未散之全樸，救已頹於道術。

translations.literal: Receiving the undispersed whole simplicity; rescuing the already collapsed way and its arts.
translations.idiomatic: He receives the undispersed whole simplicity and rescues the way and its arts, already in decline.

sentences.zh: 嗟夫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 六藝以宣聖教，九流以判賢徒。

translations.literal: The Six Classics proclaim the sage's teaching; the Nine Schools distinguish worthy followers.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Classics proclaim the sage's teaching; the Nine Schools distinguish worthy disciples.

sentences.zh: 國史以載前紀，家傳以申世模。

translations.literal: National histories record past chronicles; family biographies set forth models for the age.
translations.idiomatic: National histories record past chronicles; family biographies set forth models for the age.

sentences.zh: 篇章以陳美刺，論難以覈有無。

translations.literal: Literary compositions state praise and blame; debates test what exists and what does not.
translations.idiomatic: Literary compositions set forth praise and blame; debates test what is and what is not.

sentences.zh: 兵技醫日，龜莢筮夢之法，風角冢宅，筭數律曆之書。

translations.literal: Arts of war, skills, medicine, and day-selection; methods of tortoise shells, yarrow stalks, divination, and dream interpretation; wind-angle and tomb-location arts; books on calculation, numbers, pitch pipes, and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: Military arts, crafts, medicine, and day-selection; methods of tortoise shells, yarrow stalks, divination, and dream interpretation; wind-angle and tomb-siting arts; books on calculation, numerology, pitch pipes, and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 或平生之所流覽，竝於今而棄諸。

translations.literal: Whatever one perused in life—together now cast away.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever one browsed in life—all of it is now cast aside.

sentences.zh: 驗前識之喪道，抱一德而不渝。

translations.literal: Proving that prior knowledge has lost the Way; holding to one virtue without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: He proves that prior learning has lost the Way, and holds to one virtue without wavering.

sentences.zh: 〈莊周云「輪扁語齊桓公，公之所讀書，聖人之糟粕。」

translations.literal: 〈Zhuang Zhou says: "Wheelwright Pian spoke to Duke Huan of Qi: what Your Grace reads in books is the sage's dregs."
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhuang Zhou says: "Wheelwright Pian told Duke Huan of Qi that what Your Grace reads in books is the sage's dregs."

sentences.zh: 縢者，《金縢》之流也。

translations.literal: "Teng" refers to texts of the Metal Coffer type.
translations.idiomatic: "Teng" refers to texts such as the Metal Coffer chapter.

sentences.zh: 柱下，老子。

translations.literal: "Below the Pillar"—Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: "Below the Pillar" means Laozi.

sentences.zh: 濠上，莊子。

translations.literal: "Above the Moat"—Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: "Above the Moat" means Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 二、七，是篇數也。

translations.literal: "Two" and "seven" are the number of chapters.
translations.idiomatic: "Two" and "seven" refer to the number of chapters in each work.

sentences.zh: 云此二書，最有理，過此以往，皆是聖人之教，獨往者所棄。〉

translations.literal: It says these two books are most reasonable; beyond this going forward, all are the sages' teachings, what lone travelers discard.〉
translations.idiomatic: He says these two books hold the truest principle; beyond them lie only the sage's formal teachings, which the solitary seeker casts aside.〉

sentences.zh: 伊昔齠齔，實愛斯文。

translations.literal: In times past, in infancy, he truly loved this literature.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood on, he truly loved letters.

sentences.zh: 援紙握管，會性通神。

translations.literal: Supporting paper and grasping the brush, meeting nature and reaching spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Paper before him and brush in hand, he joined his nature to spirit in writing.

sentences.zh: 詩以言志，賦以敷陳。

translations.literal: Poetry to speak the will, rhapsody to spread and set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry gives voice to the heart; rhapsody spreads its theme in full.

sentences.zh: 箴銘誄頌，咸各有倫。

translations.literal: Admonitions, inscriptions, dirges, and eulogies—all each have their rule.
translations.idiomatic: Admonitions, inscriptions, dirges, and eulogies each have their proper form.

sentences.zh: 爰暨山棲，彌歷年紀。

translations.literal: Then reaching mountain dwelling, filling many years.
translations.idiomatic: Then came life in the mountains, and years passed one after another.

sentences.zh: 幸多暇日，自求諸己。

translations.literal: Fortunately having many leisure days, seeking in oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately he had many idle days and looked to himself alone.

sentences.zh: 研精靜慮，貞觀厥美。

translations.literal: Grinding refinement and quiet reflection, truly observing its beauty.
translations.idiomatic: With refined study and quiet thought, he truly contemplated the beauty of his work.

sentences.zh: 懷秋成章，含笑奏理。

translations.literal: Embracing autumn and completing chapters, smiling as he presented principle.
translations.idiomatic: With autumn in his heart he shaped his lines, and with a smile set forth his themes.

sentences.zh: 〈謂少好文章，及山棲以來，別緣既闌，尋慮文詠，以盡暇日之適。

translations.literal: 〈It means that in youth he loved literature; since mountain dwelling, other pursuits were ended, he pursued thoughts of literary poems, to exhaust leisure days' pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: 〈This means that from youth he loved literature; since retiring to the mountains, other distractions had ceased, and he turned to verse to fill his idle days.

sentences.zh: 便可得通神會性，以永終朝。〉

translations.literal: Then one could reach spirit and meet nature, to prolong the whole morning.〉
translations.idiomatic: Thus he could join spirit and nature, and make a whole morning last forever.〉

sentences.zh: 若乃乘攝持之告，評養達之篇。

translations.literal: If then riding the warning of preserving life, appraising the chapter on nurturing and attaining.
translations.idiomatic: Some heed Lao Zi's warning to preserve life; others weigh Zhuang Zi's chapter on nurturing life and attaining freedom.

sentences.zh: 畏絕跡之不遠，懼行地之多艱。

translations.literal: Fearing that cutting off tracks is not far-reaching, dreading that treading earth has much hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Some fear that leaving no tracks does not go far enough; others dread the many hardships of walking the earth.

sentences.zh: 均上皇之自昔，忌下衰之在旃。

translations.literal: Weighing the Upper Sovereign's from former times, shunning the Lower Decline's on the felt mat.
translations.idiomatic: Some measure themselves against the Upper Sovereign of old; others shun the decline of the age as if it were a mat beneath them.

sentences.zh: 投吾心於高人，落賓名於聖賢。

translations.literal: Casting my heart to lofty men, dropping guest-name among sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: I turn my heart to lofty men of old and cast off courtesy-names among sage and worthy company.

sentences.zh: 廣滅景於崆峒，許遁音於箕山。

translations.literal: Guang extinguished his shadow at Kongtong, Xu hid his fame at Jishan.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Chengzi extinguished his shadow on Mount Kongtong; Xu You hid his renown on Mount Ji.

sentences.zh: 愚假駒以表谷，涓隱巖以搴芳。

translations.literal: Yu, by the colt, marked the valley; Juan hid in cliffs to pluck fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gong marked his valley by the colt ford; Juanzi hid among the cliffs to gather wild herbs.

translations.literal: [lacuna] Lai sheltered at Meng and wove baskets.
translations.idiomatic: Old Master Lai took refuge on Mount Meng and wove baskets for a living.

sentences.zh: 皓棲商而頤志，卿寢茂而敷詞。

translations.literal: Hao dwelt in Shang and nourished will, Qing slept in Mao and spread words.
translations.idiomatic: The Four White-Haired Elders dwelt in the Shang Mountains and nourished their will; the Minister retired to Maoling and spread his words.

sentences.zh: □□□□□□，鄭別谷而永逝。

translations.literal: [lacuna], Zheng left the valley and passed away forever.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zizhen left the valley and was gone forever.

sentences.zh: 梁去霸而之會，□□□□□□。

translations.literal: Liang left Ba and went to Hui, [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hong left Mount Ba for Kuaiji, [lacuna].

sentences.zh: 高居唐而胥宇，臺依崖而穴墀。

translations.literal: Gao dwelt on West Tang and shared the slope, Tai leaned on cliffs and hollowed courtyard floors.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wentong lived on West Tang Mountain at ease; Tai Xiaowei leaned against the cliff and hollowed an earthen court.

sentences.zh: 咸自得以窮年，眇貞思於所遺。

translations.literal: All alike could thus extend their years, faintly true in thought at what was left behind.
translations.idiomatic: All alike could live out their years in peace, keeping fast to the pure intent of those they left behind.

sentences.zh: 〈老子云：「善攝生者。」

translations.literal: 〈Laozi says: "One who is good at preserving life."
translations.idiomatic: 〈Laozi says, "Those skilled at preserving life."

sentences.zh: 莊子云，謂之不善持生。

translations.literal: Zhuangzi says, calling this not good at holding to life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi says this is what he calls not being skilled at preserving life.

sentences.zh: 又云，養生有無崖，達生者不務生之所無，奈何。

translations.literal: Again he says, nurturing life has no cliff-edge; one who attains life does not pursue what life lacks—how then?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi also says that nurturing life has no limit, yet one who has attained life does not chase what life cannot give—what then is one to do?

sentences.zh: 絕跡，上皇，下衰，賓名，義亦皆出莊周。

translations.literal: Cutting off tracks, Upper Sovereign, Lower Decline, guest-name—the meanings also all come from Zhuang Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: "Cutting off tracks," "Upper Sovereign," "Lower Decline," and "guest-name" all likewise come from Zhuang Zhou.

sentences.zh: 廣成子在崆峒之上，黃帝之師也。

translations.literal: Guang Chengzi was atop Kongtong, Yellow Emperor's teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Chengzi lived atop Mount Kongtong; he was the Yellow Emperor's teacher.

sentences.zh: 許由隱於箕山，堯以天下讓而不取。

translations.literal: Xu You hid at Jishan; Yao yielded the realm to him but he did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu You retired to Mount Ji; when Yao offered him the realm, he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 愚公居於駒阜，齊桓公逐鹿入山，見之。

translations.literal: Yu Gong dwelt at Jufu; Duke Huan of Qi hunted deer into the mountains and saw him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gong lived at Jufu; Duke Huan of Qi, hunting deer, entered the mountains and met him.

sentences.zh: 涓子隱於宕山，好餌術，告伯陽《琴心》三篇。

translations.literal: Juanzi hid at Dangshan, fond of elixir arts, told Boyang three chapters of "Heart of the Zither."
translations.idiomatic: Juanzi retired to Mount Dang, devoted to elixir arts, and conveyed to Boyang the three chapters of "Heart of the Zither."

sentences.zh: 庚桑楚得老子之道，居隈礨之山。

translations.literal: Gengsang Chu obtained Laozi's Way, dwelt on Mount Wai Lei.
translations.idiomatic: Gengsang Chu mastered Lao Zi's Way and lived on Mount Wai Lei.

sentences.zh: 楚狂接輿，楚王聞其賢，使使者聘之，於是遂游諸名山，在蜀峨眉山上。

translations.literal: Chu madman Jieyu—King of Chu heard of his worth, sent envoys to invite him; thereupon he wandered famous mountains, on Mount Emei in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jieyu the madman of Chu—when the king of Chu heard of his worth and sent envoys to summon him, he wandered instead among famous mountains and ended on Mount Emei in Shu.

sentences.zh: 徐無鬼巖棲，魏侯勞之，問：「先生苦山林矣，乃肯見寡人。」

translations.literal: Xu Wugui cliff-dwelt; Marquis of Wei comforted him, asking: "Master, the mountains and forests have been hard—yet you deign to see me."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wugui lived among the cliffs; the Marquis of Wei came to console him and asked, "Master, you have suffered in mountain and forest—yet you will see me."

sentences.zh: 無鬼問：「君絀嗜欲，屏好惡，則耳目察矣。」

translations.literal: Wugui asked: "My lord, if you reduce desires, screen out likes and dislikes, then ears and eyes will be keen."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wugui replied, "If my lord would reduce appetites and shut out likes and dislikes, your ears and eyes would see clearly."

sentences.zh: 常采茅栗。

translations.literal: He always gathered thatch and chestnuts.
translations.idiomatic: He lived by gathering wild grasses and chestnuts.

sentences.zh: 老萊子耕於蒙山之陽，著書十五篇，言道家之事，織畚為業。

translations.literal: Old Master Lai plowed on Meng Mountain's south face, wrote fifteen chapters on Daoist matters, weaving baskets as occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Old Master Lai farmed on the southern slope of Mount Meng, wrote fifteen chapters on Daoist matters, and made his living weaving baskets.

sentences.zh: 四皓避秦亂，入商洛深山，漢祖召不能出。

translations.literal: Four Hoary Ones fled Qin disorder, entered deep Shang-Luo mountains; Han Founder summoned them but they could not be brought out.
translations.idiomatic: The Four White-Haired Elders fled Qin chaos for the deep Shang-Luo Mountains; when the Han founder summoned them, they would not come out.

sentences.zh: 司馬長卿高才，而處世不樂預公卿大事，□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□遂與弟子別於山阿，終身不反。

translations.literal: Sima Changqing was highly talented, yet in the world did not delight in joining great affairs of lords and ministers, [lacuna] thereupon parted from disciples at the mountain foot, never returning for life.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiangru was a man of rare talent, yet had no taste for the great affairs of court; [lacuna] he then took leave of his disciples at a mountain bend and never returned.

sentences.zh: 梁伯鸞隱霸陵山中，耕織以自娛，後復入會稽山。

translations.literal: Liang Boqian hid in Mount Balting mountains, plowing and weaving for self-amusement; later again entered Mount Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hong retired to Mount Balting, farming and weaving for his own delight; later he went deeper still into the Kuaiji Mountains.

sentences.zh: 臺孝威居武安山下，依崖為土室，采藥自給。

translations.literal: Tai Xiaowei dwelt below Mount Wu'an, leaning on cliffs to make earthen rooms, gathering medicine for self-supply.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Xiaowei lived below Mount Wu'an in an earthen chamber cut into the cliff, gathering herbs to sustain himself.

sentences.zh: 高文通居西唐山，從容自娛也。〉

translations.literal: Gao Wentong dwelt on West Tang Mountain, at ease and self-amused.〉
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wentong lived on West Tang Mountain, taking his ease in quiet contentment.〉

sentences.zh: 暨其窈窕幽深，寂漠虛遠。

translations.literal: And its graceful seclusion, silent emptiness and remote distance.
translations.idiomatic: And for all its graceful depth, its silence, emptiness, and remoteness—

sentences.zh: 事與情乖，理與形反。

translations.literal: Affairs and feeling diverge, principle and form oppose.
translations.idiomatic: affairs and feeling pull apart, principle and outward form run counter.

sentences.zh: 既耳目之靡端，豈足跡之所踐。

translations.literal: Since ears and eyes have no reach to ends, how could footsteps tread there?
translations.idiomatic: If even ear and eye cannot reach its limits, how could human footsteps tread there?

sentences.zh: 蘊終古於三季，俟通明於五眼。

translations.literal: Hoarding through the ages in three seasons, awaiting clarity in five eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Its truth has been hoarded since ancient times in the three seasons of darkness; only the five eyes of enlightenment could make it plain.

sentences.zh: 權近慮以停筆，抑淺知而絕簡。

translations.literal: Weighing near thought to stop the brush, restraining shallow knowledge and cutting off writing.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing my limited thought, I stop my brush; knowing my shallow insight, I cease writing.

sentences.zh: 〈謂此既非人跡所求，更待三明五通，然後可踐履耳。

translations.literal: 〈It means this is already not what human footsteps seek; one must further wait for three clarities and five penetrations, then one can tread it.
translations.idiomatic: 〈This means the place is not one human footsteps can seek; one would need the three clarities and five penetrations before one could tread there.

sentences.zh: 故停筆絕簡，不復多云，冀夫賞音悟夫此旨也。〉

translations.literal: Therefore stopping brush and cutting writing, not again saying much, hoping that connoisseurs of tone would grasp this intent.〉
translations.idiomatic: So I stop my brush and write no more, hoping that those who truly hear will grasp what I mean.〉

sentences.zh: 太祖登祚，誅徐羨之等，徵為秘書監，再召不起，上使光祿大夫范泰與靈運書敦獎之，乃出就職。

translations.literal: When the Taizu ascended the throne, after executing Xu Xianzhi and others, he was summoned as Director of the Palace Library; summoned twice again, he did not rise; the emperor sent Household Officer of the Imperial Household Fan Tai to write Lingyun a letter earnestly encouraging him, and then he came out and took office.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen took the throne and executed Xu Xianzhi and his fellows, he summoned Lingyun to serve as director of the palace library. Twice more the court called him, and twice he refused. The emperor then had Fan Tai, household officer of the imperial household, write him a letter of earnest praise and encouragement—and only then did Lingyun emerge and accept the post.

sentences.zh: 使整理秘閣書，補足闕文。

translations.literal: He was ordered to organize the secret archive books and supplement missing texts.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with putting the palace library in order and filling in lacunae in the texts.

sentences.zh: 以晉氏一代，自始至終，竟無一家之史，令靈運撰《晉書》，粗立條流；

translations.literal: Because the Jin house for one generation, from beginning to end, had not a single unified history, Lingyun was ordered to compile the "History of Jin," roughly establishing categories and sequence;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin dynasty from first to last had never possessed a unified dynastic history, Lingyun was commanded to compile a History of Jin and roughly lay out its divisions;

sentences.zh: 書竟不就。

translations.literal: The book in the end was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: but the work was never finished.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中，日夕引見，賞遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant; day and night he was summoned to audience, and favor was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to palace attendant and summoned to the emperor's presence morning and evening, with lavish marks of favor.

sentences.zh: 靈運詩書皆兼獨絕，每文竟，手自寫之，文帝稱為二寶。

translations.literal: Lingyun's poetry and calligraphy both combined supreme uniqueness; whenever an essay was finished, he personally copied it by hand; Emperor Wen called them the two treasures.
translations.idiomatic: In both poetry and calligraphy Lingyun stood alone in his age. Whenever he finished a piece, he copied it out in his own hand; Emperor Wen called his writings and ink traces "two treasures."

sentences.zh: 既自以名輩，才能應參時政，初被召，便以此自許；

translations.literal: Since he regarded himself as of eminent lineage and believed his talent ought to participate in affairs of the age, at the first summons he already promised himself this;
translations.idiomatic: Counting himself among the foremost men of the age, he felt his gifts entitled him to a share in statecraft, and from the moment of his first summons he had staked his hopes on that;

sentences.zh: 既至，文帝唯以文義見接，每侍上宴，談賞而已。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, Emperor Wen received him only with regard to literary meaning; whenever he attended the emperor's banquets, it was talk and appreciation only.
translations.idiomatic: but once at court he found that Emperor Wen received him only as a man of letters—whenever he attended imperial banquets, talk and literary appreciation were all he was offered.

sentences.zh: 王曇首、王華、殷景仁等，名位素不踰之，並見任遇，靈運意不平，多稱疾不朝直。

translations.literal: Wang Tanzhou, Wang Hua, Yin Jingren, and others—whose fame and rank had never surpassed his—were all given trust and favor; Lingyun was resentful in spirit and often claimed illness, not attending regular court duty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhou, Wang Hua, Yin Jingren, and others—men whose standing had never surpassed his—were all entrusted with real power and favor. Lingyun simmered with resentment and often pleaded illness to avoid regular attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 穿池植援，種竹樹堇，驅課公役，無復期度。

translations.literal: He dug ponds and planted trellises, grew bamboo and violets, drove corvée labor of the public service, with no further limit on schedules.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he dug ponds, trained vines on trellises, planted bamboo and violets, and pressed public labor into his service without regard for any proper limit.

sentences.zh: 出郭游行或一日百六七十里，經旬不歸，既無表聞，又不請急。

translations.literal: Going outside the city on excursions, sometimes in one day a hundred sixty or seventy li; for ten days at a stretch he did not return; he neither filed memorials informing the court nor requested urgent leave.
translations.idiomatic: On excursions beyond the city he sometimes covered a hundred and sixty or seventy li in a single day, and might stay away ten days at a stretch—filed no memorial to inform the court and sought no leave for urgent business.

sentences.zh: 上不欲傷大臣，諷旨令自解。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish to harm a great minister and hinted at his intent, ordering him to resign on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, unwilling to disgrace so great a minister openly, hinted that he should withdraw on his own.

sentences.zh: 靈運乃上表陳疾，上賜假東歸。

translations.literal: Lingyun then submitted a memorial stating illness; the emperor granted leave for him to return east.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun then memorialized the throne citing illness, and the emperor granted him leave to return east.

sentences.zh: 將行，上書勸伐河北，曰：

translations.literal: About to depart, he submitted a memorial urging an expedition against Hebei, saying:
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, he submitted a memorial urging a northern campaign against Hebei, saying:

sentences.zh: 自中原喪亂，百有餘年，流離寇戎，湮沒殊類。

translations.literal: Since the Central Plains fell to chaos, more than a hundred years; scattered by invading armies, diverse peoples submerged and lost.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a hundred years now the Central Plains have lain in chaos—peoples driven into exile by raiding armies, whole communities lost and swallowed up.

sentences.zh: 先帝聰明神武，哀濟群生，將欲蕩定趙魏，大同文軌，使久凋反於正化，偏俗歸於華風。

translations.literal: The late emperor was wise and divinely martial, compassionate and saving the multitude; he wished to sweep and settle Zhao and Wei, great unity of culture and chariot-tracks, to make long-withered lands return to proper transformation and partial customs return to Chinese style.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor was wise, resolute, and divinely martial, his heart set on succoring all under heaven. He meant to sweep Zhao and Wei clean, unite every realm under one culture and one law, restore lands long withered to civilization, and bring estranged customs back within the civilizing sway of the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 運謝事乖，理違願絕，仰德抱悲，恨存生盡。

translations.literal: Fate declined, affairs turned adverse, principle opposed and wishes cut off; looking up to his virtue with grief, regret that life remaining ends.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven withdrew its favor, affairs turned against him, righteous intent was thwarted and his great design left unfinished. Mourning his virtue from afar, how bitter the regret that one's allotted years should end before his aim was fulfilled!

sentences.zh: 況陵塋未幾，凶虜伺隙，預在有識，誰不憤歎。

translations.literal: Moreover the imperial tombs are not long sealed; fierce invaders watch for openings; all who have foresight—who does not burn with anger and sigh?
translations.idiomatic: And now the imperial tombs are scarcely sealed before fierce enemies prowl for their opening—every man of discernment burns with indignation; who does not gnash his teeth and sigh?

sentences.zh: 而景平執事，並非其才，且遘紛京師，豈慮託付。

translations.literal: Yet the officials in charge at Jingping were none of them possessed of the requisite talent, and with turmoil encountered in the capital—how could the trust have been placed?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the men entrusted with affairs in the Jingping era were none of them equal to the task, and with turmoil convulsing the capital—how could such a burden have been placed in such hands?

sentences.zh: 遂使孤城窮陷，莫肯極。

translations.literal: Thus causing isolated cities to fall in desperate straits, with none willing to exert themselves to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Isolated cities were driven to ruin, and no one would go to the utmost to save them.

sentences.zh: 忠烈囚朔漠，綿河三千，翻為寇有。

translations.literal: The loyal and brave imprisoned in the northern desert; three thousand li along the river—turned instead to invader possession.
translations.idiomatic: Men of loyalty and valor languish in the northern wastes; three thousand li of riverlands have passed into the enemy's hands.

sentences.zh: 晚遣鎮戍，皆先朝之所開拓，一旦淪亡，此國恥宜雪，被於近事者也。

translations.literal: The garrisons dispatched later were all territories the former court had opened and expanded; once lost in a day—this national shame ought to be wiped away; it falls upon recent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier garrisons sent out in later years were all lands our former sovereign had opened and won—yet they were lost in a single stroke. Such a national disgrace must be avenged; the wound is still fresh in our own memory.

sentences.zh: 又北境自染逆虜，窮苦備罹，徵調賦斂，靡有止已，所求不獲，輒致誅殞，身禍家破，闔門比屋，此亦仁者所為傷心者也。

translations.literal: Moreover the northern borderlands, since stained by rebellious invaders, have suffered every extremity of hardship; conscription, levies, and tax collection have had no stopping; what was sought not obtained, then led to execution and death; personal disaster and household ruin, whole gates and every house—this too is what the benevolent must grieve over.
translations.idiomatic: And on the northern frontier, ever since the stain of the invaders, the people have endured every form of hardship. Conscription, levies, and exactions never cease; what the authorities demand and cannot obtain they answer with punishment and death—ruined lives, shattered households, grief in every dwelling. Even the benevolent cannot bear to look upon it.

sentences.zh: 咸云西虜舍末，遠師隴外，東虜乘虛，呼可掩襲。

translations.literal: All say the western invaders abandon the secondary and send armies far beyond Long; the eastern invaders seize the void—how suddenly they may be raided!
translations.idiomatic: All agree that the Western barbarians have left their rear exposed and marched far beyond Long, while the Eastern barbarians stand open to attack—here is a chance for a swift, crushing blow.

sentences.zh: 西軍既反，得據關中，長圍咸陽，還路已絕，雖遣救援，停住河東，遂乃遠討大城，欲為首尾。

translations.literal: The western army having returned, obtained and holds Guanzhong; long siege of Xianyang; the return route already cut off; although rescue was dispatched, it halted east of the river; then went far to attack the great fortress, intending a pincer from head to tail.
translations.idiomatic: The Western army has turned back and seized Guanzhong; Xianyang is under long siege and their line of retreat is severed. Though the enemy has sent relief, those forces are stalled east of the River, while their main host marches far north to strike at the capital—stretching to link front and rear in one long line.

sentences.zh: 而西寇深山重阻，根本自固，徒棄巢窟，未足相拯。

translations.literal: Yet the western invaders in deep mountains with heavy barriers—their roots are firm by themselves; merely abandoning their nest and lair is not enough for mutual rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Western enemy holds deep mountains and hard passes; their base remains firm. To abandon their lair for such a rescue is hardly enough to save their besieged forces—and leaves their heartland exposed besides.

sentences.zh: 師老於外，國虛永內，時來之會，莫復過此。

translations.literal: Armies wearied outside, the state empty within; the moment heaven grants—none surpasses this again.
translations.idiomatic: Their troops grow weary in the field while their realm hollows out at home. No moment heaven offers could be more favorable than this.

sentences.zh: 觀兵耀威，實在茲日。

translations.literal: To display troops and show might—truly it is on this day.
translations.idiomatic: To parade one's armies and show the majesty of the throne—the day is today.

sentences.zh: 若相持未已，或生事變，忽值新起之眾，則異於今，苟乖其時，難為經略，雖兵食倍多，則萬全無必矣。

translations.literal: If the stalemate has not yet ended, or affairs change arise, suddenly meeting newly risen multitudes—then it would differ from the present; if one misses the season, hard to plan strategy; although weapons and provisions were doubled, then complete security would not be assured.
translations.idiomatic: If we let this standoff drag on, some unforeseen change may arise; should a fresh enemy rise, the situation will no longer be what it is today. Miss the season, and strategy becomes hard. Double our arms and stores as we might, certainty of complete success would still be beyond our grasp.

sentences.zh: 又歷觀前代，類以兼弱為本，古今聖德，未之或殊。

translations.literal: Moreover, reviewing past ages, generally they took conquering the weak as foundation; ancient and modern sage virtue—none differ in this.
translations.idiomatic: Review the ages past: nearly every great founding took the conquest of the weak as its foundation. Sage emperors old and new have scarcely differed on this point.

sentences.zh: 豈不以天時人事，理數相得，興亡之度，定期居然。

translations.literal: Is it not that heaven's season and human affairs, principle and number matching—the measure of rise and fall has a fixed term by nature?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not because heaven's season and human effort, principle and destiny, must align—the arc of rise and fall has a term fixed by nature itself?

sentences.zh: 故古人云：「既見天殃，又見人災，乃可以謀。」

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients said: "Having seen heaven's calamity and also seen man's disaster, only then may one plan.
translations.idiomatic: As the ancients said: "Only when heaven's calamity and man's disaster have both been seen may one begin to plan.

sentences.zh: 昔魏氏之強，平定荊、冀，乃乘袁、劉之弱；

translations.literal: In former times Wei's strength, pacifying Jing and Ji, rode on Yuan and Liu's weakness;
translations.idiomatic: When Wei grew strong and subdued Jing and Ji, it seized its chance in the weakness of Yuan and Liu;

sentences.zh: 晉世之盛，拓開吳、蜀，亦因葛、陸之衰。

translations.literal: Jin age's flourishing, expanding Wu and Shu, also relied on Ge and Lu's decline.
translations.idiomatic: when Jin rose to its height and opened Wu and Shu, it did so because the houses of Zhuge and Lu were in decline.

sentences.zh: 此皆前世成事，著於史策者也。

translations.literal: These are all previous generations' accomplished affairs, recorded in historical annals.
translations.idiomatic: Such precedents fill the historical records of earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 自羌平之後，天下亦謂虜當俱滅，長驅滑臺，席捲下城，奪氣喪魄，指日就盡。

translations.literal: Since the Qiang pacification, all under heaven also said the invaders ought altogether to perish; long drive to Huatai, sweeping down cities, losing spirit and courage, within days they would be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of the Qiang, all thought the northern invaders would soon be wiped out together—our armies would sweep to Huatai, roll through every city, and the enemy, stripped of nerve and spirit, would be spent within days.

sentences.zh: 但長安違律，潼關失守，用緩天誅，假延歲月，日來至今，十有二載，是謂一紀，曩有前言。

translations.literal: But Chang'an violated discipline, Tong Pass lost its defense; delaying heaven's punishment, borrowing extension of months; from that day until now, twelve years—this is called one cycle; formerly there was prior saying.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chang'an fell through indiscipline, Tong Pass was lost—and heaven's judgment, delayed, has borrowed month upon month of reprieve. From that day to this has been twelve years, a full cycle; the ancients foretold as much.

sentences.zh: 況五胡代數齊世，虜期餘命，盡於來年。

translations.literal: Moreover the Five Barbarians' generations align with the era; the invaders' allotted span—its remainder ends next year.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Barbarian dynasties have run their allotted generations in step with the times; the invaders' destined span will be exhausted by next year.

sentences.zh: 自相攻伐，兩取其困，卞莊之形，驗之今役。

translations.literal: Fighting each other themselves, both take their exhaustion; the form of Bian Zhuang—verified in the present campaign.
translations.idiomatic: They turn on one another and wear each other down—the stratagem of Bian Zhuang, waiting as tiger and wolf tear each other apart, is plain to see in the war they fight today.

sentences.zh: 仰望聖澤，有若渴饑，注心南雲，為日已久。

translations.literal: Looking up to sacred grace, like thirst and hunger; heart fixed on southern clouds—for days already long.
translations.idiomatic: We look up to your sacred grace as the thirsty look to water and the hungry to bread; our hearts have long been turned toward the southern clouds—the court that alone can deliver us.

sentences.zh: 來蘇之冀，實歸聖明，此而弗乘，後則未兆。

translations.literal: The hope of "coming restoration" truly returns to sage clarity; if this is not seized, afterward there will be no omen.
translations.idiomatic: The hope of deliverance rests wholly upon your sagely wisdom. Fail to seize this moment, and no such sign may ever come again.

sentences.zh: 即日府藏，誠無兼儲，然凡造大事，待國富兵強，不必乘會，於我為易，貴在得時。

translations.literal: On the present day the treasury truly has no combined stores; yet for all great undertakings one waits for rich state and strong army—not necessarily seizing the moment; for us it would be easy; what is prized is obtaining the season.
translations.idiomatic: I know well that the treasury today holds no double surplus. Yet great undertakings are not always timed to wealth and full armies alone; for us the enterprise would still be manageable—what matters is seizing the hour.

sentences.zh: 器械既充，眾力粗足，方於前後，乃當有優。

translations.literal: Weapons already sufficient, mass strength roughly adequate—compared with before and after, there should be advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Our arms are ready and our forces roughly sufficient; measured against what came before or may come after, we stand at an advantage.

sentences.zh: 常議損益，久證冀州口數，百萬有餘，田賦之沃，著自《貢》典，先才經創，基趾猶存，澄流引源，桑麻蔽野，強富之實，昭然可知。

translations.literal: Constant deliberation on increase and decrease; long verified Jizhou's population count—more than a million; the fertility of fields and taxes is celebrated in the "Tribute of Yu"; the earlier talent once established foundations, the base stones still remain; clear streams drawn from the source, mulberry and hemp covering the wilds—the reality of strength and wealth is clearly knowable.
translations.idiomatic: I have weighed the matter again and again. The registered population of Jizhou exceeds a million; the richness of its fields, recorded since the Tribute of Yu, is no empty boast. Foundations laid in earlier ages still stand; channels run clear from their sources and mulberry and hemp shade the countryside. Its wealth and strength are there for any eye to see.

sentences.zh: 為國長久之計，孰若一往之費邪！

translations.literal: For the state's long-term plan—how does it compare to the cost of one expedition!
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the long welfare of the state, what is one campaign's expense?

sentences.zh: 或懲關西之敗，而謂河北難守。

translations.literal: Some take warning from the defeat in Guanxi and say Hebei is hard to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Some, taking the defeat in Guanxi as their warning, declare that Hebei would be impossible to hold.

sentences.zh: 二境形勢，表裏不同，關西雜居，種類不一，昔在前漢，屯軍霸上，通火甘泉。

translations.literal: The two borders' terrain—exterior and interior differ; Guanxi mixed settlement, kinds not one; formerly in Former Han, garrison at Bashang, beacon fires connecting to Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: But the two frontiers differ utterly in character. Guanxi is a land of mixed settlements and many peoples—as in the Former Han, when garrisons at Bashang kept watch and beacon fires linked all the way to Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 況乃遠戍之軍，值新故交代之際者乎！

translations.literal: How much more distant garrison troops, at the juncture when old and new reliefs exchange!
translations.idiomatic: How much more vulnerable are distant garrisons at the very moment when old troops depart and new ones have not yet settled in!

sentences.zh: 河北悉是舊戶，差無雜人，連嶺判阻，三關作隘。

translations.literal: Hebei is entirely old households, barely without mixed people; connected ridges form barriers, three passes serve as narrow gates.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei, by contrast, is populated almost entirely by our own old families, with scarcely a stranger among them. Ridges link into natural ramparts, and the Three Passes choke the way like narrow gates.

sentences.zh: 若遊騎長驅，則沙漠風靡；

translations.literal: If roaming cavalry long drive, then the desert wind sweeps.
translations.idiomatic: Send our mobile cavalry in a long strike, and the desert itself will bend before their wind.

sentences.zh: 若嚴兵守塞，則冀方山固。

translations.literal: If strict troops guard the passes, then Jizhou's mountains will stand firm.
translations.idiomatic: If we station strong garrisons at the frontier passes, the mountains of Jizhou will hold fast.

sentences.zh: 昔隴西傷破，鼂錯興言；

translations.literal: In former times Longxi was wounded and broken, and Chao Cuo raised his voice;
translations.idiomatic: When Longxi was ravaged in former times, Chao Cuo spoke out;

sentences.zh: 匈奴慢侮，賈誼憤歎。

translations.literal: When the Xiongnu showed contempt and insult, Jia Yi sighed in indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiongnu grew insolent and overbearing, Jia Yi cried out in righteous anger.

sentences.zh: 方於今日，皆為賒矣。

translations.literal: Compared with today, all are already distant.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the present moment, those crises seem almost remote.

sentences.zh: 晉武中主耳，值孫晧虐亂，天祚其德，亦由鉅平奉策，荀、賈折謀，故能業崇當年，區宇一統。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin was only a middling ruler, yet he encountered Sun Hao's tyranny and disorder; Heaven blessed his virtue, and also because Wang Jun presented the surrender document and Xun and Jia broke opposing counsel, he was therefore able to elevate his achievement that same year and unify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin was no more than a ruler of middling talent, yet he met with Sun Hao's cruelty and chaos, and Heaven favored his virtue. Wang Jun also presented the surrender document, while Xun Xu and Jia Chong overcame the doubters—thus in that very year he raised his enterprise to greatness and united the realm.

sentences.zh: 況今陛下聰明聖哲，天下歸仁，文德與武功竝震，霜威共素風俱舉，協以宰輔賢明，諸王美令，岳牧宣烈，虎臣盈朝，而天或遠命，亦何敵不滅，矧伊頑虜，假日而已哉！

translations.literal: How much more so today, when Your Majesty is wise and sagely, all under Heaven turns to benevolence, civil virtue and martial achievement shake together, frost authority and plain integrity rise together, together with worthy and enlightened chief ministers, princes of fine command, regional governors proclaiming martial glory, and fierce ministers filling the court—and Heaven's mandate extends far: what enemy would not be destroyed? How much more so these stubborn barbarians—they are merely borrowing days!
translations.idiomatic: How much more is this true now, when Your Majesty is wise and enlightened, the empire turns toward benevolent rule, civil virtue and martial might resound together, stern authority and plain integrity rise as one, aided by worthy chief ministers, princes of excellent command, regional governors who proclaim their martial glory, and fierce ministers filling the court? With Heaven's mandate extending so far, what foe could fail to fall? As for those stubborn barbarians—they are living on borrowed time!

sentences.zh: 伏惟深機志務，久定神謨。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your deep designs and settled purpose have long fixed divine strategy.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that Your deep designs and long-settled purpose have already fixed Heaven's strategy.

sentences.zh: 臣卑賤側陋，竄景巖穴，實仰希太平之道，傾睹岱宗之封，雖乏相如之筆，庶免史談之憤，以此謝病京師，萬無恨矣。

translations.literal: Your subject is base, lowly, narrow, and crude, hiding my light in cliff caves; I truly look up hoping for the Way of great peace and lean forward to behold the feng sacrifice at Mount Tai. Though I lack Sima Xiangru's brush, I may yet escape Sima Tan's indignation. With this I take leave of office in the capital on grounds of illness, and would have no regret whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: I am base, obscure, and of narrow learning, hiding myself among cliffs and caves, yet I truly hope for the age of great peace and long to witness the feng sacrifice at Mount Tai. Though I lack Sima Xiangru's eloquence, I may at least avoid the wrath of Sima Tan. For this I beg leave of my post in the capital on grounds of illness, and would count myself entirely without regret.

sentences.zh: 久欲上陳，懼在觸置，蒙賜恩假，暫違禁省，消渴十年，常慮朝露，抱此愚志，昧死以聞。

translations.literal: For long I wished to submit this memorial, fearing that I might give offense. Having received Your gracious leave, I temporarily departed the forbidden precincts. I have suffered from wasting thirst for ten years and constantly fear the morning dew. Holding this foolish resolve, I risk death to make it known.
translations.idiomatic: Long I have wished to submit this memorial, yet feared giving offense. Having received Your gracious leave to depart, I temporarily left the palace precincts. For ten years I have suffered from wasting thirst and constantly feared I might not see another dawn. Clinging to this foolish purpose, I risk death to speak before You.

sentences.zh: 靈運以疾東歸，而遊娛宴集，以夜續晝，復為御史中丞傅隆所奏，坐以免官。

translations.literal: Lingyun returned east on grounds of illness, yet went on feasting and gathering for pleasure, continuing day through night, and was again impeached by the Censor-in-Chief Fu Long; on that account he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun went east on grounds of illness, yet continued to feast and hold gatherings for pleasure, turning night into day. He was impeached again by the Censor-in-Chief Fu Long and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 是歲，元嘉五年。

translations.literal: That year was the fifth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the fifth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 靈運既東還，與族弟惠連、東海何長瑜、潁川荀雍、泰山羊璿之，以文章賞會，共為山澤之游，時人謂之四友。

translations.literal: After Lingyun returned east, he joined with his clansman Huilian, He Changyu of Donghai, Xun Yong of Yingchuan, and Yang Xuanzhi of Taishan in mutual appreciation through literature, and together they roamed mountains and marshes; men of the time called them the Four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lingyun had returned east, he joined his clansman Huilian, He Changyu of Donghai, Xun Yong of Yingchuan, and Yang Xuanzhi of Taishan in literary fellowship. Together they wandered mountains and wild country, and men of the time called them the Four Friends.

sentences.zh: 惠連幼有才悟，而輕薄不為父方明所知。

translations.literal: Huilian from childhood had talent and quick understanding, yet because he was frivolous he was not appreciated by his father Fangming.
translations.idiomatic: Huilian showed talent and quick understanding even as a boy, yet his frivolous ways kept his father Fangming from recognizing his gifts.

sentences.zh: 靈運去永嘉還始寧，時方明為會稽郡。

translations.literal: Lingyun went from Yongjia back to Shining, when Fangming was administering Kuaiji commandery.
