translations.idiomatic: Lingyun traveled from Yongjia back to Shining while Fangming was serving as administrator of Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 靈運嘗自始寧至會稽造方明，過視惠連，大相知賞。

translations.literal: Lingyun once went from Shining to Kuaiji to visit Fangming, and passing by saw Huilian; they greatly recognized and appreciated each other.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun once traveled from Shining to Kuaiji to visit Fangming, and on the way stopped to see Huilian. The two took an immediate and deep liking to each other.

sentences.zh: 時長瑜教惠連讀書，亦在郡內，靈運又以為絕倫，謂方明曰：「阿連才悟如此，而尊作常兒遇之。

translations.literal: At that time Changyu was teaching Huilian to read, also within the commandery; Lingyun again considered him unmatched and said to Fangming, "Ah-Lian's talent and understanding are like this, yet you, sir, treat him like an ordinary boy.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu was then teaching Huilian to read, also within the commandery, and Lingyun likewise judged him unmatched in talent. He said to Fangming, "Ah-Lian's gifts are as remarkable as this, yet you treat him like an ordinary child.

sentences.zh: 何長瑜當今仲宣，而飴以下客之食。

translations.literal: He Changyu is today's Zhongxuan, yet you feed him with a low guest's fare.
translations.idiomatic: He Changyu is a Wang Can for our age, yet you feed him as though he were some minor guest.

sentences.zh: 尊既不能禮賢，宜以長瑜還靈運。」

translations.literal: Since you, sir, cannot treat the worthy with courtesy, you ought to return Changyu to Lingyun."
translations.idiomatic: Since you cannot honor men of talent, you ought to give Changyu back to me."

sentences.zh: 靈運載之而去。

translations.literal: Lingyun took him away in his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun then took Changyu away with him.

sentences.zh: 荀雍，字道雍，官至員外散騎郎。

translations.literal: Xun Yong, styled Daoyong, reached the office of Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yong, styled Daoyong, rose to the post of Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 璿之，字曜璠，臨川內史，為司空竟陵王誕所遇，誕敗坐誅。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi, styled Yaofan, was Interior Administrator of Linchuan, favored by the Minister of Works and Prince of Jingling, Dan; when Dan was defeated he was executed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhi, styled Yaofan, served as Interior Administrator of Linchuan and won the favor of the Minister of Works and Prince of Jingling, Dan. When Dan was defeated, Xuanzhi was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 長瑜文才之美，亞於惠連，雍、璿之不及也。

translations.literal: Changyu's literary talent was second only to Huilian's; Yong and Xuanzhi did not match him.
translations.idiomatic: In literary talent Changyu ranked only below Huilian; neither Yong nor Xuanzhi could equal him.

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶招集文士，長瑜自國侍郎至平西記室參軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Linchuan, Yiqing, gathered literary men; Changyu rose from Gentleman of the Principality to Recorder on the staff of the Pacifier of the West.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yiqing of Linchuan gathered literary men about him, Changyu served in his household, rising from Gentleman of the Principality to Recorder on the staff of the Pacifier of the West.

sentences.zh: 嘗於江陵寄書與宗人何勗，以韻語序義慶州府僚佐云：「陸展染鬢髮，欲以媚側室。

translations.literal: Once at Jiangling he sent a letter to his clansman He Xu, using rhymed lines to describe Yiqing's commandery and prefectural staff, saying, "Lu Zhan dyes his temple hair, wishing to please a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Jiangling he wrote to his clansman He Xu, using rhymed verse to describe Yiqing's staff. It began, "Lu Zhan dyes his temples, hoping to please a concubine.

sentences.zh: 青青不解久，星星行復出。」

translations.literal: Dark green cannot last long; star by star it will soon appear again."
translations.idiomatic: Black hair cannot long endure; gray strands will soon appear again."

sentences.zh: 如此者五六句，而輕薄少年遂演而廣之，凡厥人士，竝為題目，皆加劇言苦句，其文流行。

translations.literal: There were five or six lines like this, and frivolous young men then expanded and spread them; all the men involved were made subjects, and bitter, harsh lines were added to each. The text circulated widely.
translations.idiomatic: There were five or six lines like this, and frivolous young men expanded and spread them. Every man mentioned was turned into a subject, and each entry was given sharper and crueler lines. The piece soon circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 義慶大怒，白太祖除為廣州所統曾城令。

translations.literal: Yiqing was greatly enraged and reported to the Founder that he be removed and made Magistrate of Zengcheng, under Guangzhou's jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing was furious and reported the matter to the Founder, who had Changyu demoted to Magistrate of Zengcheng under Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及義慶薨，朝士詣第敘哀，何勗謂袁淑曰：「長瑜便可還也。」

translations.literal: When Yiqing died, court officials went to his residence to express mourning. He Xu said to Yuan Shu, "Changyu can now be brought back."
translations.idiomatic: When Yiqing died, court officials went to his residence to mourn. He Xu said to Yuan Shu, "Changyu can now be recalled."

sentences.zh: 淑曰：「國新喪宗英，未宜便以流人為念。」

translations.literal: Shu said, "The state has just lost a pillar of its house; it is not yet fitting to turn one's thoughts so soon to an exiled man."
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied, "The state has just lost a pillar of the realm. It is hardly fitting to turn one's thoughts so soon to a banished man."

sentences.zh: 廬陵王紹鎮尋陽，以長瑜為南中郎行參軍，掌書記之任。

translations.literal: Prince Shao of Luling was stationed at Xunyang and appointed Changyu Acting Staff Officer of the Southern Gentlemen, charged with secretarial duties.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao of Luling was then stationed at Xunyang and appointed Changyu Acting Staff Officer of the Southern Gentlemen, with charge of secretarial duties.

sentences.zh: 行至板橋，遇暴風溺死。

translations.literal: When he reached Banqiao, he met a violent storm and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Banqiao, he was caught in a violent storm and drowned.

sentences.zh: 靈運因父祖之資，生業甚厚。

translations.literal: Lingyun, relying on the resources of his father and grandfather, had a livelihood very substantial.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on the wealth of his father and grandfather, Lingyun possessed a very substantial estate.

sentences.zh: 奴僮既眾，義故門生數百，鑿山浚湖，功役無已。

translations.literal: His slaves and servants were numerous, and his clients and household retainers numbered in the hundreds; he cut into mountains and dredged lakes, and labor never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a large household of slaves and servants, with hundreds of clients and retainers, and never ceased cutting into mountains, dredging lakes, and pressing men into labor.

sentences.zh: 尋山陟嶺，必造幽峻，巖嶂千重，莫不備盡。

translations.literal: When he sought mountains and climbed ridges, he always reached secluded and steep places; among a thousand layers of cliffs and peaks, none went unexplored.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he explored mountains and climbed ridges, he pushed into the most secluded and precipitous places, leaving none of a thousandfold maze of cliffs and peaks unvisited.

sentences.zh: 登躡常著木履，上山則去前齒，下山去其後齒。

translations.literal: When climbing he usually wore wooden clogs; going up a mountain he removed the front teeth, going down he removed the rear teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When climbing he usually wore wooden clogs with removable teeth—going uphill he took off the front teeth, going downhill the rear ones.

sentences.zh: 嘗自始寧南山伐木開逕，直至臨海，從者數百人。

translations.literal: Once from the southern mountains of Shining he felled trees and opened a path all the way to Linhai, with several hundred followers.
translations.idiomatic: Once he cut timber and opened a path from the southern mountains of Shining all the way to Linhai, with several hundred followers in his train.

sentences.zh: 臨海太守王琇驚駭，謂為山賊，徐知是靈運乃安。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Linhai, Wang Xiu, was alarmed and thought them mountain bandits; only gradually learning it was Lingyun did he settle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu, Administrator of Linhai, was alarmed and took them for mountain bandits. Only when he learned it was Lingyun did he relax.

sentences.zh: 又要琇更進，琇不肯，靈運贈琇詩曰：「邦君難地險，旅客易山行。」

translations.literal: He again asked Xiu to go farther, but Xiu refused. Lingyun presented Xiu with a poem saying, "A lord of the state finds the terrain hard to leave; a traveler finds mountain travel easy."
translations.idiomatic: He asked Xiu to go farther still, but Xiu refused. Lingyun sent him a poem: "For a lord of the land the terrain is hard to leave; for a traveler, mountain paths come easily."

sentences.zh: 在會稽亦多徒眾，驚動縣邑。

translations.literal: In Kuaiji as well he had many followers, disturbing counties and districts.
translations.idiomatic: In Kuaiji too he traveled with a large retinue, alarming the counties and districts.

sentences.zh: 太守孟顗事佛精懇，而為靈運所輕，嘗謂顗曰：「得道應須慧業，丈人生天當在靈運前，成佛必在靈運後。」

translations.literal: The Administrator Meng Yi served the Buddha with earnest devotion, yet was looked down on by Lingyun. Lingyun once said to Yi, "Attaining the Way requires karma of wisdom. Your birth into heaven will come before Lingyun's, but Buddhahood must come after Lingyun's."
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator Meng Yi was a devout Buddhist, yet Lingyun looked down on him. Lingyun once told him, "Attaining the Way requires the karma of wisdom. You, sir, will be born into heaven before I will, but you will become a Buddha only after I do."

sentences.zh: 顗深恨此言。

translations.literal: Yi deeply resented these words.
translations.idiomatic: Yi deeply resented the remark.

sentences.zh: 會稽東郭有回踵湖，靈運求決以為田，太祖令州郡履行。

translations.literal: East of the outer wall of Kuaiji was Huizhong Lake. Lingyun requested that it be drained for fields, and the Founder ordered the province and commandery to investigate on site.
translations.idiomatic: East of Kuaiji's outer wall lay Huizhong Lake. Lingyun petitioned to drain it for farmland, and the Founder ordered the provincial and commandery authorities to inspect the site.

sentences.zh: 此湖去郭近，水物所出，百姓惜之，顗堅執不與。

translations.literal: This lake was close to the outer wall and produced aquatic goods; the common people cherished it, and Yi firmly refused to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The lake lay close to the city wall and supplied aquatic produce on which the people depended. Yi firmly refused to allow the project.

sentences.zh: 靈運既不得回踵，又求始寧岯崲湖為田，顗又固執。

translations.literal: Lingyun, having failed to obtain Huizhong, again requested the Bipi Lake of Shining for fields, and Yi again stood firm.
translations.idiomatic: Denied Huizhong Lake, Lingyun next petitioned to drain Bipi Lake at Shining for farmland, and Yi again refused.

sentences.zh: 靈運謂顗非存利民，正慮決湖多害生命，言論毀傷之，與顗遂構仇隙。

translations.literal: Lingyun said that Yi was not acting to benefit the people, but truly feared that draining the lake would harm many lives; he slandered and wounded him in speech, and with Yi he thus formed a bitter enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun claimed Yi was not acting for the people's good but feared that draining the lakes would destroy many living things. He attacked Yi in public and thus drew his lasting hatred.

sentences.zh: 因靈運橫恣，百姓驚擾，乃表其異志，發兵自防，露板上言。

translations.literal: Because Lingyun was overbearing and willful and the common people were alarmed and disturbed, Yi memorialized that Lingyun harbored rebellious intent, raised troops to defend himself, and posted the memorial on a public board.
translations.idiomatic: As Lingyun grew overbearing and the people grew alarmed, Yi memorialized the throne that Lingyun harbored rebellious intent, raised troops in self-defense, and posted the memorial on a public notice board.

sentences.zh: 靈運馳出京都，詣闕上表曰：「臣自抱疾歸山，於今三載，居非郊郭，事乖人間，幽棲窮巖，外緣兩絕，守分養命，庶畢餘年。

translations.literal: Lingyun galloped out of the capital and presented a memorial at the palace gate, saying, "Your subject, having taken illness and returned to the mountains, has now been three years. My dwelling is not in suburbs or market towns; my affairs are at odds with human society. I dwell in seclusion in remote cliffs; outward ties on both sides are cut off. Keeping to my place, I nourish life, hoping to finish my remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun galloped from the capital and submitted a memorial at the palace gate: "Your subject, having retired to the mountains on grounds of illness, has now been three years. I live far from town and market, apart from the affairs of the world, dwelling in seclusion among remote cliffs with all outward ties severed. Keeping to my station, I seek only to preserve my life and finish out my remaining years.

sentences.zh: 忽以去月二十八日得會稽太守臣顗二十七日疏云：『比日異論噂嚃，此雖相了，百姓不許寂默，今微為其防。』

translations.literal: Suddenly on the twenty-eighth of last month I received a memorial from the Administrator of Kuaiji, your subject Yi, dated the twenty-seventh, saying, 'Recently strange talk has been whispered abroad. Though this matter may be understood between us, the common people will not permit silence. I now make slight preparations for defense.'
translations.idiomatic: Then suddenly, on the twenty-eighth of last month, I received a memorial from Yi, Administrator of Kuaiji, dated the twenty-seventh, which read: 'Of late strange rumors have been whispered abroad. Though this may be understood between us, the people will not keep silent. I have therefore made modest defensive preparations.'

sentences.zh: 披疏駭惋，不解所由，便星言奔馳，歸骨陛下。

translations.literal: Reading the memorial, I was alarmed and grieved, not understanding the cause. I therefore set out at once and raced here to lay my bones before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Reading this memorial, I was shocked and grieved, unable to understand its cause. I set out at once and raced here to lay my fate before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 及經山陰，防衛彰赫，彭排馬槍，斷截衢巷，偵邏縱橫，戈甲竟道。

translations.literal: When I passed through Shanyin, the defenses were conspicuous and imposing: ramparts, horse-spears, and crossbeams blocking the thoroughfares and lanes; scouts and patrols crisscrossed everywhere, and spears and armor filled the road.
translations.idiomatic: When I passed through Shanyin, the defenses were imposing: barricades, horse-spears, and crossbeams blocked the streets and lanes; scouts and patrols crisscrossed the city, and arms and armor filled every road.

sentences.zh: 不知微臣罪為何事。

translations.literal: I do not know for what offense this lowly subject stands accused.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know of what crime I am accused.

sentences.zh: 及見顗，雖曰見亮，而裝防如此，唯有罔懼。

translations.literal: When I met Yi, though he said I was understood and cleared, yet such defensive preparations were in place that I could only feel groundless dread.
translations.idiomatic: When I met Yi, though he claimed my innocence was understood, the defenses remained as they were — I could only feel blind terror.

sentences.zh: 臣昔忝近侍，豫蒙天恩，若其罪跡炳明，文字有證，非但顯戮司敗，以正國典，普天之下，自無容身之地。

translations.literal: Your subject was once honored among close attendants and received Heaven's grace in advance. If the traces of guilt were clearly manifest and documents offered proof, I would not only accept public execution by the punishing office to uphold the law of the realm — under all Heaven there would naturally be no place where I could hide.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject was once privileged to serve in close attendance and received the Emperor's grace. Had my guilt been clearly established and borne out by documentary proof, I would not only accept public execution in accordance with the law of the realm — I would have nowhere under Heaven to hide.

sentences.zh: 今虛聲為罪，何酷如之。

translations.literal: Now hollow talk stands as guilt — what cruelty could equal this?
translations.idiomatic: Now I am condemned on empty rumor — what cruelty could equal this?

sentences.zh: 夫自古讒謗，聖賢不免，然致謗之來，要有由趣。

translations.literal: From antiquity, slander has afflicted even sages and worthies, yet when slander comes, there is always some cause and direction to it.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity even sages and worthies have not escaped slander, yet slander always arises from some discernible cause.

sentences.zh: 或輕死重氣，結黨聚群，或勇冠鄉邦，劍客馳逐。

translations.literal: Some hold death lightly and honor spirit highly, forming factions and gathering crowds; some outshine their village and district in courage, swordsmen racing in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold death lightly and prize honor above all, forming factions and gathering followers; some are the bravest in their district, swordsmen racing in each other's tracks.

sentences.zh: 未聞俎豆之學，欲為逆節之罪；

translations.literal: One never hears of one trained in ritual vessels and ceremony seeking the crime of treason;
translations.idiomatic: No one who has cultivated ritual and ceremony is ever heard to seek the crime of treason;

sentences.zh: 山棲之士，而構陵上之釁。

translations.literal: nor of a man dwelling in mountain seclusion fabricating the offense of encroaching upon his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: nor does a man dwelling in mountain seclusion fabricate the offense of lese-majeste.

sentences.zh: 今影跡無端，假謗空設，終古之酷，未之或有。

translations.literal: Now traces appear without cause, false slander is set up in the void — such cruelty from earliest times to the present has never been seen.
translations.idiomatic: Now evidence appears without cause and false slander is invented from nothing — such cruelty has no precedent in all antiquity.

sentences.zh: 匪吝其生，實悲其痛。

translations.literal: It is not that I begrudge my life; I truly grieve the pain of it.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I begrudge my life — I truly mourn the agony of this injustice.

sentences.zh: 誠復內省不疚，而抱理莫申。

translations.literal: Truly, though I examine myself inwardly and find no fault, yet embracing right principle I cannot make it heard.
translations.idiomatic: Though inwardly I find no fault upon reflection, I cannot make my case heard.

sentences.zh: 是以牽曳疾病，束骸歸款。

translations.literal: Therefore, dragging my illness along, I bound my body and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, dragging my sick body along, I came to lay myself before the throne and surrender.

sentences.zh: 仰憑陛下天鑒曲臨，則死之日，猶生之年也。

translations.literal: Looking up and relying on Your Majesty's Heavenly discernment bending down upon me, then the day of my death would be like a day of life.
translations.idiomatic: If I may rely on Your Majesty's discerning grace, then the day of my death would be as a day of life.

sentences.zh: 臣憂怖彌日，羸疾發動，尸存恍惚，不知所陳。」

translations.literal: Your subject has been anxious and terrified day after day; my wasting illness flares up, my body wanders in a daze, and I know not what I say."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has lived in fear and dread day after day; my wasting illness has flared up, my body is half-delirious, and I scarcely know what I have said."

sentences.zh: 太祖知其見誣，不罪也。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew he had been slandered and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew he had been falsely accused and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 不欲使東歸，以為臨川內史，賜秩中二千石。

translations.literal: Not wishing him to return east, he appointed him Administrator of Linchuan and granted him rank at mid-tier two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to let him return east, the Emperor appointed him Administrator of Linchuan and granted him mid-tier two-thousand-bushel rank.

sentences.zh: 在郡遊放，不異永嘉，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: In the commandery he roamed unrestrained, no different from the Yongjia era, and was reported by the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he roamed at will, no different from the Yongjia period, and was reported by the proper authorities.

sentences.zh: 司徒遣使隨州從事鄭望生收靈運，靈運執錄望生，興兵叛逸，遂有逆志。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works sent an envoy; Provincial Attendant Zheng Wangsheng was sent to seize Lingyun. Lingyun seized Wangsheng and bound him, raised troops and fled in rebellion, and thus formed seditious intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works dispatched an envoy, and Provincial Attendant Zheng Wangsheng was sent to arrest Lingyun. Lingyun seized Wangsheng and bound him, raised troops and fled in rebellion, and thus conceived seditious intent.

sentences.zh: 為詩曰：「韓亡子房奮，秦帝魯連恥。

translations.literal: He composed a poem, saying, "When Han was perishing Zhang Liang rose up; before the Qin emperor Lu Zhilian felt shame.
translations.idiomatic: He composed a poem, saying, "When Han was collapsing Zhang Liang roused himself; before the Qin emperor Lu Zhilian felt shame.

sentences.zh: 本自江海人，忠義感君子。」

translations.literal: Born originally a man of rivers and seas — loyalty and righteousness moved the gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Born a man of river and sea — his loyalty and righteousness stirred a noble heart."

sentences.zh: 追討禽之，送廷尉治罪。

translations.literal: They pursued and captured him and sent him to the Court for Judgment for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued him, captured him, and sent him to the Court for Judgment for sentencing.

sentences.zh: 廷尉奏靈運率部眾反叛，論正斬刑。

translations.literal: The Court for Judgment reported that Lingyun had led his band in rebellion and recommended the statutory penalty of decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: The Court for Judgment reported that Lingyun had led his followers in rebellion and recommended execution by decapitation under the law.

sentences.zh: 上愛其才，欲免官而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor cherished his talent and wished merely to dismiss him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor valued his talent and wished only to dismiss him from office.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康堅執謂不宜恕，乃詔曰：「靈運罪釁累仍，誠合盡法。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang insisted he should not be pardoned, whereupon an edict said, "Lingyun's offenses and guilt accumulate repeatedly; he truly deserves the full penalty of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang insisted that he should not be pardoned, whereupon an edict said, "Lingyun's offenses have piled up one upon another; he truly deserves the full weight of the law.

sentences.zh: 但謝玄勳參微管，宜宥及後嗣，可降死一等，徙付廣州。」

translations.literal: But Xie Xuan's merit was like that of Guan Zhong; the pardon should extend to his descendants. His sentence may be reduced one degree from death; he is to be exiled to Guangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: But Xie Xuan's merit was like that of Guan Zhong; mercy should extend to his descendants. Reduce his sentence one degree from death and send him into exile at Guangzhou."

sentences.zh: 其後，秦郡府將宗齊受至塗口，行達桃墟村，見有七人下路亂語，疑非常人，還告郡縣，遣兵隨齊受掩討，遂共格戰，悉禽付獄。

translations.literal: Thereafter, Zong Qishou, a commandery office captain of Qin, reached Tukou. Proceeding to Taoxu Village, he saw seven men dismount from the road speaking confusedly, suspected they were not ordinary people, returned to report to the commandery and county, and troops were sent to follow Qishou in a surprise attack. They fought at close quarters, captured them all, and delivered them to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Zong Qishou, a commandery guard captain of Qin, reached Tukou. On reaching Taoxu Village he saw seven men get off the road and speak confusedly together; suspecting they were not ordinary men, he returned to report to the commandery and county. Troops were sent to follow Qishou in a surprise strike. They fought hand to hand, captured them all, and delivered them to prison.

sentences.zh: 其一人姓趙名欽，山陽縣人，云：「同村薛道雙先與謝康樂共事，以去九月初，道雙因同村成國報欽云：『先作臨川郡、犯事徙送廣州謝，給錢令買弓箭刀楯等物，使道雙要合鄉里健兒，於三江口篡取謝。

translations.literal: One of them, surnamed Zhao and named Qin, a man of Shanyang County, said, "My fellow villager Xue Daoshuang had previously worked together with Xie Kangle. Early in the ninth month of last year, Daoshuang, through our fellow villager Chengguo, told Qin, 'The former Administrator of Linchuan who was convicted and exiled to Guangzhou — Xie — gave money to buy bows, arrows, swords, shields, and the like, and had Daoshuang gather stout fellows from the village to seize Xie at Sanjiangkou.
translations.idiomatic: One of them, Zhao Qin of Shanyang County, said, "My fellow villager Xue Daoshuang had previously worked with Xie Kangle. In early ninth month of last year, Daoshuang, through our fellow villager Chengguo, told me, 'The former Linchuan Administrator who was convicted and exiled to Guangzhou — Xie — gave money to buy bows, arrows, swords, shields, and the like, and told Daoshuang to gather stout fellows from the village to seize Xie at Sanjiangkou.

sentences.zh: 若得志，如意之後，功勞是同。』

translations.literal: If the plan succeeds, after all goes as desired, the credit shall be shared equally.'
translations.idiomatic: If the plan succeeds and all goes as wished, the credit will be shared alike.'

sentences.zh: 遂合部黨要謝，不及。

translations.literal: They gathered their band to waylay Xie but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered their band to waylay Xie but did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 既還饑饉，緣路為劫盜。」

translations.literal: On returning, famine set in, and along the road they turned to banditry."
translations.idiomatic: On the way back famine struck, and along the road they turned to robbery."

sentences.zh: 有司又奏依法收治，太祖詔於廣州行棄市刑。

translations.literal: The responsible officials again reported that he should be taken into custody according to law. The Emperor ordered that he be executed by public market display in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The proper authorities again reported that he should be arrested and tried according to law. The Emperor ordered that the sentence of public execution be carried out in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 臨死作詩曰：「龔勝無餘生，李業有終盡。

translations.literal: On the eve of death he composed a poem, saying, "Gong Sheng left no further days to live; Li Ye too had his end.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he composed a poem, saying, "Gong Sheng had no life remaining; Li Ye too reached his end.

sentences.zh: 嵇公理既迫，霍生命亦殞。

translations.literal: Ji Kang's principle was already pressed; Huo's life also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang's principle was already besieged; Huo's life also ended.

sentences.zh: 淒淒凌霜葉，網網沖風菌。

translations.literal: Frigid frost-bitten leaves mourn; wind-beaten mushrooms hang in nets.
translations.idiomatic: Frost-stricken leaves shiver; wind-torn mushrooms hang in tatters.

sentences.zh: 邂逅竟幾何，脩短非所愍。

translations.literal: A chance meeting — how long did it last? Length of life is not what I lament.
translations.idiomatic: A chance encounter — how long can it last? The span of life is not what I mourn.

sentences.zh: 送心自覺前，斯痛久已忍。

translations.literal: Sending my heart ahead, I know it of myself; this pain I have long endured.
translations.idiomatic: My heart has gone on ahead — I know it myself; this pain I have borne long already.

sentences.zh: 恨我君子志，不獲巖上泯。」

translations.literal: I regret that my gentleman's resolve was not granted to fade away upon the cliffs."
translations.idiomatic: I regret that my noble resolve was not granted to perish upon the mountain cliffs."

sentences.zh: 詩所稱龔勝、李業，猶前詩子房、魯連之意也。

translations.literal: The Gong Sheng and Li Ye named in the poem carry the same intent as Zhang Liang and Lu Zhilian in the earlier poem.
translations.idiomatic: The Gong Sheng and Li Ye named in the poem convey the same intent as Zhang Liang and Lu Zhilian in the earlier poem.

sentences.zh: 時元嘉十年，年四十九。

translations.literal: It was the tenth year of Yuanjia; he was forty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: It was the tenth year of Yuanjia; he was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 所著文章傳於世。

translations.literal: The writings he authored were transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The writings he left were handed down in the world.

sentences.zh: 子鳳，蚤卒。

translations.literal: His son Feng died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng died young.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：民稟天地之靈，含五常之德，剛柔迭用，喜慍分情。

translations.literal: The historiographer writes: The people receive the spirit of heaven and earth and contain the virtues of the five constants; hardness and softness alternate in use, and joy and anger divide the feelings.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Human beings are endowed with the spirit of heaven and earth and embody the five constant virtues; hardness and softness take turns, and joy and anger divide the heart.

sentences.zh: 夫志動於中，則歌詠外發。

translations.literal: When will stirs within, then songs and poems flow outward.
translations.idiomatic: When the heart moves within, song and poetry burst forth without.

sentences.zh: 六義所因，四始攸繫，升降謳謠，紛披風什。

translations.literal: The six categories provide their ground; the four beginnings bind them together; ascending and descending ballads and songs scatter through the Airs.
translations.idiomatic: The six categories of meaning supply their foundation, the four inaugural poems hold them fast, and rising and falling songs and ballads spread in profusion through the Airs.

sentences.zh: 雖虞夏以前，遺文不睹，稟氣懷靈，理無或異。

translations.literal: Though before the eras of Yu and Xia no surviving texts can be seen, in receiving vital breath and harboring spirit the principle surely does not differ.
translations.idiomatic: Though no written traces survive from before the eras of Yu and Xia, in receiving breath and harboring spirit the principle cannot have been any different.

sentences.zh: 然則歌詠所興，宜自生民始也。

translations.literal: Therefore the rise of song and poetry should properly date from the beginning of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Song and poetry, then, must have arisen with humanity itself.

sentences.zh: 周室既衰，風流彌著，屈平、宋玉，導清源於前，賈誼、相如，振芳塵於後，英辭潤金石，高義薄雲天。

translations.literal: Once the Zhou house had declined, the literary current grew ever more prominent. Qu Ping and Song Yu opened clear springs at the fore; Jia Yi and Xiangru raised fragrant traces behind them. Splendid words polish metal and stone; lofty righteousness thins to touch heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou house had already declined, the literary current grew ever more visible. Qu Ping and Song Yu opened clear springs ahead; Jia Yi and Xiangru raised fragrant dust behind them. Their splendid words enriched metal and stone; their lofty righteousness reached to the clouds and sky.

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，情志愈廣。

translations.literal: From this time onward, feeling and intent grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: From that time forward, the range of feeling and intent grew ever wider.

sentences.zh: 王褒、劉向、揚、班、崔、蔡之徒，異軌同奔，遞相師祖。

translations.literal: Wang Bao, Liu Xiang, Yang, Ban, Cui, Cai, and men of their kind — though on different tracks, they ran toward the same goal, each in turn taking another as master and model.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao, Liu Xiang, Yang, Ban, Cui, Cai, and others like them followed different paths yet raced toward the same end, each generation in turn taking the last as teacher and model.

sentences.zh: 雖清辭麗曲，時發乎篇，而蕪音累氣，固亦多矣。

translations.literal: Though clear words and lovely turns sometimes burst forth in their pages, weedy sounds that weigh down the vital breath were also indeed numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Though clear diction and lovely turns sometimes flashed forth in their pages, coarse sounds that burdened the breath were also plentiful.

sentences.zh: 若夫平子豔發，文以情變，絕唱高蹤，久無嗣響。

translations.literal: As for Pingzi's brilliant blossoming — writing changed with feeling; unsurpassed songs and lofty traces went long without echoing successors.
translations.idiomatic: As for Pingzi's brilliant flowering, in whom writing changed with feeling — his unsurpassed songs and lofty traces went long without a successor.

sentences.zh: 至於建安，曹氏基命，二祖、陳王，咸蓄盛藻，甫乃以情緯文，以文被質。

translations.literal: By the Jian'an era the Cao house had founded their mandate; the two founders and Prince Chen all stored up abundant ornament, and only then wove feeling through words and clothed substance with literary form.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jian'an era the House of Cao had founded its mandate; the two founders and Prince Chen all amassed rich ornament, and only then did they weave feeling through words and clothe substance in literary form.

sentences.zh: 自漢至魏，四百餘年，辭人才子，文體三變。

translations.literal: From Han to Wei, over four hundred years, literary men and talented youths — the literary style changed three times.
translations.idiomatic: From Han to Wei, across more than four hundred years, men of letters and literary talent saw the style of writing change three times.

sentences.zh: 相如巧為形似之言，班固長於情理之說，子建、仲宣以氣質為體，竝摽能擅美，獨映當時。

translations.literal: Xiangru was skillful at words of vivid likeness; Ban Gu excelled at discourse on reason and feeling; Zi Jian and Zhong Xuan took temperament and native quality as their substance — all alike displayed their gifts and monopolized beauty, shining alone in their age.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangru was skillful at words of vivid likeness; Ban Gu excelled at discourse on reason and feeling; Zi Jian and Zhong Xuan took temperament and native quality as their substance. All alike displayed their gifts and claimed beauty for themselves, shining alone in their own age.

sentences.zh: 是以一世之士，各相慕習，原其飆流所始，莫不同祖《風》、《騷》。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentlemen of that age each admired and emulated one another; tracing where the rushing current began, none failed to share the same ancestry in the Airs and the Sao.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the men of that age each admired and emulated one another, and tracing the source of the rushing current, all alike looked back to the Airs and the Sao.

sentences.zh: 徒以賞好異情，故意制相詭。

translations.literal: Only because tastes differed in feeling did they deliberately make their forms diverge.
translations.idiomatic: Only because tastes differed in feeling did they deliberately make their forms diverge from one another.

sentences.zh: 降及元康，潘、陸特秀，律異班、賈，體變曹、王，縟旨星稠，繁文綺合。

translations.literal: Descending to the Yuankang era, Pan and Lu stood out above the rest; their metrical rules differed from Ban and Jia, their form changed from Cao and Wang; intricate meanings clustered thick as stars, elaborate words woven like brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Descending to the Yuankang era, Pan and Lu stood out above the rest. Their metrical rules differed from Ban and Jia, their form changed from Cao and Wang; meanings clustered thick as stars, and elaborate words were woven together like brocade.

sentences.zh: 綴平臺之逸響，采南皮之高韻，遺風餘烈，事極江右。

translations.literal: Linking the refined echoes of the Pingtai gatherings, gathering the lofty tones of Nanpi — the lingering wind and surviving brilliance reached their peak in the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Linking the refined echoes of the Pingtai gatherings and gathering the lofty tones of Nanpi, the lingering wind and surviving brilliance reached their peak in the lands south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 有晉中興，玄風獨振，為學窮於柱下，博物止乎七篇，馳騁文辭，義單乎此。

translations.literal: When Jin was restored, the dark-learning current alone flourished; study exhausted itself at the Keeper under the Pillar, encyclopedic breadth stopped at seven chapters; they galloped through literary language, but meaning was confined to this alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was restored, the Neo-Daoist current alone flourished. Learning exhausted itself in the Keeper under the Pillar, encyclopedic breadth stopped at seven chapters, and though men galloped through literary language, their meaning was confined to this alone.

sentences.zh: 自建武暨乎義熙，歷載將百，雖綴響聯辭，波屬雲委，莫不寄言上德，託意玄珠，遒麗之辭，無聞焉爾。

translations.literal: From Jianwu down to Yixi, spanning nearly a hundred years — though echo followed echo and words linked together like waves massed and clouds piled, all alike lodged their words in supreme virtue and entrusted their intent to the dark pearl; forceful and beautiful language was nowhere to be heard.
translations.idiomatic: From Jianwu down to Yixi, spanning nearly a hundred years, though echo followed echo and words linked together like waves massed and clouds piled, all alike lodged their words in supreme virtue and entrusted their intent to the dark pearl. Forceful and beautiful language was nowhere to be heard.

sentences.zh: 仲文始革孫、許之風，叔源大變太元之氣。

translations.literal: Zhongwen first reformed the style of Sun and Xu; Shuyuan greatly transformed the temper of the Taixuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen first reformed the style of Sun and Xu, and Shuyuan greatly transformed the literary temper of the Taixuan era.

sentences.zh: 爰逮宋氏，顏、謝騰聲。

translations.literal: Reaching the Song house, Yan and Xie soared in fame.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the Song dynasty, Yan and Xie had risen to fame.

sentences.zh: 靈運之興會摽舉，延年之體裁明密，並方軌前秀，垂範後昆。

translations.literal: Lingyun's inspired encounters rise loftily; Yannian's craft is clear and meticulous — both matched the measure of earlier masters and bequeathed models to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun's inspired encounters rise loftily, and Yannian's craft is clear and meticulous. Both matched the measure of earlier masters and bequeathed models to later generations.

sentences.zh: 若夫敷衽論心，商榷前藻，工拙之數，如有可言。

translations.literal: As for spreading one's robe and discussing the heart, weighing earlier literary blossoms — the reckoning of skill and clumsiness, it seems, may yet be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: If one spreads one's robe and discusses the heart of the matter, weighing earlier literary blossoms, the reckoning of skill and clumsiness may yet be spoken of.

sentences.zh: 夫五色相宣，八音協暢，由乎玄黃律呂，各適物宜。

translations.literal: The five colors mutually enhance one another; the eight tones harmoniously flow — through dark and yellow, pitch pipes and pitch standards, each suited to what things require.
translations.idiomatic: The five colors enhance one another, and the eight tones harmonize and flow freely, through dark and yellow, pitch pipes and pitch standards, each suited to what things require.

sentences.zh: 欲使宮羽相變，低昂互節，若前有浮聲，則後須切響。

translations.literal: One wishes to make Gong and Yu tones alternate, low and high mutually regulating each other — if the preceding sound is a level tone, then what follows must be a sharp tone.
translations.idiomatic: One seeks to make Gong and Yu tones alternate and low and high mutually regulate each other: if the preceding sound is level, what follows must be sharp.

sentences.zh: 一簡之內，音韻盡殊；

translations.literal: Within a single line, every sound and rhyme must differ.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single line, every sound and rhyme must differ.

sentences.zh: 兩句之中，輕重悉異。

translations.literal: Within a pair of lines, every light and heavy must differ.
translations.idiomatic: Within a pair of lines, every light and heavy must differ.

sentences.zh: 妙達此旨，始可言文。

translations.literal: Only when one marvelously grasps this principle may one speak of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Only when one marvelously grasps this principle may one speak of writing at all.

sentences.zh: 至於先士茂制，諷高歷賞，子建函京之作，仲宣霸岸之篇，子荊零雨之章，正長朔風之句，並直舉胸情，非傍詩史，正以音律調韻，取高前式。

translations.literal: As for the abundant works of the ancients, lofty in import and prized through the ages — Zi Jian's piece on the capital enclosure, Zhong Xuan's piece on the Ba embankment, Zi Jing's chapter on drizzling rain, Zhengchang's line on the north wind — all alike expressed feeling straight from the breast, without leaning on the Odes and historical chronicles; it was precisely through tonal pattern and regulated rhyme that they attained the loftiness of earlier models.
translations.idiomatic: As for the abundant works of the ancients, lofty in import and prized through the ages — Zi Jian's piece on the capital enclosure, Zhong Xuan's piece on the Ba embankment, Zi Jing's chapter on drizzling rain, Zhengchang's line on the north wind — all alike expressed feeling straight from the breast, without leaning on the Odes and historical chronicles. It was precisely through tonal pattern and regulated rhyme that they attained the loftiness of earlier models.

sentences.zh: 自《騷》人以來，而此秘未睹。

translations.literal: Since the Sao writers, this secret has remained unseen.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Sao writers, this secret has remained unseen.

sentences.zh: 至於高言妙句，音韻天成，皆闇與理合，匪由思至。

translations.literal: As for lofty words and marvelous lines — tonal pattern born of nature — all tacitly accord with principle, not arrived at through deliberate thought.
translations.idiomatic: As for lofty words and marvelous lines whose tonal pattern is born of nature, all tacitly accord with principle and are not arrived at through deliberate thought.

sentences.zh: 張、蔡、曹、王，曾無先覺，潘、陸、謝、顏，去之彌遠。

translations.literal: Zhang, Cai, Cao, and Wang never had any who first awakened to it; Pan, Lu, Xie, and Yan grew ever farther from it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Cai, Cao, and Wang never had any who first awakened to it, and Pan, Lu, Xie, and Yan grew ever farther from it.

sentences.zh: 世之知音者，有以得之，知此言之非謬。

translations.literal: Those in the world who truly understand music will have grounds to grasp it and will know these words are not mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the world who truly understand music will have grounds to grasp it and will know that these words are not mistaken.

sentences.zh: 如曰不然，請待來哲。

translations.literal: If one says otherwise, one must await the sages yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: If one says otherwise, let us await the sages yet to come.
